For the sacrament of baptism which you are about to receive also expresses the form of this hope [Note: Read: “the hope of this.” — But this is erroneous]. For in it a certain death and a certain resurrection are celebrated. The old person is put off; the new person is taken up. The sinner enters the waters and comes forth justified. The one who dragged him toward death is cast away, and the one who brought him back to life is received. Through his grace you are granted to become children of God, born not by the will of the flesh but generated by the power of the Holy Spirit.

Therefore this exceedingly brief fullness must cling to your hearts in such a way that at all times you may use the protection of this confession. For the power of such weapons, which will be useful for the good warfare of Christ, is always unconquerable against all the enemy’s snares. May the devil, who never ceases to test human beings, always find you armed with this Creed. Thus, when the adversary whom you renounce has been defeated, may you preserve the Lord’s grace pure and undefiled to the end, with him whom you confess protecting you, so that in that same grace in which you receive the remission of sins you may possess the glory of the resurrection.

Therefore, dearest ones, you have now learned the aforesaid Creed of the Catholic faith in its present form. Go now and learn it without altering a single word. For the mercy of God is powerful: may it lead you, who are hastening toward the faith of baptism, to the baptismal font, and may it cause us, who hand on the mysteries to you, to reach the heavenly kingdoms together with you. Through the same Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns forever and ever. Amen.

XXXVI. ALSO, THE PREFACE OF THE LORD’S PRAYER.

[Col. 1091D] And the deacon admonishes them, as above.

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, among his other saving commandments, granted his disciples, when they asked how they ought to pray, the form of prayer which you have also come to know more fully through the present reading. Now let your love hear how he teaches his disciples to pray to God the almighty Father:

“But when you pray, enter your room, and, with the door closed, pray to your Father.”

The “room” he names does not indicate a hidden house, but signifies that the secrets of our heart are open to him alone. And by “with the door closed,” he shows that we ought to adore God—that is, we should close our breast against evil thoughts with a mystical key and, with our lips closed, speak to God with an incorrupt mind. Our God is a hearer of faith, not of the voice. Therefore let our breast be closed with the key of faith against the enemy’s snares and be open to God alone, whose temple it is known to be, so that when he dwells in our hearts, he himself may be our advocate in our prayers.

Therefore the Word of God and Wisdom of God, Christ our Lord, taught us this prayer, so that we should pray in this way.

After this you enter and say:

OUR FATHER, WHO ARE IN HEAVEN.

[Col. 1092B] This is the voice of freedom and of complete confidence. Therefore you must live according to such conduct that you may be able to be both children of God and brothers of Christ. For with what audacity can one presume to call God his Father if he degenerates from God’s will? Therefore, dearest ones, show yourselves worthy of divine adoption, since it is written: “As many as believed in him, he gave them power to become children of God.”

HALLOWED BE YOUR NAME.

That is, not that God—who is always holy—becomes holy through our sanctifications [Note: The Gallican Missal has: “may he be sanctified by prayers, who”], but we ask that his name may be sanctified in us, so that we who are sanctified in his baptism may persevere in what we have begun to be [Note: Read: “in what we begin.”].

[Col. 1092C] YOUR KINGDOM COME.

For when does our God not reign, whose kingdom is immortal? But when we say, “Your kingdom come,” we ask that our kingdom may come to us from God, promised to us and sought through the blood and passion of Christ.

YOUR WILL BE DONE, ON EARTH AS IT IS IN HEAVEN.

That is, may your will be done in this matter: that what you will in heaven, we who are placed on earth may do irreproachably.

GIVE US THIS DAY OUR DAILY BREAD.

Here we must understand spiritual food. For Christ is our bread, who said: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven.” We call it daily because we must always ask to be kept free from sin, so that we may be worthy of heavenly nourishment.

AND FORGIVE US OUR DEBTS, AS WE ALSO FORGIVE OUR DEBTORS.

By this command he signifies that we cannot otherwise deserve forgiveness of sins unless we first forgive those who have sinned against us [Note: Read: “in ourselves.” — But this is erroneous], just as the Lord says in the Gospel: “Unless you forgive people their sins, neither will your Father forgive your sins.”

[Col. 1093A] AND DO NOT LEAD US INTO TEMPTATION.

That is, do not allow us to be led into it by the one who tempts, the author of wickedness. For Scripture says: “God is not a tempter of evils.” The devil, however, is the tempter; and to overcome him the Lord says: “Watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation.”

BUT DELIVER US FROM EVIL.

He says this because the Apostle said: “You do not know what you ought to pray for.” We must pray to the one almighty God in such a way that whatever human frailty is unable to guard against and avoid, he may mercifully grant us the power to withstand. Jesus Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns as God in unity with the Holy Spirit throughout all ages of ages.

Likewise the deacon announces, as above:

[Col. 1093B] Stand with discipline and in silence, listening attentively.

You have heard, dearest ones, the holy mysteries of the Lord’s Prayer. Go now and renew them in your hearts, so that you may be perfect in Christ for asking and receiving the mercy of God. Powerful is the Lord our God: may he lead you who are running toward the faith [Note: The Gallican Missal has: “who are running”] to the washing of the water of regeneration, and may he cause us, who have together handed on to you the mystery of the Catholic faith, to reach the heavenly kingdoms with you. He lives and reigns with God the Father in unity with the Holy Spirit throughout all ages of ages.

XXXVII. SUNDAY OF THE PALMS: ON THE PASSION OF THE LORD.

[Col. 1093C]

O God, who, for the human race to imitate the example of humility, made our Savior both assume flesh and undergo the cross, mercifully grant that we may both possess the lesson of his patience and deserve to share in the fellowship of his resurrection, Christ our Lord. He lives and reigns with you as God in unity with the Holy Spirit. Through.

God, whom to love and cherish is righteousness, multiply within us the gifts of your ineffable grace, so that we who have been made to hope through the death of your Son in what we believe may, when he has risen, reach the goal toward which we strive. Through.

**Secret.**

May this offering, Lord, commend the faithful peoples to your majesty—the offering that reconciled us, though enemies, through your Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. [Col. 1093D. In the exemplar it is incorrectly written: “friend.”] He lives and reigns with you, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, throughout all ages of ages.

**Postcommunion.**

Having been satisfied with the sacred gift, we humbly beseech you, Lord, that we may receive an increase of your salvation through the service of dutiful devotion that we celebrate. Through.

**For the people.**

Purify, we beseech you, Lord, your household, and cleanse it from every contagion of wickedness, so that the unclean spirit may not again infect the vessels redeemed by their Lord’s passion, but everlasting salvation may possess them. Through.

**Monday of the sixth week.**

Remember your mercies, Lord, and sanctify your servants with eternal protection, for whom Christ your Son instituted the paschal mystery through his blood. Through our Lord.

Stir up, Lord, the hearts of your faithful, so that, attentive to sacred teachings, they may understand what they are to follow and, faithfully following it, may lay hold of it. Through.

**Secret.**

Look favorably, Lord, upon the sacred mysteries that we perform, and mercifully grant that we may bring forth eternal life through what you have provided for the removal of our prejudices.  
[Col. 1094D. The exemplar has less correctly: “perjudicia.”]

**Postcommunion.**

May your holy gifts, Lord, we beseech you, both continually renew us by giving us life and give us life by renewing us. Through.

**For the people.**

Turn your people, Lord, we beseech you, with their whole heart, because those whom you defend even when they sin, you also protect with greater compassion when they are devoted with a sincere mind. Through.

**Tuesday of the sixth week.**

Grant, merciful God, that we may faithfully perceive as salutary for us what the world enacted in the passion of your Son. Through.

[Col. 1094C] Grant, almighty God, that we may rejoice that what we recall as having truly happened passes over into our healing. Through.

**Secret.**

Give heed, we beseech you, Lord, to the offerings of your household, and grant that the one whom you make a participant in sacred gifts may reach their fullness. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Filled, Lord, with the grace of the sacred gift, we humbly entreat you that what we have touched with bodily taste and sweet veneration we may perceive as sweeter in our minds.  
[Col. 1094D. Read: “we conceal”—but incorrectly.]

Through.

**For the people.**

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, to your faithful both to receive the paschal Sacraments without ceasing and to await eagerly what is to come, so that, remaining in the mysteries through which they have been reborn, they may be brought by these works to new life. Through.

**Wednesday of the sixth week.**

Almighty and everlasting God, who restore us through the blessed passion of your Christ, preserve in us the works of your mercy, so that in the celebration of this mystery we may live in perpetual devotion. Through.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty and merciful God, that just as, in the condemnation of your Son, the salvation of all came through the impious deed of the treacherous, so also through your mercy this worship may be common to all believers. Through.

**Secret.**

Receive, we beseech you, Lord, the offering presented, and graciously accomplish this: that what we enact in the mystery of the passion, we may attain through devout affections. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Instructed by the blessing of the heavenly gift, we humbly beseech you, Lord, that this same gift may always be for us both the cause of the sacrament and of salvation. Through.

**For the people.**

Assist your people, Lord, so that, advancing in sacred devotion and growth, they may always be governed by your gift and, with you leading them, reach the fellowship of eternal redemption.  
[Col. 1095D. We have corrected it thus, since the exemplar reads: “to teach.”]

**XXXVIII. PRAYER FOR THURSDAY.**

[Col. 1095B]

On that day no psalm is sung, nor is the greeting given—that is, he does not say, “The Lord be with you”—and there is the reconciliation of the penitent.

Almighty and everlasting God, grant, we beseech you, to all your servants more fully and perfectly to enter into all the mysteries of the paschal feast, so that devout hearts may unmistakably recognize how greatly they ought to rejoice in the glorification of those reborn in Christ, which has been confirmed. Through.

Grant to believers, merciful God, a saving remedy from the passion of Christ; and by the aid of eternal compassion may the people be released from the snares of past guilt arising from human frailty.  
[Col. 1095D. Correct from the Ambrosian Breviary: “may he release from the snares of past guilt by the aid of eternal compassion.”]

[Col. 1095C] Almighty and everlasting God, who, while your Son was dying for us, saved the life of the human race, grant, we beseech you, that in this devotion of your people there may come in advance the fruit of joys.  
[Col. 1095D. In the Ambrosian Missal: “may come forth.”]

**ORDER FOR THOSE DOING PUBLIC PENANCE**

The penitent leaves the place where he has performed penance and is presented in the midst of the church, with his whole body prostrate on the ground. The deacon petitions in these words:

Here is, O venerable bishop, the acceptable time, the day of divine mercy and human salvation, when death received its destruction and life received the beginning of eternity, when in the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts the planting of new growth must be carried out in such a way that the old may be cleansed and healed.  
[Col. 1095D. In the Roman Order: “the curse.”]

Although no time is ever lacking from the riches of God’s goodness and compassion, now nevertheless the remission of sins is more generous through pardon, and the reception of those being reborn is more abundant through grace. [Col. 1095D. We emended this from the Roman Order; the exemplar has: “the giver.”] We are increased by those being regenerated; we grow through those who return. The waters wash; the tears wash. From one side comes joy at the reception of those called, from the other, gladness at the absolution of penitents.  
[Col. 1096D. The same source reads: “joy.”]

This is why your suppliant, after falling into various forms of crimes through neglect of the heavenly commandments and transgression of disreputable conduct, now humbled and prostrate, cries out to God in the prophetic words, saying: [Col. 1096D. Thus in the Roman Order; elsewhere: “approved.” Read: “disreputable.”] “I have sinned, I have acted wickedly, I have committed iniquity; have mercy on me, Lord.” Receiving the evangelical saying with an ear that does not receive it in vain: “Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.” He ate, as it is written, the bread of sorrow; he watered his bed with tears; he afflicted his heart with mourning and his body with fasts, so that he might recover the health of his soul, which he had lost.

Thus penance has one means of help, which benefits individuals and comes to the aid of all together. Therefore, while he is stirred to the practice of penitence by such great examples, before the sight of the grieving Church, the venerable bishop protests and says: [Col. 1096D. Read: “stirred.” We have nevertheless emended it from the aforementioned Order.] “I acknowledge my iniquities, and my sin is always before me. Turn your face from my sins, Lord, and blot out all my iniquities. Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me with a princely spirit.”

As he thus makes supplication and asks God’s mercy with an afflicted heart, restore in him, O apostolic bishop, whatever was corrupted when the devil tore it apart; and, with the merits of your prayers assisting him, make the man close to God through the grace of divine reconciliation, so that he who formerly displeased the Lord in his perversities may now rejoice that he pleases the Lord in the land of the living, with the author of his death defeated. Through the Lord.

After this, the bishop or another priest admonishes him not to recall by repeating what he has washed away through penance.

[Col. 1096C] Then the priest says these prayers over him:

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, and mercifully hear me, who also am the first to need your mercy, so that you, who appointed me minister of this work not by a choice based on merit but by the gift of your grace, may grant me confidence to carry out your commission; and may you yourself perform in our ministry what belongs to your compassion. Through.  
[Col. 1096D. Read: “choice.” Since the text was faulty, we have corrected it from the same Order.]

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, to this servant of yours a worthy fruit of penance, so that, having obtained forgiveness for his offenses, he may be restored harmless to your holy Church, from whose integrity he had strayed by sinning. Through the Lord.

God, most benevolent creator and most merciful fashioner of the human race, who redeemed with the blood of your Only-Begotten the human being cast down from eternity through the envy of the devil, give life, therefore, to one whom you by no means desire to die for you; and you who do not abandon the one who has strayed, receive the one who has been corrected.  
[Col. 1096D. We corrected the exemplar, which reads: “the corrupted one.”]

Move your compassion, we beseech you, Lord, by the tearful sighs of this servant of yours. Heal his wounds. Stretch out to the fallen your saving hand, lest your Church be devastated in any portion of its body, lest your flock suffer loss, lest the enemy exult at the harm done to your household, lest a second death possess one reborn through the saving bath. To you, therefore, Lord, we pour out humble prayers; to you we pour out the tears of our heart. Spare the one who confesses, so that, through your mercy, he may not fall under the impending punishments and sentence of the future judgment.  
[Col. 1097D. Thus corrected from the Roman Order; the exemplar reads: “the punishments and sentence that threaten.”]

Let him not experience what terrifies in darkness and what shrieks in the flames; and, having returned from the path of error to the way of righteousness, let him no longer be wounded by new injuries. Rather, may what your grace has bestowed and what your mercy has restored remain whole and perpetual for him. Through.

**Also, for reconciling a penitent.**

Almighty and everlasting God, in your compassion release the sins of this servant of yours who confesses to you, so that the guilt of his conscience may not harm him more toward punishment than the indulgence of your compassion toward forgiveness. Through the Lord.

Almighty and merciful God, who have placed the forgiveness of sins in prompt confession, come to the aid of those who have fallen and have mercy on those who confess, so that your great compassion may release those whom the chain of offenses binds. Through.  
[Col. 1097D. From the Roman Order. The exemplar has less correctly: “in confession.”]

God, who purify the hearts of those who confess to you and absolve those who accuse their consciences from every bond of iniquity, grant pardon to the guilty and give healing to the wounded, so that, having received remission of all sins, they may thereafter remain in sincere devotion and suffer no loss of eternal redemption. Through.  
[Col. 1097D. Read: “having been completed.” From the same Order. The exemplar has it incorrectly as “having received.”]

[Col. 1097C] Holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, look upon this servant of yours, who, overwhelmed by the hostile storm of the world, accuses his transgressions with mournful lamentation, so that you may mercifully receive his weeping and groaning, call him back from darkness to light, and grant healing to the one who confesses, salvation to the penitent, and the aid of health to the wounded. May the enemy no longer have power over his soul; and, gladly accepting his confession, restore him purified to your Church and present him at your altar, so that, admitted to the sacrament of reconciliation, he may deserve to give thanks with us to your holy name. Through.  
[Col. 1097D. Read: “of each one.” But the exemplar is faulty.]

**RECONCILIATION OF PENITENTS AT THE POINT OF DEATH**

[Col. 1097D] Merciful God, gracious God, who according to the multitude of your mercies blot out the sins of penitents and remove the guilt of past crimes through the pardon of forgiveness, look upon this servant of yours and graciously hear him as he begs and asks with a whole-hearted confession for the remission of all his sins. Renew in him, most loving Father, whatever has been corrupted through earthly frailty or violated through diabolical deceit; restore him, through perfect remission, as a member to the unity of the body of your Church. Have mercy, Lord, on his groans; have mercy on his tears; and admit to the sacrament of reconciliation one who has confidence in nothing except your mercy. Through.

We humbly beseech your majesty, Lord, that you may deign to bestow the pardon of your mercy upon this servant of yours, worn down by the long squalor of penance, so that, having received the wedding garment, he may deserve to enter the royal table from which he had been cast out. Through.

We beseech your majesty, holy Father, almighty and everlasting God, who always seek not the death but the life of sinners. Look upon your weeping servant; heed him prostrate; and by your mercy turn his lamentation into joy. Tear apart the sack of his offenses and clothe him in saving gladness, [Col. 1098B] so that, after the long hunger of his pilgrimage, he may be satisfied from your holy altars and, having entered the chamber of the King, may always bless the name of your glory in his court. Through the Lord.

Merciful God, gracious God, who do not confine your indulgence within any law of time, but open the door of your mercy to the one who knocks, and do not abandon penitents even at the very end of this life [Col. 1098D. Thus corrected. Read: “end.”], look favorably upon this servant of yours, who asks for the remission of all his sins with a whole-hearted confession. Renew in him, most loving Father, whatever has been defiled by deed, word, or finally by thought through diabolical deceit, and join him, as a member of your Church’s body, to the unity of your redemption. Have mercy on his groans; have mercy on his tears; and admit to the sacrament of reconciliation one who has confidence in nothing except your mercy, because no soul living in this body has with you a difficult or delayed healing. For you are faithful in your words: you said that a converted sinner was not to be deferred through long periods of time, but that, as soon as he had groaned toward you, he was restored. Through.

[Col. 1098D. Read: “Prayer.”]

**Prayer after reconciliation, or after he has received Communion.**

God, who purify the hearts of those who confess to you and absolve consciences accusing themselves from every bond of iniquity, grant them pardon and give healing to the wounded, so that, having received remission of all sins, they may thereafter remain in sincere devotion in your sacraments and suffer no loss of eternal redemption. Through.  
[Col. 1098D. In the Codex of Toulouse, in Morinus, *Commentary on Penance*, p. 68, it reads: “grant indulgence to the guilty.”]

After this the people offer, and the sacraments are prepared.

**Secret.**

God of the heavenly powers, from whose grace’s dew it comes that we approach your mysteries with purified minds, grant, we beseech you, that in their solemn handing-over, with due honor, we may offer service pleasing to you. Through.  
[Col. 1098D. The same codex, p. 40, reads: “to be honored.”]

[Col. 1099A] **Within the Canon.**

“Communicating, and celebrating the most sacred day on which our Lord Jesus Christ was handed over.” But also the commemoration.

**Also within the Canon.**

“Therefore, Lord, graciously regard this offering of your entire household, which they offer to you for the day of the fast of the Lord’s Supper, on which our Lord Jesus Christ handed over to his disciples the mysteries of his body and blood to be celebrated. Grant, Lord, that through many cycles of years it may deserve to offer its gifts to you, Lord, safe and unharmed, and grant our days in your peace d.”

Also within the Canon, where we say, “Who on the day before he suffered,” on this day we say: “Who on this day, before he was handed over, took bread in his holy hands, having lifted them ...”

**Postcommunion.**

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that we may perceive both in body and in mind the mystery of the new sacrament we have received. Through.

**For the people.**

Look favorably, good Shepherd, upon your flock, and do not allow the sheep whom you redeemed with the precious blood of your Son to be torn apart by the devil’s assault. Through.

**XL. ALSO FOR THURSDAY**

**Chrism Mass.**

Lord God, who use the ministry of priests in regenerating your peoples, grant us persevering service in your will, so that, by the gift of your grace, your people consecrated to you may increase in our days both in merit and in number. Through our Lord.  
[Col. 1099D. Read: “so that.” The exemplar has it incorrectly.]

Grant us, almighty God, to handle the remedies of the human condition with sincere service and to complete them with progress toward salvation. Through.  
[Col. 1099D. The exemplar has it incorrectly: “with the completed.”]

**Secret.**

May the power of this sacrifice, Lord, we beseech you, mercifully wipe away our old condition and increase in us a saving newness. Through.

We humbly implore your clemency: confirm, as a sacrament of perfect salvation and life, the chrism created for those who are to be renewed by the baptism of the spiritual bath. May, when the sanctification of anointing has been poured in and the corruption of the first birth has been swallowed up, the holy temple of each person exude the innocent fragrance of acceptable life.  
[Col. 1099D. Read: “fragrance,” although the exemplar has it incorrectly.]

May those who have been covered with the sacrament of your institution be clothed with the honor of kingship, priesthood, and prophecy, in the garment of incorruptible grace. Through him be your majesty.

**Within the Canon, “Communicating,” as above.**

“Therefore, Lord, graciously receive this offering of your male and female servants, which they offer to you for the day on which our Lord Jesus Christ handed over to his disciples the mysteries of his body and blood to be celebrated. In your goodness grant that, through many cycles of years, they may deserve to offer their gifts to you, Lord, safe and unharmed, and grant our days ...”

**Blessing of the oil. For the people, in these words:**

“This oil is for anointing the sick. When you come to: ‘To us also, your sinful servants’; and the rest through: ‘Through Christ our Lord.’ Then you enter.”

Send forth, we beseech you, Lord, from heaven the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, upon this richness of oil, which you have deigned to produce from green wood for the refreshment of mind and body. May your holy blessing be protection of body, soul, and spirit for everyone who anoints, tastes, or touches it, for removing every pain, every weakness, and every sickness of mind and body. From it you anointed priests, kings, prophets, and martyrs.  
[Col. 1099D. Thus it is read in Pamelius.]

May your perfect chrism, Lord, blessed by you, remain in our innermost parts in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.  
[Col. 1100D. Pamelius reads it thus.]

Through him you always create all these good things, Lord. And the rest.

When the Canon has been completed, he says:

“Let us pray. Instructed by saving commandments.” The Lord’s Prayer follows. Then another prayer follows: “Deliver us, we beseech you, Lord.” When this has been completed, you break the bread, cover the gifts with the altar cloth, and ascend to the seat. There, when another oil has been offered by the deacon for blessing, you say:

“The Lord be with you.”

[Col. 1100C] Response: “And with your spirit.”

[Col. 1100D. Read: “He says.” We have emended it thus.] You say: “Let us pray.” Then you enter.

God, giver of spiritual increase and progress, who strengthen the beginnings of feeble minds by the power of your Holy Spirit, we pray to you, Lord, that you grant those who are to come to the bath of blessed regeneration, through the anointing of this created substance, purification of mind and body. If any remnants of hostile spirits cling to them, may they depart at the touch of this sanctified oil. May there be no place for spiritual wickedness, no power for hostile forces, and no opportunity left for evils lying in wait to hide. Rather, for your servants who come to the faith and are to be cleansed through the operation of the Holy Spirit, may the preparation of this anointing be useful for salvation, which they are also to obtain in the sacrament of baptism through the birth of heavenly regeneration. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the world by fire.

Again you say: “The Lord be with you.”

Response: “And with your spirit.”

“Lift up your hearts.”

Response: “We have them with the Lord.”  
[Col. 1100D. The exemplar incorrectly has: “from the Lord.”]

“Let us give thanks to the Lord our God.”

Response: “It is worthy and just.”

And it is just, right, and salutary that we should always and everywhere give thanks to you, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God. In the beginning, among the other gifts of your goodness and compassion, you commanded the earth to produce fruit-bearing trees. Among them were born olive trees, ministers of this richest liquid, whose fruit would serve the sacred chrism. For David, foreseeing the mysteries of your grace through the prophetic Spirit, sang that our faces were to be gladdened with oil.

And when the sins of the world were once being cleansed by the poured-out flood, a dove, prefiguring the gift to come, announced through an olive branch that peace had been restored to the earth. This was made evident in its effects in the last times, when, as the waters of baptism erase the guilt of all crimes, this anointing with oil makes our faces joyful and serene.

Therefore you also gave commands to your servant Moses, that he should appoint his brother Aaron priest, after first washing him with water, by pouring on him this ointment. Greater honor was added to this when your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, required John to wash him in the waters of the Jordan, and, when the Holy Spirit was sent down from above in the likeness of a dove, you clearly demonstrated by the testimony of the voice that followed that this was your Only-Begotten, in whom you were supremely pleased—the one whom the prophet David had sung was to be anointed with the oil of gladness above his companions.

Therefore we beseech you, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, through Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord, that you may deign to sanctify the richness of this created substance with your blessing and to mingle into it the power of the Holy Spirit through the might of your Christ, from whose holy name the chrism has received its name. From it you anointed your priests, kings, prophets, and martyrs, so that for those reborn of water and the Holy Spirit it may be the chrism of salvation, and so that you may make them participants in eternal life and sharers in heavenly glory. Through the same Lord Jesus Christ, your Son.

[Col. 1101D. Pamelius reads: “and to mingle the Holy Spirit into it.”]

**ALSO, THE PREPARATION OF EXORCISED OIL**

Here you mix balsam with oil, and the following exorcism is said.

I exorcise you, created substance of oil, in the name of God the almighty Father, and in the name of Jesus Christ his Son, and of the Holy Spirit, so that, at this invocation of the triple power and the might of the Godhead, every most wicked power of the adversary, every long-standing malice of the devil, every assault of violence, and every confused and blind phantom may be uprooted and driven away; depart from this created substance of oil, established for the benefit of human beings.

May this anointing, purified through the divine sacraments, become an adoption of flesh and spirit for those who are to be anointed with it for the remission of all sins, so that in them it may become sanctified for every spiritual grace of the body.  
[Col. 1101D. The exemplar has it incorrectly: “in adoption.”]  
[Col. 1101D. In the Roman Order: “for those who are to be anointed with it.”]  
[Col. 1101D. Read: “spiritual.”]

Through the same Jesus Christ our Lord, who is to come in the Holy Spirit to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire. Through the Lord.

Almighty and everlasting God, who, revealing the hidden things of your mysteries, showed to Noah’s eyes the grove attested by the dove’s beak, so that the inhabitants of the ark might learn through the Holy Spirit that, through the chrism of the olive, the glory of liberation would return to the world. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire.

When this has been completed, he comes before the altar and places a portion of that same host in the mouth of the chalice. He does not say, “The peace of the Lord,” nor do they exchange the kiss of peace; rather, they communicate and reserve part of that sacrifice for the next day, from which they may communicate.

[Col. 1102B] **ALSO ON THURSDAY. Mass at Vespers. Secret.**

Receive, we beseech you, Lord, the offering presented, and graciously accomplish this: that what we enact in the mystery of the passion, we may attain through devout effects. Through the Lord.  
[Col. 1101D. Pamelius has, for Friday: “through devout affections.”]

And it is just, through Christ our Lord. On this night, while he was reproving him amid the sacred meal, the conscience of the betrayer could not bear him; but, abandoning the company of the apostles, he received the price of blood from the Jews, so that he might lose the life which he had sold. Thus today the betrayer dined upon his own death, and with bloodstained hands received bread from the hand of the Savior, soon to depart, so that greater punishment might bind the man fattened by food—one whom not even the reward of compassion could recall from his crime.

Therefore your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, endured sharing his final meal with the enemy whom he knew would immediately betray him, so that he might leave the world an example of innocence and complete his passion for the redemption of the world.  
[Col. 1102D. Pamelius has: “The gentle God is fed.”]

Thus the gentle God feeds the barbarous Judas and tolerates the cruel fellow guest at the table until he destroyed himself by his own noose—the man who had considered the blood of his Master.  
[Col. 1102D. The same source reads: “the pious one tolerates the cruel fellow guest.” Read: “the cruel one.”]  
[Col. 1102D. We have corrected this from Menardus, since the exemplar incorrectly reads: “had forced.”]

O Lord, patient in all things! O Lamb, gentle amid your own banquet! Judas was still carrying his food in his mouth, and he was summoning Jewish executioners to tear your limbs apart. But your Son, our Lord, as a gracious victim, patiently allowed himself to be offered to you for us and released the sin that the world had committed. Through him we humbly beseech you, Lord, saying with humble confession.

**Within the Canon, as above.**

**Postcommunion.**

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that we may perceive both in body and in mind the mystery of the new sacrament we have received. Through.

[Col. 1103A] **For the people.**

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that just as we pass from former things to new, so, having laid aside the old condition, we may be renewed with sanctified minds. Through.

**XLI. HERE BEGINS THE ORDER FOR FRIDAY, THE PASSION OF THE LORD**

At the ninth hour everyone proceeds to the church, and the holy cross is placed upon the altar. The priest comes out from the sacristy with the sacred ministers in silence, singing nothing, and they come before the altar. The priest asks them to pray for him and says: “Let us pray.” The deacon announces: “Let us bend our knees.” After a short while he says: “Stand.” And he gives the prayer.

God, from whom Judas received the punishment for his guilt and the thief the reward of his confession, grant us the effect of your mercy, so that, just as Christ our Lord in his passion bestowed different rewards according to the merits of each, so he may grant us, with the error of our former state removed, the grace of his resurrection. He lives with you.  
[Col. 1103D. Pamelius has: “in the passion.”]

When this prayer has been completed, you go behind the altar [Col. 1103D. Read: “he goes.”], and a reading is read. Then follows a responsory.

Again the priest says: “Let us pray.” The deacon announces as above, and another prayer follows.

God, who through the passion of your Christ, our Lord, released the hereditary death of the ancient sin into which the whole race of posterity had entered, grant that, having been conformed to him, just as by necessity of nature we have borne the image of the earthly, so by the sanctification of grace we may bear the image of the heavenly, Christ our Lord. He lives with you.

Then a reading and responsory follow.

After this the Passion of the Lord is read.

When it has been completed, the priest begins the solemn prayers that follow.

Let us pray, dearly beloved, in the first place for the holy Church of God, that God and our Lord may deign to make it peaceful, united, and protected throughout the whole world, subjecting principalities and powers to it; and that he may grant us, living a tranquil and quiet life, to glorify God the almighty Father.

Let us pray.

[Col. 1103D] The deacon announces: “Let us bend our knees.” Again he says: “Stand.”

Almighty and everlasting God, who have revealed your glory among all the nations in Christ, preserve the works of your mercy, so that your Church, spread throughout the whole world, may persevere in a steadfast faith in confessing your name. Through.  
[Col. 1103D. Pamelius omits “your glory.”]  
[Col. 1103D. Read: “Through the Lord.”]

Let us pray also for our pope, the servant of God, N., of the apostolic see, and for our bishop, N., that almighty God, who chose them for the episcopal order, may keep them safe and unharmed for his holy Church, to govern God’s holy people.  
[Col. 1103D. “And for our bishop, N.” Pamelius and Menardus omit these words.]

Let us pray.

The deacon again announces as above.

Almighty and everlasting God, on whose eternal judgment all things are founded, look favorably upon our prayers and preserve in your compassion the bishops whom you have chosen for us, so that the Christian people, governed by such leaders, may increase in the merits of their faith under such great bishops. Through.  
[Col. 1104D. We have corrected this, since the exemplar incorrectly reads: “under such a bishop.” Pamelius and Menardus read: “under such a bishop,” because the prayer speaks only of the pope.]

Let us pray also for all bishops, priests, deacons, subdeacons, acolytes, exorcists, readers, doorkeepers, confessors, virgins, widows, and for all God’s holy people.

Let us pray.

The deacon again announces as above.

Almighty and everlasting God, by whose Spirit the whole body of the Church is sanctified and governed, hear us as we petition for all its orders, so that all may faithfully serve you through the gift of your grace. Through.  
[Col. 1104D. Pamelius has: “by all the ranks faithfully serving you.”]

Let us pray also for our most Christian emperor, or our king, N., that almighty God may subject all barbarian nations to them for our perpetual peace.

Let us pray.

The deacon again announces as above.

Almighty and everlasting God, who rule all kingdoms with eternal power, look favorably and kindly upon the Roman or Frankish empire, so that the peoples who trust in their own savagery may be subdued by the power of your right hand. Through.  
[Col. 1104D. Pamelius and Menardus have: “may be subdued by the right hand of your power.”]

Let us pray also for our catechumens, that God and our Lord may open the ears of their hearts and the door of mercy, so that, having received remission of all sins through the bath of regeneration, they may be found worthy in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Let us pray.

The deacon announces as above.

Almighty and everlasting God, who always make your Church fruitful with new offspring, increase the faith and understanding of our catechumens, so that, reborn in the baptismal font, they may be joined to the children of your adoption. Through.

Let us pray, dearly beloved, to God the almighty Father, that he may cleanse the world of all errors, remove diseases, drive away famine, open prisons, release bonds, grant travelers a return, the sick health, and those sailing a safe harbor.

[Col. 1105A] Let us pray.

The deacon announces as above.

Almighty and everlasting God, comfort of the sorrowful and strength of those who labor, may the prayers of those crying out to you from every tribulation reach you, so that all may rejoice that your mercy has been present to them in their needs. Through the Lord.

Let us pray also for heretics and schismatics, that God and our Lord may rescue them from every error and deign to restore them to the holy mother Church, catholic and apostolic. Through.

Let us pray.

The deacon announces as above.

Almighty and everlasting God, who save all and desire no one to perish, look upon the souls deceived by diabolical fraud, so that, every heretical perversity having been driven away, the hearts of those who err may come to their senses and return to the firmness of your truth. Through the Lord.

Let us pray also for the faithless Jews, that God and our Lord may remove the veil from their hearts, so that they too may recognize Christ Jesus our Lord.

Let us pray.

The deacon announces as above.

Almighty and everlasting God, who do not reject even Jewish faithlessness from your mercy, hear our prayers, which we offer to you for the blindness of that people, so that, having recognized the light of your truth, which is Christ, they may be rescued from their darkness. Through the Lord.

Let us pray also for the pagans, that almighty God may remove iniquity from their hearts and, abandoning their idols, they may be converted to the true God and his only Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. With him God lives and reigns in the unity of the Holy Spirit.

Let us pray.

The deacon announces as above.

Almighty and everlasting God, who always seek not the death but the life of sinners, graciously receive our prayer, free them from the worship of idols, and join them to your holy Church, for the praise and glory of your name. Through.

When these prayers written above have been completed, the deacons enter the sacristy. They come out with the body and blood of the Lord that had remained from the previous day and place it upon the altar. The priest comes before the altar, adores and kisses the Lord’s cross, and says: “Let us pray.” Then follows: “Instructed by saving commandments,” and the Lord’s Prayer. Then: “Deliver us, Lord, we beseech you.” When all this has been completed, everyone adores the holy cross and receives Communion.

**XLII. ON SATURDAY, IN THE MORNING, THE CHILDREN RECITE THE CREED**

First you catechize them, placing your hand upon their heads, in these words:

Nor are you unaware, Satan, that punishments threaten you, that torments threaten you [Col. 1106A], that the day of judgment threatens you, the day of punishment, the day that will come like a burning furnace, in which eternal destruction will come upon you and all your angels [Note: [Col. 1105D] We have corrected this, because the exemplar erroneously has: veniat, “may come.”]. Therefore, condemned one, give honor to the living and true God; give honor to Jesus Christ, his Son, and to the Holy Spirit. In whose name and power I command you to come out and depart from this servant of God, whom today the Lord our God Jesus Christ has deigned to call to his holy grace and blessing, and to the gift of the baptismal font, so that he may become his temple through the water of regeneration for the remission of all sins, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. He will come to judge the living and the dead, and the age by fire.

Then touch his nostrils and ears with spittle, and say into his ear [Col. 1106B]:

“Ephphatha,” which means, “Be opened to the fragrance of sweetness.” But as for you, devil, be driven away, for the judgment of God has drawn near.

Afterward touch his breast and the space between his shoulders with exorcised oil; and, calling him by name, say to each one:

“Do you renounce Satan?”

Response: “I renounce him.”

“And all his works?”

Response: “I renounce them.”

“And all his pomps?”

Response: “I renounce them.”

Then recite the Creed, laying your hand upon their heads. Afterward the archdeacon says to them:

[Col. 1106C] “Pray, elect ones; bend your knees. Complete your prayer together, and say: Amen.” And they all answer: “Amen.”

Again they are admonished by the archdeacon in these words:

“Catechumens, depart: all catechumens, go outside.”

Again the deacon says:

“Most beloved children, return to your places [Note: [Col. 1105D] Thus we have corrected it from the Roman Order, because the exemplar incorrectly reads: in locis vestris (‘in your places’).]: [Note: [Col. 1106D] It is omitted also in the Roman Order.] and await the hour when God’s grace may effect baptism in you.”

## THE ORDER FOLLOWS

### How they enter the vigil on Holy Saturday

For at the eighth hour, in the middle of the day, they proceed to the church; they enter the sacristy and put on the vestments, as is customary. The clergy begin the litany, and the priest proceeds from the sacristy with the sacred orders. They come before the altar and stand with bowed heads until they say, “Lamb of God, who take away the sins of the world, have mercy.” Then the priest rises from prayer and goes behind the altar, sitting in his seat.

Next the archdeacon comes before the altar, takes some of the light that had been concealed on Good Friday, makes a cross over the candle, lights it, and completes the blessing of the candle.

God, creator of the world, author of light, maker of the stars; God, who unveiled the world lying in darkness with clear light; God, through whose ineffable power the radiance of all things received its beginning: calling upon you in your works, in this most sacred vigil of the night we humbly offer to your Majesty, from your gifts, this candle—not polluted with the fat of flesh, not corrupted by profane anointing, not touched by sacrilegious fire, but constructed of wax, oil, and papyrus [Note: [Col. 1107D] Read: “bound together.” We have corrected this from the same Order.]—and kindled in honor of your name, we offer it in the service of religious devotion.

This great mystery, therefore, and the wondrous sacrament of this night must necessarily be crowned with worthy praises. In it the long-established darkness perceived that day had been brought in for itself by the miracle of the Lord’s resurrection. And death, which had once been condemned to eternal night, when the light of true radiance was introduced, was astonished to see itself led captive in the Lord’s triumphs. And that which, when the first-created man (primo plasto) transgressed [Note: [Col. 1107D] Thus corrected from the Roman Order. The exemplar corruptly reads: primo plaustro, “in the first wagon.”], had been condemned to servitude through dark presumption [Note: [Col. 1107D] Correct thus; the exemplar reads: servitute, “servitude.”], shines upon those set free by the splendor of this night’s miracle.

Therefore, descending in the fervor of the Spirit to honor this feast, insofar as human devotion requires, we offer you, God, peaceful lights glowing with the brilliance of flames, so that, while these rites are fulfilled in complete faith, the praises of your creature may also be exalted [Note: [Col. 1107D] Corrected. The exemplar reads: “are exalted.”]. For the light of the flame must be called that through which the power of the Godhead deigned to appear to Moses [Note: [Col. 1107D] Read: “Moses.”], which offered saving light as a guide to the people departing from the land of servitude, and which preserved life for the three youths cast into the furnace by the tyrant’s sentence, with gentler caresses.

For just as, when the grace of this light goes before us, the horror of darkness is driven away, so, Lord, when the authority of your Majesty shines forth, may the burdens of sins be washed away [Note: [Col. 1107D] From the Roman Order we have restored diluantur. The codex has deluantur, likewise “may be washed away.”].

Since, therefore, we marvel at the origin of this substance, we must necessarily praise the origin of the bees. Bees are frugal in their expenditures and most chaste in procreation. They build cells founded upon the liquid of wax, which the art of human skill cannot equal [Note: [Col. 1107D] Read: “of which”—thus corrected from the same Order. The exemplar corruptly reads: “founded, of which.”]. They gather flowers with their feet, and no damage is found in the flowers. They do not produce offspring, but, gathering with their mouths, they bring forth swarms of conceived young, just as, in a wondrous example, Christ proceeded from the Father’s mouth.

In them virginity is fruitful without childbirth; and the Lord, having deigned to follow it, established that he should have a human mother through love of virginity [Note: [Col. 1108D] “Which indeed,” according to the Roman Order. The exemplar reads: “and so.”]. Such gifts, therefore, Lord, are worthily offered upon your sacred altars, gifts with which Christian devotion does not doubt that you are pleased [Col. 1107D].

### Blessing over the incense

Let the abundant outpouring of your blessing, almighty God, therefore come upon this incense [Col. 1108A], and direct this nocturnal splendor, invisible ruler [Note: [Col. 1108D] In the Roman Missal: “kindle, regenerating ruler.”], so that not only may the sacrifice offered this night shine with the secret admixture of your light [Note: [Col. 1108D] The same has: “wherever.”], but wherever any portion of this sanctification is carried from the mystery [Note: [Col. 1108D] The same Missal adds: “of the mystery.”], may the power of your Majesty stand present, once the wickedness of diabolical deceit has been expelled.

Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who with you lives and reigns as God in the unity of the Holy Spirit, throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

After this the priest rises from his seat and recites the prayers of the Paschal vigil, as they are contained in the Sacramentary.

## XLIII. PRAYERS AFTER EACH READING ON HOLY SATURDAY

[Col. 1108B]

God, who lavish the riches of your mercy especially on this night, be gracious to the entire order of priestly ministry, and sanctify all the ranks of our service with complete remission of sins, so that you may not permit those who are to minister to your regenerating grace [Note: [Col. 1108D] Thus we have corrected it from the Missal of Cardinal Sanctorius, since the exemplar corruptly reads: “those regenerated.”] to be harmed by any offense [Note: [Col. 1108D] The aforementioned Missal has: “offense.”]. Through.

The reading follows: “In the beginning God made…”

God, unchangeable power, eternal light, look graciously upon the wondrous sacrament of your entire Church, and calmly carry out the work of human salvation according to your perpetual design. Let the whole world experience and see that what has been cast down is raised up, what has grown old is renewed, and that through the one from whom all things received their beginning everything returns to wholeness. Through, etc.

[Col. 1108C] The reading concerning Noah follows.

Almighty and everlasting God, wondrous in the ordering of all your works, let your redeemed understand that the world made in the beginning was not more excellent than Christ our Passover, sacrificed at the end of the ages [Note: [Col. 1108D] In the Ambrosian Mass apud Pamelius: “at the end.”]. Through the same Lord.

The third, concerning Abraham.

Most high Father of the faithful, who throughout the whole world multiply the children of your promise by the diffusion of adoption [Note: [Col. 1108D] The same Mass in Pamelius has: “and through.”], and by the Paschal sacrament make your servant Abraham the father of all nations, as you swore, grant that your peoples may worthily enter into the grace of your calling. Through.

The fourth, in Exodus, with the canticle: “Let us sing to the Lord.”

[Col. 1108D] God, whose ancient miracles we perceive shining even in our own age: just as by the power of your right hand you granted deliverance from Egyptian persecution to one people, so you work this for the salvation of the nations through the water of regeneration. Grant that the fullness of the whole world may pass into the children of Abraham and into Israelite dignity. Through.

The fifth, in Isaiah.

Almighty and everlasting God, multiply, for the honor of your name, what you promised to the faith of the Fathers, and enlarge the children of the promise through sacred adoption, so that what the holy men of old did not doubt would come to pass, your Church may now recognize as fulfilled in great part. Through.

The sixth, in Ezekiel.

God, who have instructed us, for the celebration of the Paschal sacrament, through the pages of both Testaments [Note: [Col. 1109D] Read: “of both.” The correction from Pamelius is nevertheless mistaken.], grant us understanding of your mercies, so that from receiving present gifts our expectation of future things may be firm. Through.

### VII. In Isaiah, with the canticle: “The Lord’s Vineyard”

God, who through the voice of the holy prophets have revealed in all the children of your Church that, in every place under your dominion, you are the planter of good seeds and the cultivator of chosen branches, grant to your peoples—who are reckoned by you both as vineyards and as fields—that, once the squalor of thorns and briars has been cut away, they may be made worthy to abound in fruitful produce. Through.

Likewise, the eighth, in Exodus.

God, who have made the diversity of all nations one in the confession of your name [Note: [Col. 1109D] The Missal of Cardinal Sanctorius has: “you united in the confession of your name.”], grant us both to will and to be able to do what you command, so that, for the people called to eternity, there may be one faith of minds and one devotion in actions [Col. 1109C]. Through.

[Note: [Col. 1109D] Delete IX.] IX. In Deuteronomy, with the canticle.

God, height of the humble and strength of rulers, who through your servant Moses so willed to instruct your peoples by the singing of your sacred song that the repetition of the Law might also become our direction, awaken your power over the whole fullness of the justified nations [Note: [Col. 1109D] In the same Missal: “and give joy.”], tempering terror with joy, so that, when all sins have been erased by your forgiveness, what was announced for vengeance may pass into salvation. Through.

The tenth, in Daniel.

Almighty and everlasting God, the world’s only hope, who through the proclamation of your prophets have made known the mysteries of the present times, graciously increase the vows of your people, since no growth of any virtue in the faithful proceeds from anywhere except your inspiration [Col. 1109D]. Through.

### Prayer after Psalm XLI

Almighty and everlasting God, look graciously upon the devotion of the people being reborn. As a deer awaits springs of water, so grant graciously that its thirst for faith may sanctify soul and body through the mystery of baptism.

[Col. 1110A] From there they proceed to the fonts with the litany for baptism. When baptism has been completed, the infants themselves are confirmed by the bishop as they receive the seven gifts of the grace of the Holy Spirit, and he applies chrism to their foreheads.

Afterward the priest himself returns with all the orders to the sacristy; and after a short while they begin the third litany and enter for the Masses of the vigil, when the star has appeared in the sky. Thus they should be arranged so that the litanies themselves are performed in the number of the Trinity.

## XLIV. THEN YOU DESCEND WITH THE LITANY TO THE FONT

### Blessing of the font

Almighty and everlasting God, be present to the mysteries of your great mercy [Col. 1110B]; be present to the sacraments; send the spirit of adoption for the creation of the new peoples whom the baptismal font brings forth for you; and may what must be carried out through the ministry of our humility be completed by the effect of your power. Through.

### Likewise, CONSECRATION OF THE FONT

God, who invisibly and wondrously bring about the effect of your sacraments through your power [Note: [Col. 1110D] Thus corrected from Pamelius. The exemplar has: “affection.”], and although we are unworthy to perform such great mysteries, nevertheless you do not abandon the gifts of your grace; incline even to our prayers the ears of your mercy.

God, whose Spirit was borne over the waters at the very beginning of the world, so that even then the nature of the waters might conceive the power of sanctification.

God, who, washing away the crimes of the guilty world through the waters, marked the pattern of regeneration in the outpouring of the Flood itself, so that, through the mystery of one and the same element, there might be both an end to vices and the beginning of virtues [Note: [Col. 1110D] Pamelius has: “so that it might be the end of one.”].

Look, Lord, upon the face of your Church, and multiply your generations within it [Note: [Col. 1110D] Thus corrected from Pamelius; the exemplar corruptly has: “which you make joyful by the impetus of your flowing grace.”], you who gladden your city by the outpouring of your flowing grace. Open the baptismal font throughout the world for the renewal of the nations, so that by the command of your Majesty it may receive the grace of your Only-Begotten from the Holy Spirit, who by the secret admixture of his light makes fruitful this water prepared for the regeneration of human beings.

Thus, once sanctification has been conceived, may a heavenly offspring emerge, reborn as a new creature from the immaculate womb of the divine font; and may the one mother, Grace, bring forth all those whom either sex distinguishes in body or age distinguishes in time [Note: [Col. 1110D] Read: “may bring forth.”].

Therefore, at your command, Lord, let every unclean spirit depart from here; let all the wickedness of diabolical deceit stand far away. Let no admixture of hostile power have any place here: let it not fly around by laying ambushes, steal in by hiding, or corrupt by infecting. Let this holy and innocent creature be free from every assault of its attacker, purified by the departure of all wickedness.

Let this be a living fountain of water that regenerates, a wave that purifies, so that all who are to be washed in this saving bath, with the Holy Spirit working in them [Col. 1111A], may obtain the forgiveness of perfect purification [Note: [Col. 1111D] Pamelius has: “of perfect purification.”].

Here you make the sign of the cross.

Therefore I bless you, creature of water, through the living God, through the holy God, through God who in the beginning separated you from the dry land by his word and commanded you to water the whole earth in four rivers. He who made you drinkable in the desert by imparting sweetness, and brought you forth from the rock for the thirsty people.

I bless you also through Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord. He who by a wondrous sign and his power changed you into wine at Cana of Galilee. He who walked upon you with his feet and was baptized in you by John in the Jordan. He who brought you forth together with blood from his side, and commanded his disciples that believers should be baptized in you [Col. 1111B], saying: “Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.”

Here you change the wording.

As we keep these commandments, you, almighty God, be mercifully present; you, in your kindness, breathe upon us. Bless these simple waters with your mouth, so that, beyond the natural cleansing they can provide to bodies being washed, they may also be effective for purifying minds.

Let the power of your Spirit descend into the fullness of this font, and make the entire substance of this water fruitful for regeneration [Note: [Col. 1111D] Thus corrected from Pamelius; the exemplar reads: “for regenerating.”]. Here let the stain of all sins be erased. Here let nature, created in your image and restored to the honor of its origin, be cleansed from every defilement of old age. Thus may every person who enters this sacrament of regeneration be reborn in true innocence as a new infant [Col. 1111C].

Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who will come in the Holy Spirit to judge the living and the dead and the age by fire.

Then, after blessing the font, you baptize each person in order, with these questions [Note: [Col. 1111D] Thus we have corrected it, since the exemplar corruptly reads: “under these questions.”]:

“Do you believe in God the Father almighty?”

Response: “I believe.”

“And do you believe in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, born and having suffered?”

Response: “I believe.”

“And do you believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy Church, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the flesh?”

[Col. 1111D] Response: “I believe.”

Then immerse him three times in the water, once at each question.

After the infant has risen from the font, the presbyter signs him on the head with chrism, saying:

God, almighty Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has regenerated you from water and the Holy Spirit and has given you remission of all sins, may he himself anoint you with the chrism of salvation in Christ Jesus our Lord unto eternal life.

[Col. 1112A] Response: “Amen.”

Then the sevenfold Spirit is given to them by the bishop. For the signing, he lays his hand upon them, saying:

God almighty, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who have regenerated your servants from water and the Holy Spirit and have given them remission of all sins, you, Lord, send upon them your Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, and give them the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and fortitude, the Spirit of knowledge and piety. Fill them with the Spirit of the fear of God, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom you live and reign as God, always with the Holy Spirit, throughout all ages of ages.

[Note: [Col. 1111D] Delete “Response.”] Response: “Amen.”

Afterward he signs them on the forehead with chrism, saying:

[Col. 1112B] “The sign of Christ unto eternal life.”

Response: “Amen.”

“Peace be with you.”

Response: “And with your spirit.”

Then, with the litany, he ascends to his seat and says:

“Glory to God in the highest.”

## XLV. PRAYERS AND PREFACES FOR THE MASS AT NIGHT

Almighty and everlasting God, who illumine this most sacred night throughout all the regions of the world with the glory of the Lord’s resurrection [Note: [Col. 1112D] Read: gloriosae, “glorious”—but incorrectly. It has nevertheless been corrected from Pamelius.], preserve in the new offspring of your family the Spirit of sanctification whom you have given, so that, renewed in body and mind, they may always present to you a pure soul and a pure heart [Col. 1112C]. Through the Lord.

God, who illumine this most sacred night with the glory of the Lord’s resurrection, preserve in the new offspring of your family the spirit of adoption whom you have given, so that, renewed in body and mind, they may present pure service to you. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Receive, we ask, Lord, the offerings both of your people and of those reborn through you, so that, renewed by confession of your name and by baptism, they may attain everlasting blessedness. Through the Lord.

### Another

Receive, Lord, the prayers of your people together with the offerings of sacrifices, so that, having been initiated into the Paschal mysteries [Col. 1112D], they may, through your working, advance toward our healing unto eternity. Through the Lord.

And it is right, just, and salutary. For the most desired time is present to us, and the light of the longed-for night has arrived. What greater or better thing could be found than to proclaim the power of the rising Lord? For today, breaking the bars of hell, he took up the brightest banners of his resurrection [Note: [Col. 1112D] Read: “most beloved.” We have corrected it from Pamelius, where it reads: “he took up bright banners.” The exemplar corruptly reads: “most beloved.”], and, returning as man, he brought into the sight of the astonished stars the human being cast down by the enemy’s envy [Col. 1113A].

O mystical and venerable exchanges of this night! O pious and everlasting benefits of holy Mother Church! She does not wish to have what she might destroy, but desires to find what she might redeem. Mary rejoiced in the most sacred childbirth [Note: [Col. 1113D] The exemplar incorrectly reads: “in childbirth.”]. The Church rejoices in the appearance of the birth of her children. Thus that blessed fountain, which shone forth from the Lord’s side [Note: [Col. 1113D] Read: “surrounded with light.”], received the mass of vices, so that through these sacred altars it might provide the life-giving food of eternal life to those reborn. And therefore, with the angels.

Indeed, at all times, but more gloriously on this most powerful night, we praise you, when Christ our Passover was sacrificed. For he is the true Lamb who took away the sins of the world; who by dying destroyed our death, and by rising restored life [Col. 1113B]. Therefore the whole world throughout the earth rejoices in abundant Paschal joy. The heavenly powers and angelic authorities also sing together the hymn of your glory, saying without end.

### Within the Canon

Being in communion, and celebrating the most sacred night of the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ according to the flesh. And also commemorating.

### Likewise within the Canon [Note: [Col. 1114D] Read: “within the action.”]

Therefore, Lord, graciously receive this offering of our service and of your entire family, which we offer to you also for those whom you have deigned to regenerate from water and the Holy Spirit, granting them remission of all sins, so that you might find them in Christ Jesus our Lord. For them we pour forth suppliant prayers to your Majesty, asking that you command their names to be written in the book of the living; and our days [Col. 1113C].

### Postcommunion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, having been satisfied with the divine gift, we may be renewed both by the sacred mysteries and in our conduct.

### Another

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the reception of the Paschal sacrament may continue and remain in our minds. Through.

## XLVI. EASTER SUNDAY

God, who by your Only-Begotten, having conquered death, have opened for us the entrance to eternity, grant, we ask, that we who celebrate the solemn rites of the Lord’s resurrection may rise from the death of the soul through the renewal of your Spirit. Through the Lord.

God, who gladden us by the annual solemnity of the Lord’s resurrection, graciously grant that through the temporal feasts we celebrate we may be found worthy to attain eternal joys. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Receive graciously, Lord, the gifts of your servants, so that, renewed by confession of your name and by baptism, they may attain everlasting blessedness. Through the Lord.

Indeed, at all times, but especially on this day, we praise, bless, and proclaim you, because Christ our Passover was sacrificed [Col. 1114A]. Through him the children of light are born into eternal life, the courts of the heavenly kingdom are opened to the faithful, and, by a blessed exchange, human things are changed into divine. For the death of all of us has been redeemed by Christ’s cross, and in his resurrection the life of all has risen again. In the assumption of mortality we recognize the God of Majesty; and in the glory of divinity we confess God and man. Jesus Christ our Lord destroyed our death by dying and restored life by rising. And therefore, with the angels.

Within the Canon, as above on the holy night.

It follows:

[Col. 1114B] ### Postcommunion

Almighty and everlasting God, who restore us to eternal life in Christ’s resurrection, preserve the works of your mercy, and pour into our breasts the sweetness of the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, your Only-Begotten Son. Through the Lord.

## XLVII. THE PRAYERS AND PREFACES FOR THE WHOLE OCTAVE BEGIN. MONDAY

As we recall the Paschal mystery, Lord, may we be strengthened by the prayers of the blessed apostles, whose teaching has made known to us what must be carried out. Through.

God, redeemer and perfecter of your Church [Col. 1114C], grant, we ask, that through the prayers of the apostles we may receive the gifts of the Paschal sacrament, which you have given us to preach through their teaching. Through.

### Secret

Lord, we offer sacrifices amid Paschal joys, by which your Church is wondrously reborn and nourished.

We ask your mercy, that, in order to celebrate the Paschal mystery worthily, we may be assisted by the prayers of the blessed apostles, and that what we received as something to be believed through their preaching we may faithfully carry out through their patronage. Through Christ the Lord.

Within the Canon, as above on the holy night.

[Col. 1114D] It follows:

### Postcommunion

May the holy libation of the Paschal sacrament be fulfilled in us, we ask, Lord, and may it transfer us from earthly attachments to a heavenly way of life. Through.

## XLVIII. TUESDAY

God, who have bestowed Paschal remedies upon us, accompany your people with a heavenly gift, so that they may rejoice forever afterward in that from which they now rejoice for a time. Through.

God, who graciously work heavenly remedies for the world through the Paschal solemnity, accompany the annual gifts of this feast [Col. 1115A], so that observance in time may advance toward eternal life. Through.

### Secret

Receive graciously, Lord, we ask, the offerings that we bring both for the expiation of the sin of those reborn and for the hastening of heavenly aid. Through.

Through Christ our Lord. He who, by offering himself for our salvation, removed the sacrifices of carnal victims and displayed himself to you as both priest and sacred Lamb. Whom they praise.

Within the Canon, as above on the holy night.

It follows:

### Postcommunion

Be present, Lord, we ask, to the effects of our redemption [Col. 1115B] [Note: [Col. 1115D] Read: effectibus, “effects.”], so that those whom you instruct through the sacraments of eternity you may graciously protect, fitting them for the same.

May the saving food and sacred drink make us worthy to serve your name, Lord, we ask, so that they may continually bring about in our minds the renewal of the human condition, which the mystery contains [Note: [Col. 1115D] Read: “which.” The Ambrosian Mass has: “which may work.”].

## XLVIIII. WEDNESDAY

God, who made the Paschal sacrifice for the salvation of the world, be gracious to our supplications, so that the supreme priest who intercedes for us may absolve those whom he reconciles through what is like us, by what is equal to you—Jesus Christ our Lord. Who lives and reigns with you.

God, who made all those reborn in Christ a royal and priestly race [Note: [Col. 1115D] Thus corrected from Pamelius in the prayers after the Sunday in White. The exemplar corruptly reads: “all who in…”] [Note: [Col. 1116D] Read: “kingdom”—but less correctly. Corrected from Pamelius in the same place.], grant us both to will and to be able to do what you command, so that, for the people called to eternity, there may be one faith of hearts and one devotion in actions [Col. 1115C]. Through.

### Secret

Receive, we ask, Lord, the offerings of human redemption, and graciously work salvation for us in mind and body. Through our Lord.

As we surround your altars with hosts of virtues and glory in recognition of that immaculate Lamb who offered himself to be sacrificed for us, may we be nourished by heavenly sacrifices with his body and blood [Note: [Col. 1116D] The exemplar has: “in the blood.” Read: “and blood.”], by which we have been redeemed from sins, unto eternal life. Through Christ the Lord.

Within the Canon, as above on the holy night.

It follows:

[Col. 1115D] ### Postcommunion

Be present, Lord, we ask, to the desires of our redemption, so that those whom you instruct through the sacraments of eternity you may graciously protect, fitting them for the same [Note: [Col. 1116D] Read: “for the same.”]. Through our Lord.

## L. THURSDAY

God, who multiply the offspring of those being reborn [Note: [Col. 1116D] Read: “of those being reborn.”], graciously make them rejoice in the forgiveness of their sins. Through.

God, who prepare human nature above the dignity of its first origin [Note: [Col. 1116D] The Ambrosian Mass on Easter Day has: “restore.”], look upon the ineffable sacrament of your mercy, so that in those whom you have deigned to renew through the mysteries of regeneration you may preserve the gifts of your perpetual grace and blessing. Through our Lord.

### Secret

Grant, we ask, Lord, that through these Paschal mysteries we may always rejoice, so that the continual work of our restoration may become for us an everlasting cause of joy. Through our Lord.

For when the old has been destroyed, all things cast down are renewed; and integrity of life is restored to us in Christ [Col. 1116B]. Whom the angels praise.

Within the Canon, as above on the holy night.

It follows:

### Postcommunion

Having purified our minds graciously, Lord, we ask, renew them through heavenly sacraments, so that consequently we may receive both present and future aid for our bodies [Note: [Col. 1116D] Read: “Purification”—though this is nevertheless incorrect.]. Through.

## LI. FRIDAY

God, who open the entrance to the heavenly kingdom only to those reborn from water and the Holy Spirit, continually increase the gifts of your grace upon your servants, so that those who have been cleansed from all sins may be deprived of none of the promises. Through the Lord.

[Col. 1116C] God, who have renewed believers in you through the baptismal font, grant this protection to those reborn in Christ, so that they may not lose the grace of your blessing through any attack of error. Through.

### Secret

As we recall the Paschal sacrifices, we ask, Lord, that what we celebrate in action we may grasp in effect. Through.

Through Christ our Lord. He who, according to the unchangeable truth of his promise, became the heavenly High Priest forever, alone among all priests had no need of the remission of sin; rather, he, the true Lamb, wiped away the sin of the world. And therefore, with the angels.

[Col. 1116D] Within the Canon, as above on the holy night.

It follows:

### Postcommunion

Having obtained the nourishment of immortality, we ask, Lord, that what we receive with the mouth we may pursue with the mind. Through the Lord.

## LII. SATURDAY

God, who have granted us to celebrate your Passover with rejoicing hearts [Col. 1117A], grant, we ask, that we may rejoice both in temporal supports and in the effects of eternity. Through the Lord.

God, restorer and lover of innocence, direct the hearts of your servants toward yourself, so that those whom you have freed from the darkness of unbelief may never depart from the light of your truth. Through.

### Secret

Receive, we ask, Lord, the gifts of your rejoicing Church, and grant a perpetual fruit of joy to her to whom you have given the cause of such great rejoicing.

We earnestly beseech you that we may be able to grasp the manifest gifts of Jesus Christ our Lord, whose pledge we have received, and may be found worthy to attain what the Paschal sacrament has happily bestowed for us to hope for [Col. 1117B], through the firmness of the Lord’s resurrection. And therefore, with the angels.

Within the Canon, as above on the holy night.

It follows:

### Postcommunion

May the grace of the Paschal sacrament overflow, we ask, Lord, in our minds, so that it may itself make us worthy by its gifts [Note: [Col. 1117D] In the Ambrosian Mass on White Sunday it reads: “May it itself make us worthy of your gifts.”]. [Note: [Col. 1117D] Delete “Through.”]

## LIII. THE OCTAVE OF EASTER. ON SUNDAY

God, who by baptism take away death from those reborn and grant eternal life, grant, we ask, that, as we now celebrate the eighth day of their sacred regeneration [Col. 1117C], you may so guard their bodies and souls that, through the protection of your mercy, they may recognize that they have received the grace of the catholic faith. Through.

God, who multiply the peoples believing in you through the abundance of your grace, look graciously upon your chosen ones, so that those who have been reborn through the sacrament of baptism may be found worthy to enter the heavenly kingdom. Through.

### Secret

Receive, we ask, Lord, the offerings of your family, so that under the help of your protection they may neither lose what has been granted [Note: [Col. 1117D] Read: “consoled”—a corrupt form. Thus we have corrected it.] nor fail to reach eternal gifts. Through.

We earnestly implore your mercy, that your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who promised to be with his faithful until the end of the age and does not abandon those whom he redeemed in the mysteries of his bodily presence [Col. 1117D], may not leave them without the benefits of his Majesty [Note: [Col. 1117D] Pamelius adds: “also.”]. And therefore, with.

Within the Canon, as above.

It follows:

[Note: [Col. 1117D] Postcommunion. Read: “Communion.”] ### Postcommunion

We humbly beseech your Majesty, Lord, that those whom you have made enter the way of everlasting salvation you may not permit to become entangled in any snares of error. Through.

## LIV. PRAYERS AND PREFACES FOR THE ANNIVERSARY OF EASTER

[Col. 1118A]

God, by whose providence neither the moments of the past fail nor any expectation of the future remains, grant a lasting effect to the solemnity we have completed and recall, so that what we review in memory we may always maintain in practice. Through.

God, who have granted forgiveness of sins to those reborn in the baptismal font, mercifully grant that, as we recall the marks of this birth, you may lavish the full grace of adoption. Through.

### Secret

We earnestly implore your mercy, Lord, that we may receive with perpetual love the sacrament of the Paschal gift, which we recall in faith and ardently desire in hope [Col. 1118B]. Through the Lord.

Through Christ our Lord [Note: [Col. 1118D] Pamelius adds: “and.”], to recall the feasts of our redemption, in which human substance, freed from the bonds of transgression, received the hope of resurrection through the renewed dignity of its origin [Note: [Col. 1118D] In the margin: “Alternatively, ‘assumed.’ Pamelius has: ‘assumed dignity.’”]. Through whom [we proclaim] your Majesty.

Within the Canon.

Therefore, Lord, graciously heed this offering of your male and female servants, which they offer to you while recalling the annual mysteries through which you adopted them into your royal ordinances. For them we pour forth suppliant prayers, asking that you preserve in them what has been granted [Note: [Col. 1118D] “And.”], so that you may lavish the rewards of promised blessedness, and our days [Col. 1118C].

### Postcommunion

May your holy gifts, which we have received, purify us, we ask, Lord, and by the remedy of their working perfect us, so that we may be pleasing [Note: [Col. 1118D] Alternatively: “purified”—thus also Pamelius]. Through the Lord.

## LV. PRAYERS AND PREFACES IN THE PARISH
God, who are both the restorer and ruler of the human race, grant, we beseech you, that your Church may always increase through new offspring and grow through the devotion of all her children. Through.
