Renewed by the font and by the power of your Spirit, mercifully number us among the hereditary people, so that those who have been cleansed from a multitude of sins may also be deemed worthy of an abundance of invisible rewards. Through.

[Note: [Col. 1118D] In the margin: Secret.] We offer you praises and gifts, Lord; giving thanks for benefits already granted, we humbly plead for those yet to be granted. Through.

We humbly beseech you to grant your faithful so that they may receive the paschal sacraments and eagerly await what is to come [Note: [Col. 1118D] In the margin: Alternatively, “the coming one.”], so that, remaining in the mysteries through which they were reborn, they may be led to new life by these works. And therefore, with the angels.

## After Communion

May this holy paschal mystery, we beseech you, Lord, assist us, and may it obtain for us that we carry it out with devoted minds. Through.

## For the People

May your people, we beseech you, Lord, always rejoice with the renewed youth of the soul, so that those who had formerly come into death’s lethargic old age through sins [Note: [Col. 1119D] Alternatively, “lethargy.”] may now rejoice that they have been restored to their former glory. Through.

## LVI. Paschal Evening Prayers Begin

God, who restore us to eternal life in the resurrection of Christ, fulfill the ineffable mystery of your goodness, [Col. 1119B] so that, when our Savior comes in his majesty, those whom you caused to be reborn through baptism you may cause to be clothed with blessed immortality. Through the Lord.

Mercifully grant us, we beseech you, Lord, the remedies of Easter, so that, rejecting earthly desires, we may learn to long for heavenly things. Through.

We beseech you, almighty God, that we may no longer be held subject to the sentence of human condemnation, from whose bond this paschal redemption has absolved us. Through the Lord.

Grant, merciful God, that what we perform according to the rites of Easter may at all times prove fruitful for us. Through.

Increase the faith of your people, we beseech you, Lord, so that the faith which it received its beginning from you may receive its growth from you. Through.

Grant us, almighty God, that, receiving forgiveness of sins through the paschal gift, we may thereafter avoid sins. Through the Lord.

God, through whom both redemption has come to us and adoption has been bestowed, look upon the works of your mercy, so that those reborn in Christ may be granted both an eternal inheritance and true freedom. Through.

God, who through your Only-Begotten Son, having conquered death, opened for us the way to eternity, raise up to yourself the hearts of your believers, so that every generation may grasp by its merits what it receives through the mysteries. Through.

Almighty and eternal God, lead us into the fellowship of heavenly joys, so that, reborn through the Holy Spirit, you may grant us entrance into your kingdom; and may the humility of the flock reach the place to which the strength of the Shepherd advanced. [Note: [Col. 1119D] Alternatively, “to it.”] Through.

God, who open the entrance of the heavenly kingdom to those reborn through water and the Holy Spirit, increase upon your servants the grace you have given, so that those cleansed from all sins may be deprived of none of your promises. Through.

Blot out, we beseech you, Lord, the written bond of sin, recorded under the law, which through the paschal mystery you nullified in us by the resurrection of your Son. Through.

[Col. 1120A] Grant, almighty God, that we who, renewed by the paschal remedies [Note: [Col. 1119D] We have emended this from Pamelius; in the exemplar it is corruptly written “you renewed.”], have escaped the likeness of our earthly parent may be transferred into the likeness of the heavenly Author. Through.

Grant, merciful God, that in the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ we too may truly find a portion. Through the Lord.

Be present, we beseech you, Lord; be present to your household and mercifully grant that, to those to whom you have bestowed the grace of faith, you may also grant an eternal crown. Through.

Hear us, almighty God, and prepare the hearts of your household, to whom you have bestowed the complete grace of baptism, to merit eternal blessedness. [Note: [Col. 1120D] “Through.”]

Preserve your mercy in us, we beseech you, Lord, and cause those whom you have freed from the darkness of error [Col. 1120B] to cling more firmly to the teaching of your truth. Through.

With watchful mercy, we beseech you, Lord, guard those whom you have washed, so that those who have been redeemed by your Passion may rejoice in your resurrection. Through our Lord.

Look upon the Christian people, we beseech you, Lord, and mercifully absolve from temporal faults those whom you have deigned to renew through eternal mysteries. Through.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, continually pursuing divine things, we may always be deemed worthy to draw near to heavenly gifts. Through.

Almighty and eternal God, may we more earnestly obtain your mercy during these days in which, through your generosity, we have come to know it more fully. Through the Lord.

Grant, merciful God, that your devoted people may exist as such and may continually obtain from your clemency what benefits them. Through.

God, who perceive that our minds are held back by earthly activities, grant, we beseech you, that we may rather be fitted by your gift for your remedies. Through.

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that the affection of Christian devotion may always strive toward that place where our substance is with you. Through.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that your Church may rejoice both in the soundness of her members [Note: [Col. 1120D] Read “in the weakness of her members.” This has been corrected from Pamelius, at Thursday in White Week, since the text was faulty.] and in ever-new fruitfulness. Through.

Bestow, we beseech you, God, upon your Church the grace both always to refrain from her own offenses and from those of others, so that, serving you with a pure mind, she may without ceasing receive the remedies of your goodness. Through the Lord.

## LVII. Prayers and Petitions for the Sunday after the Octave of Easter

[Col. 1120D]

God, who raised up the fallen world through the humility of your Son, grant joy, so that those whom you have rescued from the perpetual disasters [Note: [Col. 1120D] In the margin: Alternatively, “of eternal death.”] may be made to enjoy everlasting gladness. Through.

God, whose chief wonders include the restoration of humanity, destroy the works of the devil and break apart the deadly bonds of sin, [Col. 1121A] so that, once the evil that caused harm has been destroyed, the mercy that redeemed may prevail. Through.

### Secret

May the sacred oblation always confer upon us, Lord, a saving blessing, so that what it effects as a mystery it may accomplish in power. Through.

May we always and everywhere give thanks to you and humbly beseech you to be so instructed by your eternal gifts that you may console us amid temporal things; so refreshed by present things that you may lead us to lasting joys. Through Christ our Lord.

### After Communion

Grant us, almighty God, that, having received the grace of your life-giving power, we may always glory in your gift. Through the Lord.

## LVIII. Likewise, Second Sunday after the Close of Easter

God, who show the light of your truth to those who wander so that they may return to the way [Note: [Col. 1121D] We have corrected this from Menardus, since the exemplar incorrectly reads: “to those who wander, so that they could be on the way.”], grant to all who are reckoned by the Christian profession both to reject what is hostile to this name and to follow what is suited to it. Through the Lord.

Grant your people, our God, a will pleasing to you, because you will then bestow every prosperity upon them when you have made them suited to your ordinances. Through the Lord.

### Secret

May these mysteries, Lord, grant us [Note: [Col. 1121D] Alternatively, “be granted to us”] that, while mitigating earthly desires, we may learn to possess heavenly things. [Col. 1121C] Through.

Through Christ our Lord. Who, taking pity on human errors, deigned to be born through the Virgin, and through the suffering of death freed us from everlasting death, and by his resurrection bestowed eternal life upon us. Him the angels praise.

### After Communion

May the sacraments that we have received, we beseech you, Lord, both cleanse us through spiritual nourishment and protect us through bodily assistance. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## LIX. Third Sunday after the Close of Easter

[Col. 1121D] God, who make the minds of the faithful one in will, grant your peoples to love what you command and to desire what you promise, so that amid worldly variations our hearts may be fixed there where true joys are found. Through.

Hear our prayers, Lord, so that what has been promised through the sanctification of your Word may everywhere be fulfilled by evangelical effect, and that the fullness of adoption may obtain what the testimony of truth foretold. Through [Note: [Col. 1122D] Delete “the Lord.”].

### Secret

God, who through the venerable exchange of this sacrifice have made us participants in the one supreme Divinity, grant, we beseech you, that just as we have come to know your truth, so we may attain it through worthy conduct. Through.

Asking from your gift that we may treat with devout dedication the times during which, after the resurrection, our Lord Jesus Christ dwelt bodily with his disciples. Through the Lord.

### After Communion

Be present, Lord our God, so that through what we have faithfully received we may both be cleansed from vices and stripped of every danger. [Note: [Col. 1122D] In the margin: Alternatively, “rescued.”] Through our Lord.

## LX. Fourth Sunday after the Close of Easter

God, from whom all good things proceed, grant those who plead with you [Col. 1122B] that, with you inspiring us, we may think what is right and, with you governing us, do the same. Through.

God, who willed the door of mercy to stand open to the faithful, look upon us and have mercy on us, so that we who, by your gift, follow the way of your will may never stray from the paths of life. Through.

### Secret

Grant, Lord, we beseech you, that we may receive the effect of that salvation whose pledge we have received through these mysteries. Through the Lord.

Since the first sign of your goodness is that you make us subject to you with our whole heart, infuse into us the spirit of such devotion that, being favorable, you may consequently bestow your help. Through.

### After Communion

Grant us, Lord, who have been satisfied by the power of the heavenly table, both to desire what is right and to receive what we have desired. Through.

## LXI. Fifth Sunday after the Close of Easter

Almighty and eternal God, make us always both carry out a will devoted to you and serve your majesty with a sincere heart. Through.

God, life of the faithful, glory of the humble, blessedness of the righteous, graciously receive the prayers of those who plead with you, so that the souls that thirst for your promises may always be filled from your abundance. Through our Lord.

### Secret

May the offering dedicated to your name, Lord, purify us and transfer us day by day to the practice of heavenly life. Through the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 1122D] Alternatively, “so that.”] Fashion our minds always through good works, because we shall thus be worshippers distinguished by the ready sincerity of our service, if, continually advancing toward better things, we strive to possess the paschal mystery perpetually. Through whom is majesty.

### After Communion

Filled with sacred gifts, Lord, grant, we beseech you, that we may remain always in thanksgiving. Through.

## LXII. Sixth Sunday after the Close of Easter

[Col. 1123A]

God, strength of those who hope in you, graciously be present to our invocations; and because mortal weakness can do nothing without you, grant the help of your grace, so that in carrying out your commands we may please you both in will and in action. Through the Lord.

God of hope, pure light of minds [Note: [Col. 1123D] In the margin: “light.”] and perfect light of the blessed, who truly are the light of your Church, grant our hearts both to offer you worthy prayer and always to praise you with the gift of proclamation. Through.

### Secret

Graciously receive, Lord, our offerings dedicated to you, [Col. 1123B] and grant us to attain everlasting assistance. [Note: [Col. 1123D] Alternatively, “proceed.”] Through.

As you do not cease to instruct the children of your Church, so do not cease to assist them, so that they may know what ought rightly to be done [Note: [Col. 1123D] In the margin: “to be done.”] and may receive the ability to carry it out. Through Christ.

### After Communion

Filled with such great gifts, Lord, grant, we beseech you, that we may receive saving gifts and never cease from your praise. Through.

### For the People

May the desired blessing confirm your faithful, Lord; may it cause them never to disagree with your will and always permit them to rejoice in your benefits. Through.

## LXIII. Prayers and Petitions for the Ascension of the Lord

[Col. 1123C]

God, who today, in order to display the wonders of your majesty, ascended into heaven in the presence of the apostles after rising from the dead, grant us the help of your goodness, so that, according to your promise, you may always be with us on earth and we may deserve to live with you in heaven. Through.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty Father, that the attention of our mind may always be directed to the place into which the glorious Author of today’s solemnity has entered [Note: [Col. 1123D] We have corrected this, since the exemplar corruptly reads “solemnity”], and that it may reach in conduct the place toward which it proceeds by faith. Through.

### Secret

We humbly present, Lord, the sacrifice for the venerable Ascension of your Son; grant, we beseech you, that through him we too may rise to heavenly things through these sacred exchanges. Through.

Through Christ our Lord. Who deigned to come to the aid of human salvation: by being born, he gave us glory; by suffering, he conquered the devil; by rising from the dead, he granted access to eternal life; by ascending to the Father, he restored the heavenly gates [Note: [Col. 1123D] “He opened.”]. Him the angels praise.

[Col. 1124A] ### Within the Canon

Sharing in communion and celebrating the most sacred day on which your Only-Begotten Son, our Lord, placed the human being united to himself, of our substance, at the right hand of your glory. And also commemorating.

Then, a little before the canon has been completed, he blesses the new fruits.

### The Blessing Follows

Bless, Lord, these new fruits of the bean, which you, Lord, have deigned to bring to maturity through heavenly dew and abundant rains, so that we may receive them with thanksgiving in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Through whom, O Lord, always good—and—

When the canon has been completed. [Note: [Col. 1124D] Read: “good, up to the completion of the Canon.”]

[Col. 1124B] ### After Communion

God, whose Son, powerfully ascending on high into the heavens, led our captivity captive by his might, grant, we beseech you, that he may bestow upon us also the gifts he granted to those who participate in him. Through our Lord.

### For the People

With our understanding raised up and the eyes of our heart lifted to the heights, we beseech you that what we have brought forward as the vows of our prayers we may carry back as confidence in obtaining them. Through.

## LXIV. Another Mass

Be present, Lord, to our supplications, so that just as we trust that the Savior of the human race has sat with you in your majesty, so we may experience him remaining with us until the end of the age, as he promised. Through.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that through the gift of today’s festival the attention of your children may be directed to the place where our substance is with you in your Only-Begotten Son. Through.

### Secret

May the spotless sacrifices purify us, Lord, and give strength to our minds through heavenly grace. Through the Lord.

Especially on this day, [Note: [Col. 1124D] Read “on which.”] when Jesus Christ, your Son, our Lord, having completed the divine conclusion of the mystery, fulfilled the work of the ancient dispensation [Note: [Col. 1124D] Thus corrected from Pamelius; the exemplar incorrectly reads “hand”], namely, that through the human being whom the enemy had subjugated he might crush the enemy of the heavenly work [Note: [Col. 1124D] Corrected from the same source; the exemplar corruptly has “enemy”], the devil, and restore the human substance to heavenly gifts. And therefore, with the angels.

### Within the Canon, as Above

It follows:

### After Communion

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that through these sacred things which we have received the affection of our devotion may strive toward that place where our substance is with you. Through the Lord.

[Col. 1125A] ### For the People

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the members of your faithful may follow to that place where our head, the beginning, has gone before. [Note: [Col. 1125D] In the margin: Alternatively, “which.”] Through the Lord.

## LXV. Prayers and Petitions for the Sunday after the Ascension of the Lord

Make us, Lord, possess perpetual fear and love of your holy name together, because you will never abandon those whom you establish in the firmness of your love. Through.

God, who declare that you remain in upright and sincere hearts, grant us by your grace to become such as you deign to inhabit. Through the Lord.

### Secret

May the offering, Lord, to be dedicated to your name purify us and transfer us day by day to the practice of heavenly life. Through our Lord.

This was his wondrous work and saving mystery: that we, long lost and laid low by the devil and the sting of death, should be called to this glory, because now we are called a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a people of acquisition, and a holy nation. Therefore, giving unceasing thanks and proclaiming holy generosity, we bring these sacred offerings to your majesty, which Christ himself, the author of our salvation, instituted for us. Him the angels praise.

### After Communion

Having received the gifts, Lord, we beseech you: through frequent participation in your mystery, may the affection of our salvation increase. Through our Lord.

### For the People

Bless your household in heavenly things, Lord, and fill it with your spiritual gifts. Grant them charity, joy, peace, patience, goodness, gentleness, hope, faith, and self-control, so that, filled with all your gifts—chastity [Note: [Col. 1125D] “Chastity” is redundant]—they may deserve to attain you whom they desire. Through our Lord.

## LXVI. On the Saturday of Pentecost you shall celebrate baptism, as on the night of holy Easter. The Laying-on of Hands over a Sick Catechumen

We implore the countless attentions of your healing, Lord, [Col. 1125D] holy Father, almighty and eternal God, which Christ distributes to human weaknesses. Raise up your servant, weighed down by the weakness of illness, and deign to refresh all his senses through your visitations, so that he may be able to receive your adoption with the joy of health. Therefore drive away from him every weapon of contrary illness, so that he may advance step by step toward your grace. Raise up him whom you glory in redeeming, so that baptism may be for him the palm of victory, not of death, and so that he may always bear gloriously the sign of the cross that he receives. [Col. 1126A] Through Christ our Lord, who will come to judge the living and the dead.

## LXVII. Another Laying-on of the Hand [Note: [Col. 1125D] Read: “after the hand has been laid on.”] over a Possessed Catechumen

Almighty and eternal God, before whose face the heavens drip, mountains melt like wax, the earth trembles, the abysses lie open, hell is afraid, and every movement of wrath is humbled when it looks upon you, I suppliantly beseech you, Lord and Ruler, that at the invocation of your name the enemy may depart in confusion from the affliction of this servant of yours [Note: [Col. 1125D] “So that”], and that, once the soul has been freed from this possession [Note: [Col. 1126D] “To the Author”], it may return to the Author of its salvation and follow its liberator [Note: [Col. 1126D] “Its own liberator”], after the devil’s stench has been driven away and the sweetest fragrance of the Holy Spirit has been received. Through.

## LXVIII. Another Prayer for a Small Child Who Is Possessed

[Col. 1126B]

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, I implore your power with every groan for this child oppressed by the devil, you who grant protection even to the unworthy amid their afflictions. Rise up for the child who has been defeated, and do not retain vengeance for long. Let not the sins of the parents come before your sight, since you have promised to judge neither the father for the son nor the son for the father. Help, we beseech you, the one afflicted by the fury of the enemy; do not allow his soul to be possessed by the devil without baptism, but rather may this tender age, freed from malignant oppressions, render eternal thanks to you. [Col. 1126C] Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who will come to judge the living and the dead and the age.

## LXIX. Prayer over a Sick Catechumen

Deign to look upon and preserve your servant, Lord, who is turning back to the grace of your baptism, so that, under the sign of your name, whatever the devil was holding in him as liable to punishment through the transgression of original sin may be released by the forgiveness of the sacred font; so that he may lay aside the vigilance of the old man and rise clothed in the garment of new life. [Note: [Col. 1126D] “All things.”] Drive away from him the poisons of every most wicked spirit and fill him with the saving grace of your baptism, so that through receiving your gift he may rejoice in eternal life. [Note: [Col. 1126D] Alternatively, “in everlasting life.”] Through the Lord.

## LXX

[Col. 1126D]

If he is to be baptized, the priest approaches and says a prayer, the Creed, and catechizes him with these words, laying his hand upon his head; then he says this prayer over him: “Let it not be hidden from you, Satan.” As it is written on Saturday.

We humbly beseech you, Lord, that by your holy visitation you may raise this servant of yours toward yourself, lest the adversary be permitted to reach the soul as far as temptation; but, as in the case of Job, set a limit, lest the enemy begin to triumph over the soul of this person without the redemption of baptism. Delay, Lord, the exit of death, and extend the span of life. Raise up him whom you are leading to the sacrament of baptism, lest you bring harm to your redemption. Take away the opportunity for the devil to triumph, and reserve for Christ’s triumphs him whom you associate [Note: [Col. 1127D] Read: “join as a companion.”], so that, restored to health, he may be reborn for you in your Church through the grace of baptism and may do all that we ask. Through.

## LXXI. Likewise, Concerning Making a Catechumen from a Pagan

When you have received a gentile, first catechize him with divine teachings and give him instructions about how he ought to live after learning the truth. After this, make him a catechumen: blow upon his face [Col. 1127B] and make a cross on his forehead; lay your hand upon his head with these words:

Receive the sign of the cross both on your forehead and in your heart; receive the faith of the heavenly commandments; be such in conduct that you may now be able to be a temple of God. Having entered the Church of God, gladly acknowledge that you have escaped the snares of death. Shudder at idols; reject images; worship God the almighty Father and Jesus Christ his Son, who lives with the Father and the Holy Spirit, throughout all ages of ages.

### The Prayer Follows

I beseech you, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, that you command the way of your truth and knowledge to be shown to this servant of yours, who wanders uncertain and doubtful in the night of this age, so that, when the eyes of his heart have been opened, he may recognize you, the one God and Father in the Son, and the Son in the Father with the Holy Spirit, and may deserve to receive the fruit of this confession both in this age and in the age to come. Through.

Then, after he has tasted the medicine of salt and signed himself, you bless him with these words:

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who are, were, [Note: [Col. 1127D] Alternatively, “and”] and remain unto the end, whose origin is unknown and whose end cannot be comprehended, we humbly invoke you, Lord, over this servant of yours, whom you have freed from the error of the gentiles and from a most shameful way of life. Deign to hear him who humbles his neck before you. May he reach the font of the bath, so that, reborn from water and the Holy Spirit, stripped of the old man, he may put on the new, who has been created according to you; may he receive a garment incorrupt and undefiled, and may he deserve to serve you, our Lord. Through the Lord.

## LXXII. Likewise, for Assisting [Note: [Col. 1127D] Read: “a sick catechumen.”] a Sick Catechumen

If he is to be baptized, the priest approaches and says over him the prayers written above; he gives him the Creed and the Prayer; and he catechizes him with these words: “Let it not be hidden from you, Satan.” And the rest, as it is written above for the holy night. Then with the saliva of his mouth he touches his nostrils and ears with his finger and says to him:

[Col. 1128A] “Ephphetha,” which means: “Be opened for the fragrance of sweetness.” But you, devil, flee, for the judgment of God is drawing near.

Then he touches his chest and the space between his shoulders with exorcized oil, using these questions:

Do you renounce Satan?

Response: I renounce him.

And all his works?

Response: I renounce them.

And all his pomps?

Response: I renounce them.

## LXXIII. When the Sick Person Is Undressed, He Blesses the Font. The Prayer Begins

[Col. 1128B]

Hear us, almighty God, and infuse your power into the substance of this water, so that the one to be washed through it may deserve to receive both health and eternal life. Through.

### Another Blessing of Water for Assisting the Sick

I exorcize you, creature of water, by the living God, by the holy God, by God the creator of all sweetness, who in the beginning separated you from the earth by his word and, dividing you into four rivers, commanded you to water the whole earth. I adjure you by Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, that you may become, for the one who is to be baptized in you, a spring of water leaping up into eternal life, regenerating him for God the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. He will come in the Holy Spirit [Col. 1128C] to judge the living and the dead and the whole age by fire.

## LXXIV. Another Prayer for Assisting the Sick

Be present, Lord; be present to your gifts, so that what is to be performed by our ministry may be fulfilled by your assistance. Through the Lord.

### The Blessing Follows

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, sanctifier of spiritual waters, we humbly beseech you to deign to look upon this ministry of our humility and to send over these waters, prepared for washing and giving life to human beings [Note: [Col. 1128D] Alternatively, “over the waters prepared for washing and vivifying those who are to be cleansed”], an angel of holiness, so that, once the sins of the former life have been washed away and guilt removed, he may procure a pure dwelling place for the Holy Spirit in those who are reborn. [Col. 1128D] Through our Lord.

## LXXV. Another Blessing

I exorcize you, creature of water, in the name of God the almighty Father, and in the name of Jesus Christ his Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May every power of the adversary, every attack of the devil, and every phantom be rooted out and driven away from this creature of water, so that it may become a spring [Note: [Col. 1128D] Alternatively, “leaping up.”] of water leaping up into eternal life; and, when he has been baptized [Note: [Col. 1128D] Alternatively, “whoever is baptized in it”], may he become a temple of the living God for the remission of sins. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who will come to judge the living and the age by fire.

[Col. 1129A] And before you pour water over him, you question him on the words of the Creed and say:

Do you believe in God the almighty Father?

Response: I believe.

And do you believe in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, born and having suffered?

Response: I believe.

And do you believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy Church, the remission of sins, and the resurrection of the flesh?

He responds: I believe.

And as you question him, you immerse him three times in the water on each occasion. Then, when the infant has risen from the font, the presbyter signs him on the head with chrism, saying:

Almighty God, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, [Col. 1129B] who regenerated you from water and the Holy Spirit, and who gave you remission of all sins, may he himself anoint you with the chrism of salvation in Christ Jesus unto eternal life.

Response: Amen.

Afterward, if an offering has been made, Masses are to be celebrated and he receives Communion; but if not, you shall give him only the sacraments of the body and blood of Christ, saying:

May the body of our Lord Jesus Christ be for you unto eternal life.

And he gives him the prayer, saying:

Almighty and eternal God, who regenerated your servant from water and the Holy Spirit, and who gave him remission of all sins, grant him [Col. 1129C] continual health so that he may acknowledge the truth of your unity. Through the Lord.

Almighty and merciful God, we humbly beseech your majesty to deign to let your servant appear before you with serene regard [Note: [Col. 1129D] Alternatively, “before your serene eyes”]; and to him to whom you have given the sacrament of baptism, grant lasting health. Through our Lord.

Then he is signed by the bishop with these words:

God, almighty Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who regenerated your servant from water and the Holy Spirit, and who gave him remission of all sins, you, Lord, send upon him your Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, and give him the Spirit of wisdom and understanding; the Spirit of counsel and fortitude; [Col. 1129D] the Spirit of knowledge and piety. Fill him with the Spirit of fear of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and command him to be signed with the sign of the cross unto eternal life. Through the same Lord Jesus Christ, with whom you live and reign in the unity of the Holy Spirit.

Afterward he signs him on the forehead with chrism, saying:

The sign of Christ unto eternal life.

Response: Amen.

Peace be with you.

Response: And with your spirit.

## LXXVI. For Assisting the Sick: Blessing of Exorcized Oil

[Col. 1130A]

I exorcize you, creature of oil, by almighty God, who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them. May every power of the adversary, every army of the devil, every attack, and every phantom of Satan be rooted out and driven away from this creature of oil, so that it may become, for all who are to be anointed with it, a means of adoption as children through the Holy Spirit, in the name of God the almighty Father and in the love of Jesus Christ our Lord, who will come in the Holy Spirit to judge the living and the dead and the age by fire.

God, glory of the faithful and [Note: [Col. 1130D] Alternatively, “life”] life of the righteous, who also instructed us through Moses your servant by the melody of a sacred song, work the gift of your mercy among all nations, granting blessedness and removing terror, so that what was foretold as punishment may be transformed into an eternal remedy. Almighty and eternal God, who through your only Son showed that you are the cultivator of your Church [Note: [Col. 1130D] “So that” is redundant … “cultivator” should be understood. Through.

[Col. 1131A] Lord God of hosts, who restore fallen things and preserve what has been restored, increase the peoples who are to be renewed in the sanctification of your name, so that all who are washed in sacred baptism may always be directed by your inspiration. Through.

God, who always multiply your Church through new offspring, grant your servants to hold fast by their lives to your sacrament, which they received by faith. Through.

Through Christ our Lord. Who, ascending above all the heavens and sitting at your right hand, poured out the promised Holy Spirit upon the children of adoption. Therefore, rejoicing among your altars, Lord of hosts, we offer you sacrifices of praise through Christ the Lord. Whom the angels praise.

Sharing in communion and anticipating the most sacred day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit filled the apostles and the people of believers with the presence of his majesty. And also commemorating.

## LXXX. PRAYERS AND PETITIONS FOR THE LORD’S DAY OF PENTECOST

Almighty and eternal God, who willed the Paschal sacrament to be contained within the mystery of fifty days, grant that the dispersion of the nations through the division of languages may be gathered together by a heavenly gift into one confession of your name [Note: Col. 1132D: The Ambrosian Mass in Pamelius reads: “may be gathered together.”]. Through him.

God, who by the sacrament of today’s feast sanctify your whole Church among every people and nation, pour out the gifts of your Holy Spirit over the entire breadth of the world, so that what divine condescension accomplished at the very beginnings of the preaching of the Gospel may now also be spread through the hearts of believers.

### Secret

We ask, Lord, that the Holy Spirit prepare our minds for the divine sacraments, for he himself is the forgiveness of all sins. Through our Lord.

May the offering of the present gift purify us, we ask, Lord, and make us worthy to participate in the sacred mysteries. Through the Lord.

For today we celebrate the coming of the Holy Spirit. He who, at the beginnings of the Church’s birth, imbued all nations with instruction, bestowed both knowledge of the Godhead and speech; wonderful in producing unity amid the diversity of gifts, he is likewise the one and same giver and author of various graces, and himself the distributor of the languages of those who preach. Whom the angels praise.

[Column 1132D] Within the Canon.

Communicating with the saints and celebrating the most holy day of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit filled the apostles and the people of believers with the presence of his majesty. And also commemorating.

This offering, therefore. You say it as on the holy night.

### After Communion

May our vices be cleansed by the heavenly mysteries, Lord, so that we may always be made fit for your gifts. Through him.

### For the People

Grant, we ask, Lord, that the Holy Spirit remove carnal desires from our minds and powerfully pour spiritual gifts into us. Through our Lord.

Be present, Lord, we ask, with your people, and defend from the attack of enemies those whom you have satisfied with the heavenly mysteries. Through the Lord.

## LXXXI. OTHER PRAYERS FOR VESPERS DURING THE OCTAVE OF PENTECOST

God, who deigned to send the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, to your disciples in the fervor of the fire of your love [Note: The Ambrosian Mass in Pamelius reads: “in the fiery manifestation of the fervor of your love”; Pamelius judges that the word “manifestation” should be added.], grant your peoples to be fervent in the unity of faith, so that, always remaining in you [Note: In the same Mass: “always remaining in love.”], they may be found steadfast in faith and effective in action. Through him.

Almighty and eternal God, lead us to fellowship with the joys of heaven, so that, having been reborn by the Holy Spirit, you may make us enter your kingdom, and that the humility of the flock may reach the place where the exalted Shepherd has gone before [Note: In the margin: “or, to it.”]. Through him.

May the power of the Holy Spirit be with us, we ask, Lord, who may mercifully cleanse our hearts and protect us from every adversity [Note: In Pamelius, on Tuesday of Pentecost week: “which.”]. Through the Lord.

May the Spirit, the Paraclete, who proceeds from you, enlighten our minds, Lord, and lead them into all truth, as your Son promised. Through him.

May the infusion of the Holy Spirit cleanse our hearts, Lord, and make them fruitful through the abundance of his dew. Through our Lord.

Grant us, merciful God, that just as we understand the truth of the divine nature in the name of the Father and the Son [Note: In the same author: “in the name.”], so in the Holy Spirit we may recognize the substance of the entire Trinity. Through him.

## LXXXII. ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE FASTS

Of the fourth, seventh, and tenth months.

Dearest brothers, the restored observance of that month reminds us of the annual purity of fasting, by which holiness is acquired both for the body and for the soul. Therefore, assembling on Wednesday and Friday with an earnest gathering [Note: Read: “earnestly.”], let us offer spiritual fasting to God; but on Saturday, at blessed Peter’s, whose intercessions we believe will aid us, let us celebrate the holy vigils with Christian devotion. Thus, through this saving institution, may we wash away by fasts and almsgiving the stains of sins that we contract through the frailty of the body, with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns as God, forever and ever.

### Another Form

The fasts of that month are to be observed by us in this week; therefore we exhort your holy faith to fast on Wednesday, Friday, or Saturday, so that, adhering to the divine commandments, we may obtain the favor of our God through the perseverance of devoted service [Note: Read: “of due service.”]. Through him.

## LXXXIII. PRAYERS AND PETITIONS BEGIN

Of the fourth month.

### Wednesday

Grant us, Lord, to begin the defenses of Christian warfare with holy fasts, so that, about to fight against spiritual wickedness [Note: We have corrected the exemplar, which reads: “to fight.”], we may be fortified by the aids of self-restraint. Through him.

Almighty and merciful God, graciously make us suited to your will, for just as, while passing along its path, we go astray, so may we be guided along an unbroken course [Note: Read: “land”; but this is incorrect.—Corrected from Menardus], always returning to its order. Through him.

Give us, Lord, a mind that is pleasing to you, because you will continually supply whatever is prosperous to such people. Through him.

### Secret

May this sacred gift, after we have been purified by solemn fasts, make us, Lord, fitting for its mystery [Note: Menardus: “your”; the exemplar reads “sacred gift” (sacro munus), while Menardus has “by a sacred gift” (sacro munere)], because it will be more beneficial to us the more devoutly we receive it [Note: Menardus: “you will be present” (aderis)]. Through him.

For after those days of rejoicing which we spent in honor of the Lord rising from the dead and ascending into heaven [Note: The exemplar and Menardus write: “in honor.”], after [Note: Or: “and after” (postque).] the gift of the Holy Spirit had been received, holy fasts were necessarily provided for us [Note: “For” is redundant.], so that, as we live in pure conduct, the things divinely bestowed upon the Church may remain. Through Christ our Lord.

### After Communion

May your sacraments give life, Lord, to those whom prescribed fasts discipline, so that, with earthly desires quieted, we may more easily grasp heavenly things. Through him.

### For the People

May your Church always give thanks to you, Lord, with a submissive heart, and consequently obtain what it seeks; and, continually reviewing ancient observances, may it advance into the future. Through him.

### Friday

To grant us abundance of earthly fruits, Lord, make our minds fruitful with heavenly fertility. Through him.

May your grace, Lord, make fruitful the affection of our devotion [Note: We have corrected the exemplar, which mistakenly reads “Let them be” (Fiant) and “more fruitfully” (fructuosius)], for our fasts will benefit us in practice [Note: Elsewhere: “then”] if they are pleasing to your mercy. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Almighty and eternal God, who are not appeased by the ambition of sacrifices but regard the zeal of pious devotion, give your household a right spirit and a pure heart, so that their faith may commend these gifts to you and their humility may make the offerings acceptable. Through him.

### After Communion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, recalling the actions of your sacraments, we may be relieved by temporal security and instructed by legal ordinances. Through him.

### For the People

Graciously bestow your mercy, Lord, upon the faithful people, and grant abundant bodily defenses to those who beseech you. Through him.

### Saturday at the Twelve Lessons

Grant, Lord, we ask, that your servants may be such, and by the abundance of your grace make us such, that we may confidently seek your good things [Note: In Menardus: “obtain them.”] and receive them without difficulty. Through him.

Give us, Lord, we ask, always to seek your kingdom and righteousness, so that you may mercifully cause to abound for those whom you see to be in need. Through him.

God, who willed us to be concerned about present helps, grant, we ask, that, by pursuing with devotion the things that are yours, all things salutary may be granted to us [Note: In the margin: “or, devoutly”; in Menardus: “to those who devoutly pursue them.”]. Through him.

God, who in your mercy go before those who do not ask, give us the disposition continually to implore your majesty, so that in perpetual goodness you may defend suppliants with better things. Through him.

God, who do not despise the contrite in heart and those afflicted by miseries, hear favorably your people crying out to you in the devotion of fasting [Note: In the same author: “favorably”], so that the prosperity of your restoration may raise up those whom adversity has humbled. Through him.

### Also after the Blessing

God, whose power of majesty is to be adored [Note: Read: “power.”], by which the blaze of a raging flame was transformed into splendor for the three holy youths, be present to your Church’s souls with similar remedies [Note: Read: “souls.”], so that your people, rescued from the more grievous adversities of this world by heavenly favor, may rejoice. Through him.

### Secret

Our Lord God, who, among those creatures that you created as a protection for our frailty, also commanded gifts to be established and dedicated in your name [Note: Menardus reads: “you commanded gifts to be dedicated to your name”], grant, we ask, that they may become for us both a help in the present life and a sacrament of eternity. Through him.

We ask you to sanctify the fast that you have taught us to observe for the edification of souls and the chastisement of bodies, because when bodies are restrained, souls are nourished; in what the outer person is afflicted, the inner person is enlarged [Note: Or: “and in it.”]. Remember, Lord, our fasting and your mercies, which you have always graciously bestowed upon sinners who fast, so that, abstaining not only from food but from every sin, we may please you by the fast of devotion. And therefore with the angels.

### After Communion

May the venerable sacrament we have received, we ask, Lord, nourish us with the supports both of the present life and of the eternal one. Through him.

### For the People

May your people dedicated to you advance, Lord, we ask, in the affection of pious devotion, so that, instructed by sacred acts, the more pleasing it becomes to your majesty, the more it may be increased by greater gifts. Through him.

## LXXXIV. PRAYERS AND PETITIONS ON THE SUNDAY OF THE OCTAVE OF PENTECOST

Savior and Guardian of those who fear you, Lord, turn away from your Church the deceptive allurements of worldly wisdom [Note: Pamelius reads more suitably: “the deceit.”], so that, instructed by your Spirit, we may be delighted rather by the form established by the prophets and apostles than by philosophical words, lest the vanity of falsehoods deceive those whom the instruction of truth enlightens. Through him.

Graciously pour your Holy Spirit into our understanding, Lord, so that we may always be devoted to you, by whose wisdom we were created and by whose providence we are governed. Through him.

Almighty and merciful God, to whose eternal blessedness one ascends not by the frailty of the flesh but by eagerness of mind, make us always aspire to the courts of the heavenly city by your inspiration, and by your indulgence faithfully enter them. Through him.

### Secret

With the shadows of carnal victims removed, we bring you, supreme Father, in humble service a spiritual offering, which by a wondrous and ineffable mystery is always sacrificed and always offered, and which is equally both the gift of the devout and the reward of the one who rewards [Note: The same author more correctly has: “wondrous and ineffable.”]. Through him.

You are one God and one Lord with your Only-begotten Son and the Holy Spirit—not in the singularity of one person, but in the Trinity of one substance [Note: We have corrected this from the same source; the exemplar mistakenly reads: “of the Trinity.”]. For whatever we believe concerning your glory because you have revealed it, we also understand concerning your Son and concerning the Holy Spirit, without distinction [Note: Read: “without discrimination.”]. Thus, in the confession of the true and eternal Godhead, let the distinctness of the persons, the unity of the essence, and equality in majesty be adored. Whom the angels praise.

### After Communion

May the venerable solemnity of the sacrament make us glad, we ask, Lord; and may it likewise make our minds and bodies fruitful through spiritual sanctification and always exercise them in chaste joys. Through him.

### For the People

May your Church, Lord, be filled and grow with heavenly grace; and, purified from every vice, may it receive the increase of eternal redemption, so that what it venerates in its members through the abundant prolongation of time [Note: Read: “by abundant prerogative.”] it may receive through the spiritual abundance of gifts. Through our Lord.

## LXXXV. BLESSING OVER THOSE WHO RETURN FROM THE ARIAN TO THE CATHOLIC UNITY

Lord God almighty, Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who have deigned to rescue your servants, men and women, from the error and falsehood of the Arian heresy and to lead them to your Catholic Church, send upon them, Lord, the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and fortitude, the Spirit of knowledge and piety; and fill them, Lord, with the Spirit of the fear of God, in the name of Jesus Christ our God and Savior. Through him, and with him, is honor and glory to you forever and ever. Amen.

## LXXXVI. ANOTHER PRAYER FOR THOSE WHO COME FROM VARIOUS HERESIES

Holy Father, almighty God, who have deigned to rescue your servant from the error of heresies [Note: Read: “of heretics”] and recall him to the holy Catholic Church, we ask you, Lord, send into him your Holy Spirit, the sevenfold Paraclete: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and fortitude, of knowledge and piety; fill your servant with the Spirit of the fear of God. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## LXXXVII. RECONCILIATION OF ONE REBAPTIZED BY HERETICS

Almighty Father of mercies and God of consolation, who through your Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, so consecrated the mystery of human regeneration that, even among those who through the deceit of diabolical wickedness depart from the unity of baptism, there can be no repetition [Note: “To be rescinded, or to be reviewed.”], because, when sacred law is doubled [Note: “It is doubled.”], the power of the consecration once imparted is not excluded, but an injury is inflicted upon the faith while the sacraments remain; therefore, when apostates, having come to their senses through the inspiration of your gift, return to the true mother, the Catholic Church, they do not receive again baptism as though they had lost it, but are restored by the satisfaction of true repentance for the insult they committed against what remains in them.

For this reason we humbly implore your mercy, holy Father, that you graciously receive this servant of yours, returning to your holy courts which he had abandoned, with immense kindness, and save him by the most devout favor; so that he who now condemns Arius for his own fall [Note: “By anathematizing him.”], may, with continual lamentation, worthily bring forth the fruits of repentance [Note: It seems that “worthy” should be read]. By your regard, satisfaction took its beginning; by your gift, may he now recognize himself as having returned from the distance of his destruction. For one departs farther from you through denial of the faith once bestowed than through wickedness of deeds [Note: “From you.”]. Therefore, we ask that, according to the multitude of your mercies, the monstrous impiety of your suppliant may be forgiven, and that your majesty may deign to call back the one who has strayed farther from the path of eternal salvation.

And although we are shown to be unworthy in carrying out your mysteries, we are nevertheless utterly confident in your mercy. For this reason we do not dare to close the door of reconciliation to one who returns and knocks, since we trust that you have revealed to him the eyes of his heart so that he might return. And although we set temporal limits upon the act of repentance [Note: Read: “upon the action”], nevertheless, because we know neither the day of death nor the quality of the heart, we admit him to the hope of reconciliation in such a way that he does not abandon the disposition of continual penitence, but, renewed through perpetual fear and continuous lamentation, may merit to remain perpetually in communion with the heavenly sacraments. Through him.

### Another, for a Younger Person [Note: In the margin: “instead of.”]

God, who restore the human being created in your image to what you created, look favorably upon this servant of yours, and forgive by the indulgence of your goodness whatever the depravity of heresy has introduced through his ignorance, so that what was committed in him through the devil’s deceit and harmed him through the wickedness of Arian faithlessness may not be counted against him as guilt, but that he may be restored as a member of the Catholic Church by the mercy of your forgiveness, so that he may be returned to the sacred altars, having received communion in your truth [Note: “And.”]. Through him.

### Another, for a Younger Person

God, creator and redeemer of the human race, God who, according to the riches of your goodness, restore the work fashioned in the likeness and image of you to what you created, look favorably upon this servant of yours, so that you may forgive whatever the necessity of hostile ignorance has poured into him [Note: Read: “and whatever.”] through the indulgence of your goodness; so that, in one who as yet does not possess sound understanding, nothing may be counted as guilt, but he may be reckoned, through the kindness of your forgiveness, a member of the Church. Through him.

## LXXXVIII. PRAYER AT THE DEDICATION OF A NEW BASILICA

God, who sanctify places dedicated to your name, pour out your grace upon this house of prayer, so that all who invoke you here may experience the help of your mercy. Through him.

### Consecration of the Basilica

Almighty ruler, God of sanctifications, whose goodness is felt without end; God who embrace both heavenly and earthly things, preserving your mercy for your people who walk before the sight of your glory: hear the prayers of your servants, so that your eyes may be open over this house day and night. In your clemency, dedicate this basilica, established in honor of that holy person [Note: The name is left as a placeholder in the source], through the sacred mysteries; in your mercy, enlighten it; glorify it by your own splendor. Graciously admit every person who comes to worship in this place; deign to look upon them favorably. For the sake of your great name, your strong hand, and your outstretched arm, willingly protect those who supplicate you in this dwelling, graciously hear them, and preserve them by eternal defense, so that they may always be happy and, always rejoicing in your worship, steadfastly persevere in the Catholic faith of the Holy Trinity. Through him.

### Prayer over Water and Wine for the Consecration of an Altar

Creator and preserver of the human race, giver of spiritual grace, bestower of eternal salvation, permit [Note: Or: “send.” Menardus reads “permit”] your Spirit to come upon the wine mixed with water, so that it may furnish arms [Note: Pamelius’s text: “armed”] with the power of heavenly defense for the consecration of this church or altar [Note: Read: “may advance”; Menardus reads: “may advance,” plural]. Through him.

The preface of the consecration of the altar follows.

First you place wine mixed with water upon the horn of the altar with your finger, and sprinkle the altar seven times; then pour the remainder at the base, and offer incense upon the altar as a most sweet fragrance to the Lord.

### Blessing of the Altar [Note: “Preface of the consecration.”]

Dearest brothers, let us implore the mercy of God the almighty Father, so that he may sanctify this altar, which is to be consecrated for spiritual sacrifices, with the present blessing sought through the service of our voice [Note: Or: “so that he may always bless the offerings of your servants placed upon it.”], and may deign to bless and sanctify the offerings placed there through the zeal of their devotion; and, appeased by spiritual incense, may he stand ready as a willing hearer of his beseeching household. Through him.

### Blessing, or Consecration, of the Altar

Almighty God, in whose honor we consecrate this altar under the invocation of your name [Note: Menardus: “we consecrate this altar, unworthy, to your name.”], mercifully and graciously hear the prayers of our humility, and grant that upon this table libations may be acceptable, pleasing, and rich to you, and always drenched with the dew of your Holy Spirit, so that at every time and in this place you may relieve the distresses of your household supplicating you [Note: In the margin: “or, anxieties.”], heal sicknesses, hear prayers, receive vows, confirm desires, and grant requests. Through him.

### Preface of the Altar Cloths

Lord God almighty, just as from the beginning you created for human beings things vital and necessary [Note: Menardus: “useful”], and just as you created priestly vestments for priests and ornaments for Levites—which Mary wove and made for use in the ministry of the tabernacle of the covenant—deign to sanctify, bless, and consecrate these linens for use on your altar, to cover and wrap the body and blood of your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, who with you lives and reigns as God [Note: Or: “which you decreed should be made.”].

### For Consecrating the Paten

We consecrate and sanctify this paten for making upon it the body of our Lord Jesus Christ, who suffered the cross for the salvation of us all. He who with the Father and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns as God forever and ever [Note: The second “who” is redundant].

Then make the sign of the cross with holy oil over the paten and say this prayer:

Deign, Lord, to consecrate and sanctify this paten through this anointing and our blessing, in Christ Jesus our Lord. He lives and reigns [Note: Menardus: “Who lives, etc.”].

### For Blessing the Chalice

Dearest brothers, let us pray that the Lord our God may sanctify his chalice, consecrated for service, through the inspiration of heavenly grace, and adapt it, by divine favor, to the fullness of blessing for humankind [Note: In him we read: “the chalice to be consecrated for use in his ministry.”]. Through the Lord.

### Another

Deign, Lord, to pour into this chalice, fashioned for use in your ministry through the pious devotion of your servant, that sanctification with which you bestowed the sacramental chalice upon your servant Melchizedek [Note: Or: “the consecrated chalice.”], and may what cannot be made worthy of your altars by craftsmanship or metal become precious through your blessing [Note: Thus we have corrected it; the exemplar incorrectly reads: “of office.”]. Through him.

### Another Blessing for All Things Used in the Basilica

Deign, Lord God almighty, King of kings and Lord of lords, Priest of all and High Priest of all, through whom all things were made together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, Christ Jesus, to bless, consecrate, and sanctify these vessels together with this altar, the linens, and the remaining vessels. Just as you once sanctified the services of the tabernacle of testimony with the ark, the oracle, the winged cherubim, curtains, columns, lampstands, altar [Note: Read: “lampstands, altar”;], silver bases, gilded boards, holocausts, victims, bronze altar, bronze vessels [Note: Read: “bronze vessels”;], tents, ropes, oil of anointing, and all the rest, in figure of us, through the hands of holy priests, so now, remaining forever as the supreme High Priest of priests according to the order of Melchizedek, as we have said, we beseech you from our heart to bless, purify, consecrate, and bring to completion this paten, this chalice, and all the instruments of this church or basilica altar, which are held among our hands; through these things, we believe, our unity with the eternal unity is established without end at the supreme passage [Note: “This is read almost in this form in the Roman Order: ‘through which among us, etc.’”]. Through him.

### Preface of the Chrism

Dearest brothers, let us pray that almighty God may deign, as we pray, to fill this instrument bearing the body of his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, with blessing, the protection of sanctification, and the gift of defense. Through the Lord.

### Another

Inseparable Trinity, pour the help of your blessing into our hands, so that through our blessing this little vessel may be sanctified and become, by the grace of the Holy Spirit, a new tomb of Christ’s body. Through the Lord.

## LXXXIX. PRAYERS AND PETITIONS FOR MASSES AT THE DEDICATION OF A NEW BASILICA

God, who are the author of the gifts to be consecrated to you, graciously deign to be present for the sanctification of this place, so that those who have built these things in honor of your name may merit to have you as their protector in all things. Through him.

Magnify yourself, Lord our God, in your holy ones, and appear in this temple of edification, so that you, who work all things in adopted children, may always be praised in your inheritance. Through him.

### Secret

Almighty and eternal God, who have established the different kinds of flock-offerings in the perfection of this one sacrifice, look favorably from the throne of your glory and pour out the gift of your blessing upon this altar, so that temporal sacrifices may be consecrated upon it in such a way that they may provide the substance of eternal life for those who receive them. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Although you are wholly present everywhere and contain all things in your entire majesty, you nevertheless willed places suited to your mysteries to be consecrated to you, so that the houses of prayer themselves might stir the minds of suppliants to invoke your name. Pour out your grace upon this place, and show the gift of your help to all who hope in you, so that here both the power of the sacraments and the fulfillment of vows may be obtained. Through him.

### Within the Canon

We ask you, Lord, graciously to accept this offering of your servant, this man or woman, which they offer to you while dedicating this church, and graciously hear our prayers, so that your eyes may be open over this house day and night. In your clemency, dedicate this temple, established through sacred mysteries in honor of your blessed martyrs, those men or those holy women, and confessors [Note: The names are left as placeholders in the source]; in your mercy, enlighten it; graciously glorify it by your splendor. Kindly hear your whole household gathering for the assistance of this court, and piously fulfill all the desires of the hearts of its founders that are pleasing to you, and answer their vows. Increase their years of life and the happiness of their times, so that, living through long periods, this place may shine with better adornments through their zeal; and our days—

### After Communion

May the Christian people obtain abundant benefits, we ask, Lord, so that one who receives the present lights at the thresholds being consecrated to you in the fragrance of the saints [Note: Menardus more correctly has: “in honor”; alternatively, and likewise in Menardus: “the devout person comes, and the supports of life.” Read: “lights” (luminibus)] may also find the grace of eternal redemption. Through [Note: Delete: “the Lord.”] the Lord.

## XC. ANOTHER MASS

God, who are the author of the gifts to be consecrated to you, pour your blessing upon this house of prayer, so that all who invoke your name may experience the help of your defense. Through the Lord.

God, who build for yourself an eternal dwelling from the fitting-together of all the saints, grant heavenly growth to your building [Note: Menardus: “so that”], and may we always be helped by the merits of those whose relics we piously embrace here. Through him.

### Secret

Almighty and eternal God, pour your grace upon this place and show the gift of your help to all who invoke you, so that here the power of all the sacraments may strengthen the hearts of all the faithful. Through our Lord.

Through Christ our Lord. Through him we humbly beseech you to sanctify this altar, prepared for holy uses, with heavenly dedication; and just as you received with wondrous condescension the offering of the chief priest Melchizedek, so may you deign always to accept the gifts placed upon this new altar [Note: Menardus: “always accepted.”], so that your people, gathering in this holy house of the Church, may be saved through these pure libations by heavenly sanctification and also attain the perpetual salvation of their souls. Through him your majesty.

### Within the Canon

We ask you, Lord, graciously to regard this offering of your servant, this man or woman, which they offer to you to be sacrificed for the sanctification of this temple [Note: Read: “which cannot equal.”], so that your countenance of glory may enlighten the court that cannot equal the merits of your blessed martyr, and so that by your favor it may become worthy of your sacred and holy mysteries. Thus, a temporal dwelling of eternal light. May no worldly filth or darkness possess anything here, so that your people, coming here, may obtain the effect of their prayer and recognize this place as worthy of your majesty, while they receive from you what they have requested; and may it be counted to those who build it as the price of their sins, since it is received by you not according to the quantity of their work but according to the devotion of those offering it; and our days—

### After Communion

Trusting in the prayers of your saints, we ask, Lord, that through what we have received we may attain eternal remedies. Through him.

## XCI. PRAYERS AND PETITIONS AT THE DEDICATION OF A BASILICA THAT ITS FOUNDER LEFT UNDEDICATED

God, who sanctify places dedicated to your name and go before with your blessings those that are to be dedicated, grant, we ask, that what your servant, this man, assigned in this building to your blessed apostle, this man, and to those holy martyrs [Note: The names are left as placeholders in the source], may be prepared with suitable service. Through him.

We ask, Lord, that your holy one, this man, as intercessor, may entreat your omnipotence, so that by his merits you may mercifully enlighten this church assigned to him, since whatever honor is bestowed upon the saints concerns the insignia of your majesty. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Grant, we ask, Lord, that just as your servant, this man, desired through the gifts offered, so the merits of your blessed martyrs, those men, may always be celebrated here. Through him.

You grant your faithful to fulfill what, under your inspiration, they have vowed [Note: We corrected the exemplar, which mistakenly reads: “and to you.”]. Therefore, anticipating with pious service the dedication of this basilica, which your servant, this man, instituted to offer to your blessed apostle, that man, and to your holy martyrs, those men, we offer worthy praises to your majesty. Through him your majesty.

### After Communion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, satisfied with the divine gift, your devoted people may venerate your glory, just as your servant, this man, assigned it for the repose of his soul, for the repose of this completion, and for the glory of your blessed apostle, that man, and of those holy martyrs. Through him.

## XCII. At the Services for the Same Founder

God, receiver of the souls of the faithful, grant, we ask, that your servant, this man, may rest in perpetual light and obtain what he desired concerning this place. Through our Lord.

### Secret

For the soul of your servant, this man, we humbly implore you, Lord, with sacrifice, so that you may graciously fulfill his vows in order to confer your perpetual mercy. Through him.

### Within the Canon

We ask you, Lord, graciously to regard this offering, which we offer to you for the soul of your servant, this man, and fulfill what he promised in Christian faith in these places, so that he may obtain the fruit of good works; and our days—

### After Communion

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the soul of your servant, this man, may receive a full reward from the completion of this Church. Through our Lord.

## XCIII. PRAYERS AND PETITIONS AT THE DEDICATION OF THE PLACE WHERE A SYNAGOGUE PREVIOUSLY STOOD

God, who arrange all things without any mutability of time and lead toward improvement the things you choose to be changed [Note: Read: “to better things,” or “to things to be improved.”], look upon this basilica dedicated to your name in honor of that blessed person [Note: The name is left as a placeholder in the source], so that, once the antiquity of Jewish error has been expelled, you may grant this place the truth of the Church through the newness of the Holy Spirit. Through our Lord.

Almighty and eternal God, who, after the foulness of Jewish superstition had been wiped away, have deigned to adorn this place with the beauty of your Church in honor of that blessed person [Note: “To adorn. Through him.” Something is missing for the sentence to be complete.]. Through our Lord.

Grant, we ask, Lord, that the faith which, raised up by the sign of the cross, subdued death and brought us salvation and triumph may shine here. Through him.

### Secret
God, the life of believers and the source of virtues, we beseech you: fill this temple with the glory of your majesty, so that, dedicated in honor of blessed N., it may become a house of prayer, which had previously been a place of hiding; and because an opposing throng of unbelievers used to assemble in this place, may your people always deserve to find you here favorably disposed through their offerings. Through [our Lord].

[Col. 1144C] Postcommunion.

We give you thanks, Lord, having been strengthened by the sacred gift, and we beseech your mercy that you may make us worthy of its participation. Through.

For the people.

May spiritual wickedness be driven away from your people, we beseech you, Lord, and may the malignity of the aerial powers depart. Through the Lord.

## XCIV. PRAYERS AND PETITIONS: At the dedication of a baptistery

Almighty and everlasting God, sanctify this baptistery, dedicated by a heavenly visitation, through the illumination of your Spirit, so that all whom this font will wash, cleansed by a threefold washing, may by your gift obtain the forgiveness of all their sins. Through.

Almighty and everlasting God, fountain of all virtues and fullness of graces, deign to consecrate this sacred baptism, prepared by the presence of your majesty, so that although you are wholly present everywhere, we may also feel you present here in our prayers. Through.

### Secret

Receive, we beseech you, Lord, our prayers together with the offerings of those who implore you, and mercifully grant that whatever new thing they receive here for rebirth through the Holy Spirit may by your grace become eternal. Through.

[Col. 1145A] Through Christ our Lord. Through him the dawn of rebirth has risen for us, so that although we came into this world mortal through carnal origin, we might be reborn from water and the Holy Spirit to the hope of eternal life. In order that the sacrament of your loving-kindness, Lord, may be celebrated in this place with the full power of your grace, we humbly offer you this sacrifice of praise, beseeching your mercy that you grant the power of your Spirit to preside continually over this font. Through its operation, may all who descend into these waters, cleansed from the contagion of every crime and purified by perpetual sanctification, deserve to be inscribed in the book of blessed life. Through.

### Within the Canon

[Col. 1145B] Therefore, we beseech you, Lord, mercifully accept this offering which we offer to you at the consecration of this baptistery, and in your goodness grant that all whom this font will wash may be cleansed by the abolition of every crime; and bestow upon your servants, its founders, the reward of so great a work according to the promised recompense. This offering, O God, ...

### Postcommunion

Multiply your blessing, Lord, and strengthen our faith through the Spirit of your gift, so that you may command that those who descend into these waters be inscribed in the book of life, to be handed over to you, God the Father, in the resurrection, in your kingdom. Through.

### For the people

[Col. 1145C] Be favorable, Lord, to your household; graciously sanctify the vows of our humility; and preserve, through universal adoption, all who are to be reborn in this font. Through.

## XCV. HERE BEGINS THE ORDER: On blessing those who are to receive the sacred orders

The following periods are to be observed for each rank. If from childhood he has attached himself to ecclesiastical ministers [Note: In the Roman Order it is written: “ministries.”], let him remain continuously among the readers until his twentieth year. If he has entered at a more advanced age, but nevertheless desires after baptism to devote himself to the service of God [Note: The same Order reads: “immediately himself.”], let him be retained either among the readers or among the exorcists for five years; thereafter let him serve as acolyte or subdeacon for four years, and then, if he is worthy, let him approach the blessing of the diaconate. In that order he must remain for five years, if he has conducted himself blamelessly; by merits that support him and by the stipends given through all these ranks, after providing proofs of his own faith, he may merit the priesthood. If from that position a more exacting life has led him to good morals, he ought to hope for the supreme pontificate. This rule, however, must be observed: neither a bigamist nor a penitent may be admitted to these ranks. [Col. 1146A] Certainly, even defenders of the Church who come from the laity must be held to the foregoing observance if they merit being in the clerical order.

When a bishop is ordained, two bishops shall place and hold the Book of the Gospels over his head; and while one pours the blessing over him, all the other bishops who are present shall touch his head with their hands.

When a priest is ordained, while the bishop blesses him, all the priests who are present also [shall do so]. [Note: Menardus: “While the bishop blesses him and holds his hand over his head, also ...”] [Note: In the same author is added: “let them hold their hands over his head beside the bishop’s hand.”]

When a deacon is ordained, only the bishop who blesses him shall place his hand upon his head; but the other priests shall place their hands upon his head beside the bishop’s hand, because he is consecrated not to the priesthood but to the ministry.

[Col. 1146B] When a subdeacon is ordained, because he does not receive the imposition of hands, let him receive from the bishop’s hand an empty paten and an empty chalice; from the archdeacon’s hand, however, let him receive a water jug, a basin, and, perhaps, a towel. [Note: Perhaps: “with.”] [Note: Read: “who places his hand.”]

When an acolyte is ordained, he is indeed to be instructed by the bishop how he ought to conduct himself in his office; but from the archdeacon let him receive a candlestick with a candle, so that he may know that he is being assigned to light the lamps of the church; let him also receive an empty water jug for supplying wine at the Eucharist of the body of Christ. [Note: Menardus: “in his office.”]

When an exorcist is ordained, let him receive from the bishop’s hand a booklet in which the exorcisms are written, while the bishop says to him:

“Receive this, commit it to memory, and have the power to place your hand upon a possessed person, whether baptized or a catechumen.” [Note: “By heart.”]

When a reader is ordained, the bishop shall speak of him to the people, indicating his faith and ability. After this, in the presence of the people, let him hand him the Book from which he is to read, saying to him:

“Receive this and be a herald of the word of God; if you faithfully and usefully fulfill your office, you shall have a share with those who have ministered the word of God.” [Note: Thus we have corrected the text from Menardus. The Exemplary incorrectly reads: “who will inhabit.”]

When a doorkeeper is ordained, after he has been instructed by the archdeacon how he ought to conduct himself in the house of God, the bishop, at the archdeacon’s direction, shall hand him the keys of the church from the altar, saying to him:

“Act as one who must render an account to God for these things, and for whatever is locked away with these keys.” [Note: Menardus: “which.”]

A psalmist, that is, a cantor, may undertake the office of singing without the bishop’s knowledge, solely at the command of a priest, the priest saying to him:

“See that what you sing with your mouth, you believe in your heart; and what you believe in your heart, prove by your works.”

When a consecrated virgin is presented to her bishop for her consecration, she is to be brought in such garments as she will always wear, suitable to her profession and religious life. [Note: Read: “to her bishop for her consecration.”]

## XCVI. Likewise, blessings over those who are to be blessed in the sacred orders

### Preface of the doorkeeper

[Col. 1147A]

Let us humbly beseech God the almighty Father to deign to bless this servant of his, N., whom he has deigned to choose for the office of doorkeeper, so that he may have most faithful care by day and by night, at the appointed hours, for invoking the name of the Lord. Through the Lord. [Note: Read: “we beseech.”]

### Blessing of the same

Holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, deign to bless this servant of yours, N., the doorkeeper, so that he may render dutiful service among the doorkeepers of the church and deserve to have a share of the reward among your elect. Through.

### Preface of the reader

Your brothers choose you to be a reader in the house of your God, so that you may recognize your office and fulfill it; for God is powerful enough to increase his grace in you. Through.

### Blessing of the reader

Holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, deign to bless your servant, N., in the office of reader, so that, distinguished and adorned by the assiduity of his readings, he may resound in the church with harmonious measures of spiritual devotion. Through the Lord. [Note: In Menardus and in the Frankish Missal: “ordered.”] [Note: In the Frankish Missal: “may it resound.”]

### Preface of the exorcist

Let us humbly beseech God the almighty Father to deign to bless this servant of his, N., for the office of exorcist, so that he may be a spiritual commander for driving demons out of possessed bodies together with all their manifold wickedness. Through.

### Blessing of the exorcist

Holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, deign to bless this servant of yours, N., as an exorcist, so that through the laying on of hands and through the ministry of his mouth you may deign to choose him for this office, and so that he may have power to restrain unclean spirits and may be a proven physician of your Church, strengthened by the power of the grace of healings. Through the Lord. [Note: Read: “as an exorcist.”] [Note: “The laying on.”] [Note: Menardus reads: “and for the laying on of hands and the ministry of his mouth.”] [Note: The same: “so that he may have authority.”] [Note: In the same author: “to be restrained.”]

### Preface for the ordination of a subdeacon

Let us pray to God our Lord that over his servant, N., whom he has deigned to call to the office of subdeacon, he may pour out his blessing and his grace, so that, faithfully serving in his sight, he may obtain the rewards appointed for the saints. Through. [Note: Menardus: “to call.”] [Note: Corrected from the same source.]

### Blessing of the subdeacon

Holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, deign to bless this servant of yours, N., whom you have deigned to choose for the office of subdeacon, so that you may train him in your holy sanctuary as an energetic and diligent soldier of the heavenly army, so that he may faithfully serve at the holy altars; and may the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and fortitude, the Spirit of knowledge and piety rest upon him. Fill him with the Spirit of your fear, so that you may strengthen him in divine ministry, so that, obedient in deed and submissive in speech, he may obtain your grace. Through. [Note: Menardus: “and him.”] [Note: In the same author: “so that, obedient in deed and ...”]

[Note: This consecration pertains to the ordination of a priest; it has been placed here incorrectly.]

### Consecration of the hands

“Let these hands be consecrated by this anointing and our blessing, so that whatever they bless may be blessed, and whatever they sanctify may be sanctified.” Through our Lord.

## XCVII. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE CONSECRATION OF A DEACON

[Col. 1148B] Hearken favorably to our prayers, we beseech you, Lord, so that your Levites, serving at the sacred altars, may be grounded in the truth of faith and distinguished in spiritual understanding. Through the Lord.

### Secret
