Receive, we beseech you, Lord, the offerings of your servant and Levite, N., by which you have granted us, devoted in mind to your name, both to be purified from earthly contagions and to draw near as companions to heavenly things. Through our Lord.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, we beseech you, Lord, mercifully accept this offering of your servant, N., which we offer to you on the day when you appointed him to the ministries of the Levites in the sanctuary; and, being favorable to him, grant that, to whom you gave the capacity for the ministry of a Levite, you may grant sufficient grace to minister. This offering ...

### Postcommunion

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that we may rejoice in the increase of our progress and in the fitting service of the paschal sacrament. Through the Lord.

## XCVIII. [Note: Read: “ON THE ANNIVERSARY.”] ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE CONSECRATION OF A PRIEST: How he ought to celebrate Mass for himself

God, at whose command the order of all the heavens proceeds, mercifully regard the age of our time, so that our service may please you, and grant us the gifts of your mercy. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Having received our gifts and prayers, cleanse us by the heavenly mysteries and mercifully hear us. Through the Lord.

“It is right and salutary, because your praise endures for ever and ever, Lord.” We beseech you that this voice of your people singing faithfully together may be pleasing and joyful to your Majesty. At the same time I humbly ask this also: deign to look down from the lofty throne of your judgment upon these sacrifices, which I, though unworthy, presume to offer to you on the day when you commanded me to be consecrated a priest at the sacred altars; fill them with your blessing and sanctify them with your sanctification. Through Christ the Lord.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, I, your servant, offer you this offering today on the day when, though worthy by no merits, but solely by the gift of your mercy, you deigned to bring me to this place of the priesthood. I ask you to receive it favorably, humbly beseeching your Majesty that, just as your goodness commanded me to serve at the sacred altars in the priestly office, so it may make me both worthy and deserving. This offering ... [Note: I would read: “deservedly.”]

[Col. 1149B] Postcommunion.

May the heavenly performance of the sacrament purify us, Lord, and continually renew us with divine affections for receiving your magnificence. Through.

## XCIX. PRAYER FOR THE ORDINATION OF BISHOPS

Let us pray, most beloved, that for these men, being provided for the benefit of the Church, the kindness of almighty God may grant the abundance of his grace. Through.

Hear the prayers of those who implore you, Lord, so that what must be carried out through our ministry may be firmly established by your favorable power. Through the Lord.

Be favorable, Lord, to our supplications, and, bending over these servants of yours the horn of priestly grace, pour out upon them the power of your blessing. Through the Lord.

### Consecration

God of all honors, God of all dignities that serve your glory in the sacred orders; God who, among the other teachings of heavenly worship, instructed your servant Moses with the affection of intimate friendship concerning the form of priestly clothing, and commanded elect Aaron to be clothed in a mystical vestment amid the sacred rites, so that succeeding posterity might derive understanding from the examples of those who came before, lest the instruction of your teaching be lacking to any age—for among the ancients the very appearance of the symbols possessed reverence, while among us the realities themselves provide more certain experience than the enigmas of figures.

[Col. 1149D] For the clothing of that former priesthood is the adornment of our mind, and the glory of the pontifical office no longer commends to us the honor of garments but the splendor of souls, since those things that then pleased the bodily eyes demanded rather that the things within them be understood. And therefore, we beseech you, Lord, grant this grace to your servants whom you have chosen for the ministry of the high priesthood, so that whatever those coverings signified by the gleam of gold, the brilliance of jewels, and the variety of workmanship of many kinds may shine forth in the conduct and deeds of these men.

Complete, Lord, in your priests the fullness of your ministry [Note: In Menardus: “mystery.”], and sanctify those equipped with ornaments of every glorification by the flower of heavenly ointment. May this flow abundantly upon their heads; may it run down over their mouths beneath; may it descend to the extremities of their whole bodies, so that the power of your Spirit may fill the inner parts and surround the outer. May steadfastness of faith, purity of love, and sincerity of peace abound in them. May their feet be beautiful through your gift for announcing peace and announcing your good things.

Grant them, Lord, the ministry of reconciliation in word, deed, and the power of signs and wonders. May their speech and preaching be not in persuasive words of human wisdom but in the manifestation of the Spirit and of power. Grant them, Lord, the keys of the kingdom of heaven, so that they may use them and not glory [Note: In the Frankish Missal: “nor glory.”] in the authority you grant for building up, not for destroying. Whatever they bind on earth shall be bound also in heaven, and whatever they loose on earth shall be loosed also in heaven. Whose sins they retain, let them be retained; and whose sins they forgive, may you forgive. Whoever blesses them, let him be blessed; and whoever curses them, let him be filled with curses.

Let them be faithful and prudent servants whom you, Lord, appoint over your household, so that they may give them food at the proper time and present every person complete. Let them be diligent in care and fervent in spirit. Let them hate pride; let them love truth, and never abandon it, overcome either by weariness or fear. Let them not call light darkness or darkness light; let them not call evil good or good evil. Let them be debtors to the wise and obtain fruit from the progress of all.

[Col. 1150C] Grant them, Lord, the episcopal chair for governing your Church and the whole people. Be their authority; multiply your blessing and your grace over them, so that, always able through your gift to entreat your mercy, they may through your grace be devoted to you. Through.

### Secret

Receive, Lord, the gifts that we offer to you for your servant, N., and mercifully preserve your gifts in him. Through the Lord.

### Postcommunion

Work in us, we beseech you, Lord, the complete remedy of your compassion, and mercifully deign to make us such and foster us. [Note: “Foster” appears redundant.] Through.

## C. ALSO, A MASS WHICH THE BISHOP SINGS FOR HIMSELF ON THE DAY OF HIS ORDINATION

[Col. 1150D]

God, who commanded me to preside over your household not through merits of my own but solely through the ineffable abundance of your grace, grant that I may render the ministry of the priestly office worthily to you, serve ecclesiastical ministries fittingly, and govern the people entrusted to me, while you protect them in all things. Through.

God, creator and ruler of the world, mercifully heed the prayers of my humility, and make me, your servant, whom you have granted to serve the heavenly mysteries not through any merits of my own but through the immense abundance of your clemency, a worthy minister at the sacred altars, so that what is uttered by my voice for celebration may be confirmed by your sanctification. Through.

### Secret

Repeating the annual feasts of the beginning of the priesthood for the glory of your name, Lord, we offer you a sacrifice of praise, humbly imploring that we, though unworthy, may be rendered acceptable to you through the intercession of the one whose ministry we serve in your place. Through.

### Within the Canon

I, your servant and priest, offer this offering also on the day on which you deigned to appoint me a priest in the sacred ministry. I beseech you, Lord, mercifully receive it. Therefore I humbly implore your Majesty to deign mercifully to preserve what you have deigned to bestow upon me. Through Christ our Lord. This offering ...

[Col. 1151B] Postcommunion.

May the hearts of your faithful, Lord, be filled with your consolations, and may they likewise give thanks both for the bishop of the Church and for the fullness of their petitions. Through.

## CI. ALSO, ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF A BISHOP, If he is ill or absent, how a priest ought to celebrate Mass [Note: Read: “the Mass.”]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty and everlasting God, that we may show your faithful an ordered affection, and graciously pour into us also a similar love of the Holy Spirit. Through.

[Col. 1151C] ### Secret

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that in sincere hope and charity we may offer you an acceptable sacrifice for both the people and the bishop. Through.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, this offering of our holy Father, Bishop N., which we offer to you on the day when you enriched him with pontifical blessing: grant him, we beseech you, longer spans of life, since you have deigned to grant us the distinguished seasons of his priesthood. This offering ...

### Postcommunion

God, who do not cease to feed us with your sacraments, grant, we beseech you, that the refreshment granted to us through them may confer eternal life. Through.

## CII. ALSO, A MASS FOR ANOTHER PRIEST

[Col. 1151D]

God, who by the power of your majesty distribute the number of our days and measure the periods of time, mercifully regard the service of our humility, and in the abundance of your peace graciously increase our times and those of our bishop through your grace. Through.

### Secret

Mercifully regard, we beseech you, Lord, our service, [Note: Read: “so that”] and may this offering of ours be an acceptable gift to you, an everlasting support for our frailty. Through.

[Col. 1152A] ### Within the Canon

Therefore, this offering of your servant and bishop, N., which he offers to you out of the devotion of his mind, we beseech you, Lord, mercifully accept, and yourself preserve your gifts in him; grant him a span of years so that, happily presiding over your Church, with you accomplishing all things in all, he may use temporal things in such a way as to merit eternal rewards. And our days ...

### Postcommunion

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that the gift of so great a mystery, granted to those who receive it, may be not condemnation but healing. Through.

## CIII. CONSECRATION OF A SACRED VIRGIN, Which is celebrated on Epiphany, or on the second feria of Easter, or on the anniversary of the apostles

[Col. 1152B]

### The prayer follows

Mercifully regard, Lord, this servant of yours, so that she may preserve, under your guidance, the purpose of holy virginity which she has undertaken at your inspiration. Through.

### Likewise, a blessing

God, gracious inhabitant of chaste bodies, God who loves incorrupt souls, God who so repairs in your Word, through whom all things were made, the human substance corrupted in the first human beings by the devil’s deceit, that you not only restore it to the innocence of its original state but also lead it to experience certain goods that are to be possessed in the new age, and advance those still bound by the condition of mortality to the likeness of angels.

Regard, Lord, this servant of yours, who, placing the purpose of her continence in your hand, offers her devotion to you, from whom she herself has received her vows. For when would a mind surrounded by mortal flesh overcome the law of nature, the freedom of license, the force of habit, and the impulses of age, unless you mercifully kindled this love of virginity through free choice, unless you graciously nourished this desire in her heart, unless you supplied strength?

For your grace, poured out upon all nations, has adopted heirs of the New Testament from every nation under heaven, an innumerable number like the stars. Among the other virtues that you have implanted in your children, begotten not from bloods nor from the will of the flesh but from your Spirit, this gift also has flowed from the fountain of your generosity into certain minds: although no prohibition diminished the honor of marriage and the primordial blessing remained upon holy wedlock, there nevertheless arose souls of a higher order who disdained union in the joining of man and woman, desired the sacrament, and did not imitate what is done in marriage but loved what marriage signifies beforehand.

Blessed virginity recognized its author and, emulating angelic purity, devoted itself to the bridal chamber and bed of the one who is the son of perpetual virginity. [Note: From another Vatican Codex supply: “the Bridegroom, just as he is the Son of perpetual virginity.”]

Therefore, to her who implores your help, Lord, and desires to be strengthened by the consecration of your blessing, grant the protection and guidance of your defense, lest the ancient enemy, who harasses higher aspirations with more subtle snares, creep through some negligence of mind to obscure the palm of perfect continence and seize from the purpose of virgins what ought also to be present in the conduct of married women. [Note: I would read: “of married women.”]

May there be in her, Lord, through the gift of your Spirit, prudent modesty, wise kindness, grave gentleness, and chaste freedom. May she burn with love, love nothing outside you, live laudably, and not desire to be praised. [Note: In the Roman Order: “May she glorify you in holiness of body and in purity of soul.”] May she glorify you in holiness of body and in the purity of her soul. May she fear you through love and serve you through love.

May you be her honor, her joy, her will; in sorrow, her consolation; in uncertainty, her counsel; in injury, her defense; in tribulation, her patience; in poverty, her abundance; in fasting, her food; in sickness, her medicine. May she have everything in you, whom she desires to love above all things, and may she preserve what she has professed, pleasing the Searcher of hearts not by her body but by her mind.

May she enter the number of wise young women, so that she may await the heavenly Bridegroom with lamps lit and oil prepared; and, not thrown into confusion by the unexpected arrival of the King, may she go out with her light, join the procession of those going before, and meet him. May she not be shut out with the foolish, but may she freely enter the royal door with the wise virgins and remain with worthy chastity forever in the perpetual company of your Lamb. Through the Lord.

### Blessing of the garments of virgins

God, the most faithful promiser and most certain fulfiller of eternal goods, who promised your faithful a garment of salvation and a clothing of joy, we humbly implore your clemency: mercifully bless these garments, signifying humility of heart and contempt for the world, with which your servants are visibly to be formed in holiness, so that they may preserve, under your protection, the habit of blessed chastity which they receive through your inspiration; and those whom you clothe temporally with the garment of venerable promise, make them be clothed with blessed immortality. Through our Lord.

## CIV. Likewise, a prayer over the handmaids of God when, after their conversion, their garments are changed

We invoke you, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, over these servants of yours who desire to serve you with pure minds and a clean heart, that you may deign to associate them with those 144,000 infants [Note: The Roman Order reads: “who remained virgins.”] who remained virgins and did not defile themselves with women, in whose mouth no deceit was found. So also make these servants of yours remain immaculate to the end. Through the immaculate Jesus Christ our Lord, with whom you live and reign, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, throughout all ages.

## CV. ALSO, PRAYERS FOR THE MASSES OF THE SAME

[Col. 1154A]

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, to your servant, whom you have deigned to adorn with the honor of virginity, the completed result of the work begun; and, so that she may offer you perfect fullness, may she deserve to bring her beginnings to completion. Through.

### Secret

With the offerings made, we beseech you, Lord, grant this servant of yours perseverance in perpetual virginity, so that, when the highest King arrives, she may deserve to enter with joy through open doors. Through.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, we beseech you, Lord, mercifully sanctify this offering of your servant, N., which she offers to you on the anniversary of her birth, on which day, joining her to yourself, you deigned to protect her with the sacred veil, so that she may deserve to meet you, the Lord and her Bridegroom, when you come, with her unquenchable lamp, pleasing to you. Through.

### Postcommunion

Regard, Lord, the service owed to you by your servant, so that amid the uncertainties of human frailty she may not be overcome by any adversities, since she trusts in your protection. Through.

## CVI. ALSO, ANOTHER OF THE SAME

God, lover of chastity and guardian of continence, graciously hear our supplication and mercifully look upon this servant of yours. May she who, out of fear of you, has vowed the purity of continence be preserved by your help, so that, by your generosity, she may receive the sixtieth fruit of continence, eternal life. Through.

### Secret

May the gifts, we beseech you, Lord, of your servant and consecrated woman, N., which she will offer to you for the consecration of her body, together advance toward the healing of her soul. Through the Lord.

### Postcommunion

God, author of good works, purify the heart of your servant, N., so that you may find nothing in her to punish but only what you can crown. Through.

### ALSO, ANOTHER OF THE SAME

Mercifully hear the prayers of your servant, N., we beseech you, Lord, so that, with your help, she may preserve the grace of chastity she has undertaken. Through.

### Secret

Be present, we beseech you, Lord, to the votive offerings of your servant, N., so that, preserved with you as her guardian, she may receive the inheritance of eternal blessing. Through.

### Within the Canon

Therefore, we beseech you, Lord, mercifully accept this offering of your servant, N., which we offer to you on the anniversary of her birth, on which you deigned to protect her with the sacred veil. For her we pour out humble prayers to your Majesty, asking that you command her to pass into the number of the holy virgins, so that she may be able to meet you, her Bridegroom, when you come with your unquenchable lamp, and, joined to the choirs of holy virgins, may give you thanks within the gates of the heavenly kingdom. This offering ...

[Col. 1156A] ### Postcommunion

God, who established your dwelling in a chaste heart, regard your servant, and may she who asks through continual discipline receive consolation from you. Through.

# Α + Ω HERE BEGINS THE SECOND BOOK: PRAYERS AND PETITIONS FOR THE ANNIVERSARIES OF THE SAINTS

[Col. 1155]

## I. ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE ANNIVERSARY OF ONE MARTYR

[Col. 1155B]

Let your devotion know, most holy brothers, that the anniversary of blessed N., the martyr, is approaching—the day on which, overcoming the temptations of the devil, he was joined to the Creator of the universe in the glory of his passion. [For several: “On which, overcoming the devil’s assaults, they were joined to the Creator of the universe in glorious passion.”] Therefore let us praise the Lord together, who is wondrous in his saints, so that he who bestowed upon them the crown of victory may, through their merits, grant us forgiveness of our sins. Let us therefore celebrate this same feast with our customary devotion in that place, or on that road, on that feria.

### ANNOUNCEMENT WHEN THE RELICS OF MARTYRS ARE TO BE PLACED

[Col. 1155C] Most beloved brothers, among the other solemn rites of virtues that pertain to the glory of Christ our Lord, he also granted this to the martyrs [Note: Add: “who.”]: having accepted death for the confession of his name, they deserved heavenly rewards, so that, when their illustrious relics are placed in accordance with the vows of the faithful, the integrity of the holy body may be believed to be present. And therefore we inform your affection that on that feria, in that place, the relics of that holy martyr, N., are to be placed; we ask you not to refuse your presence when we remind you.

## II. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF SAINT FELIX THE CONFESSOR. 18 Kalends of February

[Col. 1155D] May the recounting of the confession of Saint Felix, Lord, increase in us pious devotion, since, persevering in the confession of your name, he deserved to be honored.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty [Note: Pamelius adds: “God.”] God, that blessed Felix, who was glorious through your gifts, may stand before you as an able intercessor for our needs. Through.

### Secret

We offer you, Lord, sacrifices for the commemoration of your confessor Saint Felix, humbly beseeching that, just as you granted him an abundance of sacred faith, so you may grant us peace. Through the Lord.

[Col. 1156B] ### Postcommunion

Trusting in the prayers of the saints, we beseech you, Lord, that through what we have received we may obtain eternal remedies. Through.

## III. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF SAINT MARCELLUS THE CONFESSOR. 17 Kalends of February

Hear our prayers, Lord, which we offer on the solemnity of your confessor and bishop, Marcellus, so that, through the interceding merits of him who deserved to serve you worthily, you may absolve us from all sins. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that blessed Marcellus may shine in the pontificate’s office, pleasing to you, and commend us to your mercy by his pious supplication. Through [Col. 1156C] our Lord.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who celebrate the solemnity of your confessor and bishop, blessed Marcellus, may be helped before you by his intercessions. Through.

### Secret

May the annual solemnity of your confessor and bishop, Saint Marcellus, render us acceptable to your mercy, Lord; through these dutiful services of offering, may blessed recompense accompany him and procure for us the gifts of your grace. Through the Lord.

### Postcommunion

God, the rewarder of the souls of the faithful, grant that through the prayers of your confessor and bishop, blessed Marcellus, whose venerable feast we celebrate, we may obtain forgiveness. Through the Lord.

## IV. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE HOLY MARTYRS SEBASTIAN, MARIA, MARTHA, AUDIFAX, AND ABACUC. 13 Kalends of February

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we may share also in the rewards of your holy martyrs whose victories we celebrate. Through the Lord.

Grant, we beseech you, Lord, that through the intercession of your blessed martyr Sebastian we may be protected in body from every adversity and cleansed in heart from evil thoughts. Through.

### Secret

With Saint Sebastian intervening, Lord, may our service please you, and may the offerings’ acts of service become defenses for the devoted. Through.

### Postcommunion

Satisfied with the heavenly gift, we beseech you, Lord our God, that these gifts may sanctify us through the supplication of your martyr Sebastian. Through.

## V. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF SAINT FABIAN. Likewise, 13 Kalends of February

May the holy prayer of your blessed bishop and martyr Fabian be present for us, Lord, we beseech you; may it continually free us from earthly affections and bring heavenly desires to fulfillment. Through the Lord.

### Secret
Intercession, we beseech you, O Lord, of your pontiff and martyr Fabian, commend our offerings, and may veneration of him render us acceptable to your Majesty. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

We have received the heavenly sacraments on the solemnity of Saint Fabian, O Lord; through his intercessions, we beseech you, grant that what we perform in temporal life we may attain in eternal joys.  
[Note: We have emended the text thus, since the exemplar reads corruptly: “of generosity.”]

### VI. On the Feast of Saint Agnes the Virgin, concerning her Passion. Twelfth day before the Kalends of February.

[Col. 1157C]

May the disposition of holy joy always increase within us, O Lord, and may the venerable festival of blessed Agnes, your virgin and martyr, be enlarged. Through Christ our Lord.

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that our minds, carried forward with exultation, may follow also the constancy of faith of blessed Agnes, your martyr, whose day of passion we commemorate each year with devotion. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: In Pamelius: “progress.”]

**Secret.**

Today, O Lord, we joyfully perform this sacrifice; recalling the heavenly victory of blessed Agnes, we both proclaim your mighty works and rejoice that we have obtained glorious intercessions. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

As we receive everlasting joys from participation in the sacrament of the festival of the holy martyr Agnes, we humbly beseech you that, through your gift, we may receive with worthy understanding whatever we undertake through diligent service, by your granting it. Through Christ our Lord.

### VII. Also on the Feast of the Same, concerning her Nativity. Fifth day before the Kalends of February.

[Col. 1158A]

Be present with us, almighty God, as we celebrate again the feasts of blessed Agnes, whom you raised up by an ineffable gift at the emergence of today’s festival. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: We have emended this from Pamelius, since the exemplar incorrectly reads: “having been mourned.”]

**Secret.**

May the gifts be pleasing to you, O Lord, by which the magnificent solemnity of Saint Agnes is commemorated; for from its beginning to the end of her blessed contest she was so glorious that we ought to pass over neither its beginning nor its end. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

May these holy mysteries that we have received assist us, we beseech you, O Lord, and may the venerable intercession of blessed Agnes assist us also. Through Christ our Lord.

### VIII. Prayer for the Purification of Saint Mary. Fourth day before the Nones of February.

[Note: Pamelius more correctly has: “God, whose present day …”]

O God, whose Only-Begotten Son was presented in the temple on this day in the flesh he assumed for us, grant that, as we joyfully receive him as our Redeemer, so we may confidently behold him coming as Judge. Through the same Lord our God.

**Secret.**

May the offering of today’s festival be acceptable to you, O Lord, we beseech you; and, by the abundance of your grace, may we through these sacred exchanges be found in that form in which our substance is with you. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Read from the Roman Missal: “through these.”]

**Postcommunion.**

Grant us, O Lord, we beseech you, that through the sacraments we have received, whatever has been wounded in our mind may be healed by the gift of his mercy. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.  
[Note: It should be read: “that through …”]

### IX. On the Feast of Saint Agatha. The Nones of February.

May the martyr Saint Agatha, pleasing to you through the virtue of martyrdom and the merit of chastity, implore your forgiveness for us, O Lord. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Pamelius has: “blessed Agatha the martyr.”]

**Secret.**

May the gifts of your supplicating Church become pleasing in your sight, O Lord; and, that they may advance our salvation, may the intercession of your blessed martyr Agatha be present. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

We rejoice together both in having received the bread of righteousness and in the festival of your martyr, O Lord, Agatha; trusting that, through the intercessions of those who please you, what we have received will profit us unto everlasting life. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: In the same Mass: “of the martyr.”]  
[Note: In that Mass: “because.”]  
[Note: In the Ambrosian Mass: “may profit.” The word “advance” is redundant, and is so omitted in that Mass.]

### X. On the Feast of Saint Soteris. Fourth day before the Ides of February.

[Col. 1159A]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we may experience the benefits of the holy martyr Soteris, whose beginnings in human life we celebrate. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

Receive our prayers graciously, we beseech you, O Lord, and may the sacrifice dedicated to you commend blessed Soteris. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Trusting in the prayers of Saint Soteris, we beseech you, O Lord, that through what we have received we may obtain eternal remedies. Through Christ our Lord.

### XI. Prayer for the Feast of Valentine, Vitalis, and Filicula. Sixteenth day before the Kalends of March.

[Col. 1159B]

Protect us, O Lord, through the prayers of your saints, so that, venerating without ceasing the feasts of your martyrs Valentine, Vitalis, and Filicula, we may be fortified by faithful assistance and advance through their magnificent example. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

As we come to the feasts of your martyrs Valentine, Vitalis, and Filicula, O Lord, we approach with gifts dedicated to your name, so that, paying them reverence, we may obtain pardon for ourselves. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 1159C] **Postcommunion.**

Protect your people, O Lord, and by the prayers of your saints grant that the feast of your martyrs Valentine, Vitalis, and Filicula, which you hand down to us as continually owed to you, may be paid without ceasing. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Read: “continually owed.”]

### XII. On the Feast of Saint Juliana. Thirteenth day before the Kalends of March.

Almighty and everlasting God, who choose the weak things of the world to confound the strong, grant us to rejoice at the festival of your holy martyr Juliana with fitting devotion, so that we may both praise your power in her passion and receive the assistance prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 1159D] **Secret.**

As we proclaim you wonderful, O Lord, in the precious passion of your holy martyr Juliana, we bring votive gifts; grant, we beseech you, that just as her merits are pleasing to you, so the services of our obedience may be made acceptable. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

As we partake, O Lord, of the blessed mysteries of your table, we beseech you that through the intercessions of your martyr Saint Juliana they may confer upon us both temporal and present mercy, and eternal mercy. Through Christ our Lord.

### XIII. On the Feast of Saints Perpetua and Felicity. The Nones of March.

[Col. 1160A]

Grant us, O Lord our God, to venerate continually the palms of the holy martyrs, so that those whom we cannot celebrate with a worthy mind we may at least honor with humble and frequent services. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: It should read: “at least, and …”]

**Secret.**

Look favorably, O Lord, upon the gifts set before your altars in commemoration of your saints Felicity and Perpetua; just as through these blessed mysteries you conferred glory upon them, so grant us forgiveness. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Grant us, O Lord, we beseech you, through the intercession of the saints, that we may receive with a pure mind what we touch with our mouth. Through Christ our Lord.

### XIV. On the Annunciation of Saint Mary, Mother of Our Lord Jesus Christ. Eighth day before the Kalends of April.

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God, who, through the overshadowing of divine grace over the sacred womb of blessed Mary, deigned to illumine the whole world; we humbly entreat your Majesty that what we cannot obtain by our merits we may deserve to attain through her protection. Through Christ our Lord.

As your servants, O Lord, we beseech you with humble prayer, imploring your help; may the joys of blessed Mary, ever virgin, accompany us in these solemn celebrations. Through her proclamations and merits, may the documents of our sins be erased, and may we be cleansed from the rust of our criminal deeds—[uncertain word: moliviciorum]—by the fire of compunction, through an inrush of love for you. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Read: “by her proclamation,” or “by her proclamations.”]  
[Note: The passage is very corrupt and can be emended only from other codices.]

**Secret.**

Look favorably, we beseech you, O Lord, upon our offerings, which we bring in the annual solemnity in honor of blessed and glorious Mary, ever virgin, Mother of God; and may your coeternal Holy Spirit, who filled her womb with the splendor of his grace and truth, graciously cleanse us from every crime of sin. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

You have fed us with heavenly nourishment, O Lord; through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, ever virgin and Mother of God, preserve us, we beseech you, from every adversity. Through Christ our Lord.

**Prayers at Vespers.**

May the merits of blessed and glorious Mary, ever virgin and Mother of God, accompany us, O Lord, we beseech you, and may they always implore your forgiveness for us. Through Christ our Lord.

May the glorious intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, ever virgin and Mother of God, protect us, we beseech you, almighty God, and lead us to eternal life. Through Christ our Lord.

Extend your right hand to us, O God, and through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, ever virgin and Mother of God, grant us the help of heavenly power. Through Christ our Lord.

### XV. On the Nativity of Saint Euphemia. The Ides of April.

[Note: Read: “On the Feast,” rather than “On the Nativity.”]

Grant us, almighty God, both to rejoice in the merits of Saint Euphemia the martyr and, through her intercessions, to render thanks for her benefits. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that we may be helped by the prayers pleasing to you of Saint Euphemia the martyr.

[Col. 1161B] May the joyous solemnity of Saint Euphemia the martyr cherish us, O Lord, and never cease to commend us to your goodness. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

With the gifts offered, O Lord, we magnify you; through them, at the solemnities of Saint Euphemia, you both arrange heavenly joys for us and grant us everlasting protection. Through Christ our Lord.

**Another.**

May your abundant blessing descend, O Lord; through the pleading of blessed Euphemia, may it render our gifts acceptable to you and make them for us a sacrament of redemption. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

May the prayer of Saint Euphemia the martyr accompany us, O Lord, pleasing to you, and may it never cease to ask your forgiveness for us. Through Christ our Lord.

### XVI. On the Feast of the Apostles Philip and James. The Kalends of May.

O God, who are the wondrous splendor of all your saints, and who consecrated this day through the martyrdom of the blessed apostles Philip and James, grant your Church to rejoice in the feast of so great a solemnity, and may we be helped before your mercy both by their examples and by their merits. Through Christ our Lord.

Almighty God, may the festive solemnity of Saints James and Philip gladden us, and may we glory in the feasts of those whose intercessions support us. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

Look upon the gifts we bring in commemoration of your holy apostles Philip and James, O Lord; since they are pleasing in their honor, may they become beneficial to us through their perpetual intercession. Through Christ our Lord.

**Preface.**

For it is your work and your power that the glorious confession of the blessed apostles James and Philip should bring us, unto the end of the age, an increase of the heavenly kingdom. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Emended thus from the Ambrosian Mass. The exemplar corruptly reads: “Who, for you, and of your work and power …”]

[Col. 1162A] **Postcommunion.**

Help us, O Lord, through the intercession of the blessed apostles whose solemnity we joyfully celebrate as we receive your holy gifts. Through Christ our Lord.

### XVII. On the Feast of Saint Juvenal. Fifth day before the Nones of May.

May the confession and merit of Juvenal always benefit us, we beseech you, O Lord. Through Christ our Lord.

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that the merits pleasing to you of your holy confessor and bishop Juvenal may always entreat your goodness for the flocks he governed with sincere sacramental care. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

May the holy pontiff Juvenal render our offerings acceptable to your name, O Lord, for he was well pleased worthily to offer them to you. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Joyfully, O Lord, we have received the heavenly sacraments, and through the intercession of your blessed confessor and pontiff Juvenal we trust that they will benefit us more abundantly. Through Christ our Lord.

### XVIII. On the Finding of the Holy Cross. Also, fifth day before the Nones of May.

O God, who, in the glorious finding of the life-giving cross, revived the miracles of your passion, grant that through the price of the life-giving wood we may attain the assistance of eternal life. Through Christ our Lord.

O God, to whom all creatures obey, and who made all things in your Word, in wisdom, we humbly beseech your ineffable clemency: those whom you deigned to redeem through the wood of the holy cross by the loving blood of your Son—since you are the tree of life and the restorer of Paradise—extinguish, with all interceding, the dreadful poisons of the serpent, and continually pour forth through the grace of the Spirit the cup of salvation. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Pamelius has: “and who …”]

**Secret.**

Look favorably, O Lord, upon the sacrifice we offer, so that it may strip us of every wickedness of warfare and, through the banner of the holy cross of your Son, establish us in the security of your protection, to crush the snares of the adversaries’ power. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Filled with heavenly nourishment and refreshed by the spiritual cup, we beseech you, almighty God, that you defend from the evil enemy those whom, through the wood of the holy cross of your Son—the weapons of righteousness for the salvation of the world—you commanded to triumph. Through Christ our Lord.

### XIX. On the Feast of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, Brothers, and Saint Pancratius. Fourth day before the Ides of May.

May the blessed solemnity of your martyrs Nereus and Achilleus always cherish us, O Lord, we beseech you, and make us worthy of your service. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 1163A] **Secret.**

May the pleasing confession of your saints Nereus and Achilleus commend our gifts to you, O Lord, and always implore your forgiveness for us. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

We beseech you, O Lord, that through the prayers of your blessed martyrs Nereus and Achilleus the holy sacraments we have received may advance us toward an increase of your reconciliation. Through Christ our Lord.

### XX. On the Feast of Saints Peter and Marcellinus. Fourth day before the Nones of June.

May your Church rejoice, O God, trusting in the intercessions of your martyrs Peter and Marcellinus; through their glorious prayers may it remain devoted and stand secure. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

As we bring votive gifts, O Lord, in the passion of your martyrs Peter and Marcellinus, we venerate your magnificence and through it implore the help of your goodness for us. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Pamelius more correctly reads: “in the passion, your [magnificence].”]

**Postcommunion.**

We beseech you, O Lord, that, filled with the saving mysteries, we may be helped by the prayers of those whose solemnity we celebrate. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Through the intercession of your saints, O Lord, grant assistance to your people, so that, freed from all harmful things, they may receive everything beneficial to them. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXI. Also on the Feast of Saints Cyrinus, Nabor, and Nazarius. The day before the Ides of June.

[Col. 1163C]

May the vows of the feast of Saints Cyrinus, Nabor, and Nazarius shine for us, O Lord; and may what granted them everlasting excellence increase through the fruits of our devotion. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: The same source has: “may votive offerings shine.”]

**Secret.**

For the venerable blood of Saints Cyrinus, Nabor, and Nazarius, we solemnly sacrifice offerings to you, O Lord, recounting your wonders, through which such a victory was achieved. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Pamelius: “through whom.”]

**Postcommunion.**

May we always celebrate the solemnities of the holy martyrs Cyrinus, Nabor, and Nazarius, O Lord, and continually experience their protection. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: The same source has: “may we celebrate.”]

### XXII. On the Feast of Saint Vitus. Seventeenth day before the Kalends of July.

Grant your Church, O Lord, we beseech you, through the intercession of Saint Vitus, not to think arrogantly but to advance in humility pleasing to you, so that, despising insolence, it may exercise free love in all mature things. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 1164A] **Secret.**

Just as the gifts offered for the saints testify to the glory of divine power, so may they bestow upon us, O Lord, the effect of your salvation. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: In the Ambrosian Mass preserved by Pamelius: “We humbly implore your Majesty, almighty God, that just as glory …”]

**Postcommunion.**

Refreshed, O Lord, by the solemn blessing, we beseech you that, through the intercession of Saint Vitus, the medicine of the sacrament may benefit both our bodies and our minds. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXIII. On the Feast of Saints Mark and Marcellianus. Fourteenth day before the Kalends of July.

May the feast of your saints Mark and Marcellianus protect us, O Lord, for the more frequently we are cherished by the blessings of the martyrs, the more confidently we beseech your name. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

Receive, O Lord, the votive gifts of your peoples, and grant that through the prayers of Saints Mark and Marcellianus they may be pleasing to you, since they are offered for their solemnities. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

As we partake, O Lord, of the blessed mysteries of your table, we beseech you that through the intervention of the blessed saints Mark and Marcellianus they may confer upon us both temporal and eternal mercy. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXIV. On the Vigil of the Holy Martyrs Gervasius and Protasius. Also, fourteenth day before the Kalends of July.

[Col. 1164C]

As we anticipate the feast of your martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, we humbly ask you, O Lord, to grant that those whom you have exalted with heavenly glory may be present to your faithful. Through Christ our Lord.

Let us implore the help of Saints Gervasius and Protasius, so that, O Lord, we may be freed from all offenses. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

May the sacrifice that our devotion offers beforehand for the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius increase for us, by your gift, the assistance of their merits. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: In the aforementioned Mass: “your martyrs Protasius and Gervasius.”]  
[Note: The same Mass: “by their merit.”]

**Postcommunion.**

May the perpetual protection of the sacrifice received, O Lord, never abandon us, and may it always drive every harmful thing away from us. Through Christ our Lord.

**Also on their Feast. As above. Thirteenth day before the Kalends of July.**

May the blessed confession of your holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius unite us, O Lord, and may it graciously entreat assistance for our weakness. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: In the same Mass: “for our frailty.”]

[Col. 1165A] **Secret.**

Grant us, almighty God, that through these gifts, which we bring in honor of the holy martyrs Gervasius and Protasius, we may both please you by what is offered and be brought to life by what is received. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that through the power of the mysteries the life of us who celebrate Saints Gervasius and Protasius may be strengthened. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXV. On the Vigil of Saint John the Baptist. Eighth day before the Kalends of July.

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that your people may be prepared through the feast of blessed John the Baptist for the accomplishment of complete devotion; you sent him before your Son to prepare a perfect people for Jesus Christ.  
[Note: Pamelius has: “for Jesus Christ our Lord.”]

May the splendid prayer of blessed John the Baptist accompany us, O Lord, and may he who foretold that Christ would come ask that he be made favorable to us. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

Look favorably, O Lord, upon the gifts of your people, and grant that we, who are allowed to anticipate the solemnity of blessed John the Baptist, may rejoice in his intercessions. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Grant, merciful God, that, instructed by the mystical beginnings of your Church and by the sacred proclamations of blessed John the Baptist, it may continually produce worthy fruits of salvation for avoiding the anger of the coming judgment. Through Christ our Lord.

May the prayer of blessed John the Baptist ask for us both understanding of the mystery of your Christ and the grace to attain it. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXVI. Also on the Feast. From the foregoing.

O God, who have made this day honorable for us through the birth of blessed John, grant your peoples the grace of spiritual joys, and direct the minds of all the faithful in the way of salvation and peace. Through Christ our Lord.

Almighty and everlasting God, who fulfilled the legal ordinances and the proclamations of the holy prophets in the days of blessed John the Baptist, grant, we beseech you, that, when the figures of signs have ceased, Truth itself may speak through its manifestation: Jesus Christ our Lord. Who lives and reigns with you.

[Col. 1165D] **Secret.**

We heap your altars with gifts, O Lord, celebrating with due honor the birth of Saint John, who both proclaimed beforehand that the Savior of the world would come and showed that Jesus Christ was present.

**Postcommunion.**

May your Church, O God, receive the joy of the birth of blessed John the Baptist, through whom it came to know the author of its own rebirth. Through Christ our Lord.

As we celebrate the feast of Saint John, we humbly beseech you, O Lord, that this same celebration may always be for us both a cause of forgiveness and of salvation. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 1166A] **This is for the Vigil of Saint John.**

May the splendid prayer of blessed John the Baptist accompany us, O Lord; he foretold that Christ would come, and may he ask from him an everlasting remedy for us. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXVII. On the Vigil of the Martyrs John and Paul. Seventh day before the Kalends of July.

May your Church, O Lord, devoutly receive the venerable feast of the blessed martyrs John and Paul, and may it become more devoted through love of their great glorification. Through Christ our Lord.

May the merits of your blessed martyrs John and Paul accompany us, O Lord, and may they always implore your forgiveness for us. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 1166B] **Secret.**

May the gifts of our fasting be pleasing to you, O Lord, whenever we bring them in worthy commemoration of your saints John and Paul, provided that we likewise follow their deeds. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Protect your people, O Lord, and grant through the prayers of the just that the people whom you make devoted through the continual festival of your martyrs John and Paul may always become pleasing to you. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXVIII. Also on their Feast. Sixth day before the Kalends of July.

We beseech you, almighty God, that the doubled joy of today’s festival may receive us, as it proceeds from the glorification of the blessed John and Paul, whom the same faith and passion made brothers. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

We shall place offerings of reconciliation upon your altars, O Lord, honoring your power in the passions of your saints and imploring through them forgiveness for us. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Pamelius has: “we place.”]

**Postcommunion.**

Grant, O Lord, through the prayers of your saints, that the gifts received may bring about our sanctification. Through Christ our Lord.

Filled with heavenly gifts, we beseech you, O Lord our God, that these gifts may sanctify us through the prayer of your martyrs John and Paul. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Pamelius has: “that they may sanctify us.”]

### XXIX. On the Vigil of the Apostles Peter and Paul. Third day before the Kalends of July.

[Col. 1166D]

O God, who grant us to anticipate the glorious feast of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, grant, we beseech you, that we may always be preceded by their benefits and helped by their prayers. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

We offer gifts of your glorification, O Lord; may the prayer of the holy apostles, whose solemnity we anticipate, make them pleasing to you as offerings for our fasting. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 1167A] **Postcommunion.**

May your people always rejoice in continuous honor of the blessed Peter and Paul, and may they be governed by these leaders, whose teaching and merits are their joy. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXX. Also on the Feast of Saint Peter in Particular. Third day before the Kalends of July.

O God, who, having bestowed on your blessed apostle Peter the keys of the heavenly kingdom, entrusted to him the pontifical authority of binding and loosing souls, grant that through the assistance of his intercession we may be freed from the bonds of our sins. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

May the prayer of blessed Peter the apostle commend to you, O Lord, the prayers and offerings of your Church, so that what we celebrate for his glory may profit us toward forgiveness. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

May the gift offered gladden us, O Lord, so that, just as we proclaim you wonderful in your apostle Peter, so through him we may receive the abundance of your forgiveness. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXXI. On the Feast of the Apostles Peter and Paul. Third day before the Kalends of July.

O God, who consecrated this day through the martyrdom of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, grant your Church, spread throughout the whole world, always to be governed by their teaching, through whom it received the beginning of its religion. Through Christ our Lord.

By your generosity, O Lord, the feast of the blessed Peter and Paul has shone upon us; grant, we beseech you, that the glory of their passion today, just as it bestowed everlasting magnificence upon them, may likewise work perpetual protection for us. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

May the blessed passion of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul make acceptable to you the offerings of your people, O Lord; and may those things that are not suited to our merits become pleasing to you through the prayer of your righteous ones. Through Christ our Lord.

**Preface.**

With you there is a continual festival and eternal celebration of the blessed apostles, and the perpetual feast of their heavenly triumph; nevertheless, as we recall the beginnings of their blessed confession, grant us to rejoice with frequent devotion, so that the more often honor is returned to their most sacred passion, the greater grace of recompense it may bestow upon us. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Having received everlasting remedies, may the hearts of your faithful be cleansed, O Lord, so that with devout understanding they may comprehend the insignia of the apostolic feast of Peter and Paul, which they carry out through bodily observances. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Pamelius has: “of the apostles.”]

**Another.**

We have received, O Lord, the pledge of eternal salvation, celebrating the votive solemnity of the apostles Peter and Paul and venerating their everlasting merits. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXXII. Also on the Feast of Saint Paul in Particular. Third day before the Kalends of July.

[Col. 1168A]

O God, who taught the multitude of the nations through the preaching of the blessed apostle Paul, grant, we beseech you, that we who celebrate his feast may experience his protection with you. Through Christ our Lord.

We humbly implore your Majesty, O Lord, that, just as the holy apostle Paul was a preacher of your Church, so he may be our perpetual intercessor. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

May the desired communion with your apostle come before us, O Lord, we beseech you, so that those whose perpetual dignity we honor on earth in the sacred mystery may ask for us both present and eternal assistance. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Having received the sacraments, we humbly pray and ask, O Lord, that, through the intercession of your blessed apostle Paul, the things performed for his passion may profit us for healing. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXXIII. Prayers at Vespers.

O God, who granted your apostles the authority to bind and loose, grant, we beseech you, that through them, freed from earthly vices, we may be able to participate in the heavenly mysteries. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Read: “expeaitique” (that is, “and, being freed …”).]

[Col. 1168C] Almighty and everlasting God, who cause us to rejoice in the manifold celebration of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, grant, we beseech you, that their solemnity, repeated more frequently, may increase our protection. Through Christ our Lord.

Raise us up, O Lord, through the apostolic protection of the blessed Peter and Paul, so that, the more fragile we are, the stronger assistance may cherish us. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that your apostles may intercede for us, for we trust that we can then be saved if your Church is governed by their prayers—those apostles whom, by your appointment, it employs as its leaders. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Almighty and everlasting God, who have granted us to venerate the merits of all the apostles in one celebration, we beseech you to grant us swiftly an abundance of your favor through these multiplied intercessors. Through Christ our Lord.

Hear us, God our Savior, and protect us through the intercessions of the apostles whose teachings you have granted your faithful to follow. Through Christ our Lord.

Rejoicing in the multiplication of the apostolic solemnity, we beseech your clemency, almighty God, that you may continually grant us to be blessed by their confession and cherished by their protection. Through Christ our Lord.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that we who are continually fortified by apostolic defense may neither succumb to vices nor be oppressed by adversities. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXXIV. Also for the Vigil of All the Apostles.

[Col. 1169A]

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that just as we anticipate the glorious feasts of your apostles, so they themselves may anticipate your Majesty for us, that we may merit your benefits. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

With our gifts we precede the feasts of those apostles, O Lord, so that what is hindered by obstacles in our conscience may be made pleasing through their merits. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Having received the sacrament, we humbly beseech you that, through the intercession of the blessed apostles, we may receive unto eternal life what we perform in temporal life. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 1169B]

### XXXV. Also on the Feast of All the Apostles.

O God, who have granted us to come to knowledge of your name through the blessed apostles, grant us to celebrate their everlasting glory by advancing, and to advance by celebrating. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: We have emended this, since the exemplar incorrectly reads: “by perfecting.”]

**Secret.**

As we anticipate the perpetual glory of the holy apostles, we beseech you that, purified by the sacred mysteries, we may celebrate that same glory more worthily. Through Christ our Lord.

**Preface.**

You do not abandon your Church in everlasting goodness; through your apostles you continually both instruct and protect it. And therefore, with the angels …  
[Note: We have emended this, since the exemplar corruptly has: “deserting.”]

**Postcommunion.**

Having received the sacraments, we humbly ask that, through the intercession of your blessed apostles, what we undertake for their venerable passion may profit us for healing. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXXVI. On the Octave of the Apostles. The day before the Nones of July.

O God, whose right hand raised up the blessed apostle Peter as he walked upon the waves, lest he be drowned, and delivered his fellow apostle Paul from the depths of the sea when he had suffered shipwreck three times, graciously grant that through the merits of both we may attain the eternal grace of the Trinity. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Pamelius and Menardus have: “the glory of eternity.”]

**Secret.**

We offer the sacrifice, O Lord, which we continually both render and owe to your Majesty out of reverence for the apostles Peter and Paul. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Humbly entreating you, eternal Shepherd, not to abandon your flock, but to guard it through the blessed apostles with continual protection, so that it may be guided by those same leaders whom you appointed as shepherds to preside as vicars of your work. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Menardus reads: “but through …”]  
[Note: The same source has: “may it be governed.”]  
[Note: Menardus has: “to the same.”]

**Postcommunion.**

Receiving the pledge of eternal life, we humbly implore you that, supported by apostolic protection, we may receive in manifest possession what we touch in the image of the sacrament. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXXVII. On the Feast of Saints Simplicius, Faustinus, and Viatrix. Fifth day before the Kalends, or rather the fourth day before the Kalends, of August.

Grant, O Lord, we beseech you, that just as the Christian people rejoices with your martyrs Simplicius, Faustinus, and Viatrix in a temporal solemnity, so it may enjoy an eternal one, and may attain in reality what it celebrates in its vows. Through Christ our Lord.

[Col. 1170B] **Secret.**

We bring offerings to you, O Lord, in commemoration of the holy martyrs Simplicius, Faustinus, and Viatrix, humbly entreating that they may confer upon us both forgiveness and salvation. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: Read: “simply.”]

**Postcommunion.**

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the solemnity of your saints Simplicius, Faustinus, and Viatrix, celebrated through the heavenly mysteries, may obtain for us the forgiveness of your favor. Through Christ our Lord.

### XXXVIII. On the Feast of Abdo and Senis. Third day before the Kalends of August.

May your saints Abdo and Senis, O Lord, attend us with their devout prayers, and continually ask that we be freed from the dangers of this life. Through Christ our Lord.

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that your Church, trusting in the intercessions of your martyrs Abdo and Senis, may remain devoted and, through their glorious prayers, stand secure. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

We bring gifts to you, O Lord, for the slaughter of the holy martyrs Abdo and Senis, who, while they were brought to an end on earth, became everlasting in heavenly light. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Defend your people, O Lord, with perpetual protection, and do not allow them, for whom the merits of your saints intercede, to obtain with difficulty what they rightly and justly ask. Through Christ our Lord.  
[Note: We have emended this from Menardus. The exemplar corruptly reads: “difficulty.”]

### XXXIX. On the Feast of the Maccabees. The Kalends of August.

[Col. 1170D]

O God, who dwell in the saints and do not abandon devout hearts, graciously receive our prayer and grant your mercy, so that, preserved under your protection, we may be freed from all the dangers of this life. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

May the gifts of your supplicating Church become pleasing in your sight, O Lord; and, that they may advance our salvation, may the intercession of your blessed saints be present. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Filled with heavenly gifts, we beseech you, O Lord our God, that these gifts may sanctify us through the prayer of your martyrs. Through Christ our Lord.

### XL. On the Feast of Saint Sixtus. Eighth day before the Ides of August.

As we commemorate the annual feast of blessed Sixtus, your priest and martyr, O Lord, we beseech you that those things which are instruments of your present gifts for us may become the protection of eternal graces. Through Christ our Lord.

May the frequently celebrated solemnity of Saint Sixtus, O Lord, both instruct us through priestly teachings, by your mercy, and everywhere cherish us through the intercessions of his martyrdom. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

Graciously receive the offerings presented, O Lord, which blessed Sixtus, priest and martyr, commends to your Majesty. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

We have been filled, O Lord, with the gift of the desired solemnity, through which we are helped both by the celebration and by the prayers of blessed Sixtus. Through Christ our Lord.

### XLI. On the Feast of Saint Donatus. Seventh day before the Ides of August.

Be present, O Lord, with our prayers, which we bring in commemoration of your holy confessor and bishop Donatus, so that, since we have no confidence in our own righteousness, we may be helped by him who pleased you through his merits. Through Christ our Lord.

O God, glory of your priests, grant, we beseech you, that we may experience the help of your holy confessor and bishop Donatus, whose feast we celebrate. Through Christ our Lord.

**Secret.**

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that the fruit of devout worship may increase for us through your holy confessor and bishop Donatus, whom we honor with gifts dedicated to the praise of your name. Through Christ our Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

We receive votive offerings, O Lord, for your blessed confessor and bishop Donatus; we beseech you to grant us, through his prayers, protection both for the present life and for the eternal one. Through Christ our Lord.

### XLII. On the Vigil of Saint Lawrence. Fifth day before the Ides of August.

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that the venerable solemnity of your blessed martyr Lawrence, which we anticipate, may increase in us both devotion and salvation. Through Christ our Lord.

We ask, almighty God, that our devotion, which precedes the feast of blessed Lawrence the martyr, may accumulate his patronage for us. Through.

May the doubled grace of blessed Lawrence your [Col. 1172A] martyr refresh us, as we anticipate his glorification with desired offices and await his coming with longing. Through.

### Secret

We recount, Lord, the splendid solemnities of blessed Lawrence, which, approaching them with ready hearts, we both receive and anticipate with the gifts offered. Through.

In anticipation of the devout struggles of the glorious martyr Lawrence—whose honorable annual recurrence is always both perpetual and new, because before the sight of your Majesty the death of your righteous ones remains precious and the beginnings of joy are restored when the origins of eternal blessedness are recalled. [Note: [Col. 1171D] Read: “are restored.” We have corrected it, because the reading was faulty.] And therefore, with the angels.

### Postcommunion

The sacred rites, Lord, and the precious passion of blessed Lawrence [Col. 1172B] the martyr, which we anticipate, refresh us; by them we are continually joined to him, and we always desire to be filled with them. Through.

## XLIII. Also, on the feast of the same [Lawrence]. 4th day before the Ides of August

God, by whose love’s ardor blessed Lawrence, despising the persecutor, conquered the flames of devouring fire, mercifully grant that all who venerate the merits of his martyrdom may be defended by the help of your protection. Through.

God, creator and ruler of the world, who consecrated this day through the martyrdom of your Levite Lawrence, mercifully grant that all who venerate the merits of his martyrdom may, through his intercessions, be delivered from the eternal fires of Gehenna. [Col. 1172C] [Note: [Col. 1171D] In Pamelius, “that” is absent.] Through.

### Secret

Grant, we ask, Lord, that through the intercessions of blessed Saint Lawrence you may mercifully guard your gifts within us, for whose honored confession we offer you sacrifices of praise.  
[Note: [Col. 1171D] Read “mercifully.” We emended it, since the text was faulty.]

On this day of solemnity, when you received blessed Lawrence as a pleasing and undefiled sacrifice in his glorious struggle, for his living limbs, placed upon the coals, hissed; yet it was not the punishment of one suffering, but the progress of a devout confession. Nor did the martyr desire to be freed from earthly torment, but he begged to be crowned in heaven. [Note: [Col. 1172D] Thus we corrected it; the exemplar reads, less correctly, liberato (“having been freed”).] Through Christ the Lord.

### Postcommunion

[Col. 1172D] We receive, Lord, votive gifts for the passion of your blessed martyr Lawrence; we ask that through his prayers you grant us protection alike in the present life and in the eternal one. Through.

## Prayers at Vespers

May the holy prayer of Saint Lawrence protect us, Lord, and may what our conscience does not deserve be granted to us through the prayer of him who pleased you. Through.

May the blessing of Saint Lawrence the martyr be with us, we ask, in your glorification; today his [Col. 1173A] confession has become an intercession for us through your power.  
[Note: [Col. 1172D] In Pamelius: “in his glorification.”]

Grant, we ask, Lord, that the votive martyrdoms of blessed Lawrence may always gladden us, though they never cease to be wondrous. Through the Lord.

## XLIIII. On the feast of Saint Tiburtius. 3rd day before the Ides of August

Almighty and eternal God, who gladden us by the feast of your holy martyr Tiburtius, grant that we who rejoice in his commemoration may be defended by his protection. Through.

### Secret

Look upon, Lord, the gifts that we bring in commemoration of Saint Tiburtius, so that what is pleasing because of his [Col. 1173B] honor may become perpetual for us through his intercession. Through.

### Postcommunion

May the solemnity celebrated for Saint Tiburtius benefit us, Lord, for the more fragile we are, the more we need the protections that please you. Through.

## XLV. On the feast of Saint Hippolytus. Ides of August

May the venerable feast of Saint Hippolytus the martyr, Lord, grant us an increase of saving help. Through.

### Secret

Grant us, almighty God, we ask, that the offering of our humility may be pleasing both for the honor [Col. 1173C] of your saints and may purify us alike in body and mind. Through.

### Postcommunion

Having received the sacraments, Lord, we ask that, through the intercession of your blessed martyr Hippolytus, we may advance toward the increase of eternal redemption.

## XLVI. On the octave of Saint Lawrence. 16th day before the Kalends of September

May the venerable passion of blessed Lawrence make us joyful, Lord, and render us capable of recalling it adequately. Through.

With the feast repeated, we venerate the nativity of blessed Lawrence, which we know shines eternally in heavenly blessedness. Through.

### Secret  
[Col. 1173D]

With doubled gifts, Lord, we celebrate the honorable passion of blessed Lawrence the martyr; although it is to be commemorated in its own origins, it nevertheless remains gloriously without end. Through.

For the repeated solemn rites of blessed Lawrence the martyr are joyful to us in proportion as his merits must be proclaimed by us without ceasing. And therefore, with the angels.

### Postcommunion

May the solemn intercession of blessed Lawrence the martyr, Lord, we ask, provide us help, so [Col. 1174A] that participation in the heavenly table which we have received may grant your Church renewed joy.  
[Note: [Col. 1173D] In Pamelius: “solemn.”]  
[Note: [Col. 1173D] In the same source: “which we have taken.”] Through.

## XLVII. On the Assumption of Saint Mary. 18th day before the Kalends of September

God, who through the fruitful virginity of blessed Mary granted the human race the rewards of eternal salvation, grant, we ask, that we may experience her interceding for us with you, through whom we were found worthy to receive the author of our life. Through the Lord.

Almighty and eternal God, who willed to join to earthly bodies, through the venerable and glorious ever-virgin Mary, an ineffable mystery—the truth of your Word, your only-begotten Son—we ask your boundless clemency, that what we request in her honor we [Col. 1174B] may, with you propitious, deserve to obtain. Through.  
[Note: [Col. 1173D] The Ambrosian Mass reads *semperque*, “and always.”]

### Secret

Receive, Lord, the gifts we bring at the repeated solemnity of blessed Mary, because even the assumption of such a one redounds to the praise of your proclamations. Through.

### Postcommunion

Satisfied with the heavenly gift, almighty God, guard us by your protection; and, with holy Mary interceding, mercifully grant purity and peace to our minds and bodies. When your only-begotten Son, the Bridegroom, comes, may we, with lamps lit, be found worthy to await his arrival.  
[Note: [Col. 1174D] In the same Mass: “satisfied.”]  
[Note: [Col. 1174D] The same source: “may your protection guard us.”] Through.

## XLVIII. On the feast of Saint Agapitus. 15th day before the Kalends of September

[Col. 1174C] May the merits of the holy martyr Agapitus, Lord, protect us—merits in which, while proclaiming the works of your Majesty, we may receive both present and future help. Through.

### Secret

We bring you gifts, Lord, for the passion of the holy martyr Agapitus, who, when he came to an end on earth, became perpetual in the heavenly dwelling. Through.

### Postcommunion

May the perpetual guardianship of the sacrifice received, Lord, never abandon us, and may it always drive away everything harmful from us. Through.

## XLVIIII. On the feast of Saint Magnus. 14th day before the Kalends of September

[Col. 1174D] Be present to our supplications, Lord, and, with your blessed martyr Magnus interceding, mercifully defend us from the assault of our enemies. Through.

### Secret

May our gifts be pleasing to you, Lord, since they have been established by your commands and are commended by the glorious feast of blessed Magnus. Through.

### Postcommunion

As we receive your holy gifts, we ask, Lord, that the continued protections of blessed Magnus may sustain us. Through.

## L. On the feast of Saint Rufus. 6th day before the Kalends of September

[Col. 1175A] Be present to our supplications, Lord; trusting in the intercessions of blessed Rufus, may we be troubled neither by the threats of those who oppose us nor by any assault. Through.

### Secret

May the intercession of your saint Rufus commend our gifts, Lord, we ask, and through his veneration render us acceptable to your Majesty.  
[The source has “Rum”; evidently “Rufus.”]

### Postcommunion

As we receive everlasting joys from participation in the sacrament and from the feast of your blessed martyr Rufus, we humbly beg that what, by your gift, we carry out through diligent service, we may receive through your gift with worthy [Col. 1175B] understanding. Through the Lord.

## LI. On the feast of Saint Hermes. 5th day before the Kalends of September

May the votive feast of your saint Hermes gladden us, Lord, we ask, and lift us up through the benefits of his intercession. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Mercifully receive our gifts, Lord, we ask; and guard us through the intercession of your saint Hermes, so that we may serve your altars worthily. Through.

### Postcommunion

May your people rejoice, Lord, we ask, in the commemoration of your saint Hermes; and may the one whose votive service brings joy be raised up by the desired intercession. Through.

## LII. On the day of the passion of Saint John the Baptist. 4th day before the Kalends of September

[Note: [Col. 1175D] Bede, chapter 26, or book II, chapter 6, on Mark, says this concerning the passion of John the Forerunner: “In the Book of Sacraments his feast is marked on the fourth day before the Kalends of September; and in the Martyrology distinguished by the names of Eusebius and Jerome, one reads: ‘On the fourth day before the Kalends of September, at Edessa, etc.’”]

[Col. 1175C] May the venerable feast of Saint John the Baptist and your martyr, Lord, grant us the effect of saving help. Through.

Protect us, Lord, by the perpetual protections of Saint John the Baptist; and the more fragile we are, the more lift us up with necessary intercessions. Through.

### Secret

We bring you gifts, Lord, for the passion of Saint John the martyr and Baptist, because, when he came to an end on earth, he became perpetual in the heavenly dwelling.  
[Note: [Col. 1175D] In Menard: “who, when…”]  
[Note: [Col. 1176D] In the same source: “perpetual; we ask that through his favor it may advance us toward salvation.”] Through.

### Postcommunion

May the solemnity of Saint John grant us both, Lord, so that [Col. 1175D] we may venerate the magnificent sacraments we have received in their signification and rejoice that they have been produced rather within us.  
[Note: [Col. 1176D] Menard likewise has this reading; Pamelius reads “the blessed solemnity.”]  
[Note: [Col. 1176D] Pamelius has the same reading; Menard has: “may we venerate them worthily and experience them as salutary for us.”] Through the Lord.

## LIII. On the feast of Saint Priscus. Kalends of September

Almighty and eternal God, strength for those who struggle and crown of martyrs, mercifully look upon the solemnity of this day; make your Church rejoice in continual [Col. 1176A] celebration, and through the intercession of blessed Priscus the martyr advance the petitions of all who intercede. Through.

### Secret

May the offering be made pleasing to you, Lord, through his prayers, for whose feast it is to be sacrificed. Through.

### Postcommunion

Grant, we ask, Lord, that, strengthened by participation in your sacrament, we may also be helped by the prayers of Saint Priscus the martyr. Through.

## LIIII. On the Nativity of Saint Mary. 6th day before the Ides of September

May the glorious intercession of Saint Mary [Col. 1176B] help us, Lord, whose day we also remember—the day on which her blessed birth began. Through.

### Secret

Receive, Lord, we ask, the sacrifices of reconciliation and praise that we offer to you for the Nativity of blessed and glorious Mary, ever-virgin and Mother of God; through her holy intercessions may they benefit us all unto salvation. Through.

### Postcommunion

Be present, we ask, Lord, to your faithful, so that what they have faithfully received they may preserve for themselves in mind and body through the intercession of blessed Mary. Through.

### Another

Having received the sacraments, Lord, and with blessed and glorious Mary, ever-virgin and Mother of God, interceding, we [Col. 1176C] ask that we may advance toward the increase of eternal redemption. Through.

## LV. On the feast of Saint Gorgonius. 5th day before the Ides of September

May Saint Gorgonius gladden us by his intercession, Lord, and make us rejoice in devout solemnity. Through the Lord.

May the offering of our service be pleasing to you, Lord, through which Saint Gorgonius the martyr intervenes. Through.

May that sweetness reach and strengthen your household, God, by which it is continually nourished with the good fragrance of your Christ in your martyr Gorgonius. Through the Lord.

## LVI. On the Exaltation of the Holy Cross. 18th day before the Kalends of October

[Col. 1176D] God, who gladden us on this day by the annual solemnity of the Exaltation of the holy cross, grant that we who have come to know its mystery on earth may obtain the rewards of its redemption. Through.

### Secret

May the help of your mercy precede, Lord, the devout prayers and sacrifices of our humility; and may faith in the wood once again open the salvation that rash presumption [Col. 1177A] had closed through the tree in paradise because of Adam. Through the Lord.

### Postcommunion

Be present to your household, we ask, merciful and compassionate God; hear our prayers in adversity and prosperity, and deign through the help of the holy cross to crush the wickedness of our adversaries, so that they may be able to reach the harbor of your salvation.  
[Note: [Col. 1177D] Pamelius: “in adversity.”] Through.

## LVII. On the feast of Saints Cornelius and Cyprian. 16th day before the Kalends of October

May the feasts of the blessed martyrs and bishops Cornelius and Cyprian protect us, Lord, we ask, and may their venerable prayer commend us. Through.

### Secret  
[Col. 1177B]

Look kindly upon the gifts of your people, Lord, which are dedicated to your Majesty for the solemnities of the holy martyrs Cornelius and Cyprian. Through.

### Postcommunion

Strengthened by the sacred gift, may the prayer of the holy martyrs Cornelius and Cyprian commend us to you, Lord, on their feast. Through the Lord.

## LVIII. On the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian. 5th day before the Kalends of October

May the blessed solemnity of Saints Cosmas and Damian magnify you, Lord, because through ineffable providence you have granted them everlasting glory and us help.  
[Note: [Col. 1177D] In the same source: “by which also…”]  
[Note: [Col. 1178D] Pamelius: “and help.”] Through.

### Secret  
[Col. 1177C]

In the precious death of your just ones, Lord, we offer that sacrifice from which every beginning of martyrdom received its origin. Through.

### Postcommunion

May your sacrament be certain salvation for us, Lord, which is implored through the merits of your blessed martyrs Cosmas and Damian. Through the Lord.

## LVIIII. Prayers for Saint Michael the Archangel. 3rd day before the Kalends of October

Grant us, almighty God, to advance sufficiently in honor of blessed Michael the archangel, so that, while we proclaim his glory on earth, we may be helped by his prayers [Col. 1177D] in heaven.  
[Note: [Col. 1178D] Pamelius: “to that extent.”] Through.

Supported by the intervention of blessed Michael the archangel, we humbly beseech you, Lord, that we may reach in spirit those whom we honor. Through.

Grant us perpetual assistance from your mercy, Lord, since you have also granted that angelic intercessions should not be lacking for us. Through.

### Secret

Mercifully receive the offering of your people, Lord, we ask, so that it may be pleasing not through our merits but through the supplication of your holy archangel Michael. Through.

### Postcommunion  
[Col. 1178A]
