Be present to your people, merciful God; and, so that they may receive the greater benefits of your grace, make them be raised up through the supplications of blessed Michael the archangel. Through.

## LX. Prayer for the fast of the seventh month

Grant, we ask, Lord, that your faithful may receive the venerable solemnities of the fast with fitting devotion and carry them through with confident dedication. Through.

God, who affirm that you remain in sincere hearts, grant us by your grace to become such as you may deign to dwell in. Through.

### Secret

[Col. 1178B] God, who willed your sacraments to consist of these fruits of the earth, grant, we ask, that you confer help upon us both for the present life and for the future. Through.

### Postcommunion

Satisfied with your saving gift, Lord, we humbly beseech you: by the effect of that whose taste gives us joy, renew us. Through the Lord.

## On the Friday of the seventh month

Having begun the fast, Lord, we ask that you pursue it with kindly favor; and just as we fast from food in body, so may we fast from vices in mind. Through.

### Secret

By the offering of this gift, Lord, we propitiate you, [Col. 1178C] and through this work may we be made participants in eternal life. Through.

### Postcommunion

May the most holy draught of the heavenly table, Lord, we ask, always cleanse and nourish our hearts. Through.

## On the twelve lessons. Saturday

Grant, we ask, Lord, that your faithful may be suitably prepared by the fast of the seventh month, and that the bodily discipline solemnly undertaken may pass into the fruit of all souls. Through.

Grant, almighty God, that whoever abstains from food by afflicting the flesh may fast from sin by pursuing righteousness. Through our Lord.

God, author of human salvation, grant us to practice [Col. 1178D] the fasts fittingly, through which you have provided eternal remedies for our nature. Through.

Receive, Lord, the prayers of your suppliant people, and through the vows of our fast bring to fulfilment the mystery of your salvation. Through.

Praising you, almighty Lord, with ready mind, we bring you consecrated fasts, so that, while we are ungrateful for what we have received, we may become more grateful through the fruits we are to receive. Through the Lord.

God, who moderated the fiery flames for the three young men, mercifully grant, we ask, that the flame of vices may not burn us, your servants. Through.

### Secret  
[Col. 1179A]

May this sacrifice, Lord, we ask, both loosen the bonds of our iniquity and reconcile for us the gifts of your mercy. Through.

### Postcommunion

May your sacraments, Lord, we ask, accomplish within us what they contain, so that what we now perform under a figure we may receive in the reality of the things themselves. Through.

### To the people

Help your people, Lord, so that, advancing through the increase of sacred devotion, they may always be governed by your gift and, under your guidance, belong to the fellowship of eternal redemption. Through the Lord.

## LXI. On the feast of Saints Marcellus and Apuleius. Nones of October

[Col. 1179B] May the blessed merits of your saints Marcellus and Apuleius, Lord, accompany us and always bring to perfection those who burn with their love. Through.

### Secret

May this sacrifice, which is to be offered, render your Majesty propitious to us, Lord, through the worthy petition of your saints. Through.

### Postcommunion

May we be fortified by the sacraments received, Lord, and protected by the heavenly arms of your saints Marcellus and Apuleius against all the wickedness that assails us. Through our Lord.

## LXII. On the feast of the Four Crowned Saints: Costianus, Claudius, Castor, and Simpronianus. 6th day before the Ides of November

We return annually to the vows of your martyrs, Lord, humbly beseeching your Majesty that, together with temporal increase, we may receive an increase of eternal prosperity through the Crowned Saints. Through.  
[Note: [Col. 1179D] Add: “Secret.”]  
[The printed source then has a long lacuna.]

We bring you sacrifices, Lord, for the commemoration of your martyrs the Crowned Saints, asking that they grant us both pardon and salvation. Through.

### Postcommunion

May the feasts of your Crowned Saints, Lord, always gladden us, we ask, and commend us to your Majesty through perpetual reconciliation. Through.

## LXIII. On the feast of Saint Cecilia. 11th day before the Kalends of December

[Note: [Col. 1179D] In the margin: “vigil.”]

Grant that we may be strengthened by the supplications of your holy martyr Cecilia, so that, having anticipated her venerable solemnity through our service, we may be commended by her intercessions. Through the Lord.

### Secret

Receive, Lord, the sacrifice of reconciliation and praise, which, with your holy Cecilia intervening, we [Col. 1180A] offer; may it bring us, as we anticipate her feast, both to pardon and to perpetual thanksgiving. Through.

### Postcommunion

As we partake, Lord, of the blessed mysteries of your table, we ask that, through the intervention of Saint Cecilia the martyr, it may grant us both mercy in the present life and eternal mercy. Through.

## LXIIII. Also, on the feast of the same. 10th day before the Kalends of October

[Note: [Col. 1179D] “of December.”]

Almighty and eternal God, who choose the weak things of the world in order to confound the strong, grant us to rejoice with fitting devotion on the feast of your holy martyr Cecilia, so that in her passion we may also [Col. 1180B] receive the help of your power. Through.

Hear us, God our Savior, so that, just as we rejoice in the feast of Saint Cecilia, we may likewise be instructed by the effect of devout devotion.  
[Note: [Col. 1179D] In the Roman Missal: “with devout affection.”] Through the Lord.

May the affection of holy joy always increase within us, Lord, and may the venerable feast of your blessed martyr Cecilia be increased. Through the Lord.

### Secret

[Note: [Col. 1180D] The Ambrosian Mass in Pamelius: “Grant, we ask, God of the heavenly powers.”]

We ask, Lord of the heavenly powers, that the sacrifices brought for the solemnity of Saint Cecilia may teach us to hold temporal desire in contempt and make us seek the gifts of heavenly joys.  
[Note: [Col. 1180D] In the same Mass: “temporal.”] Through.

### Postcommunion

May this grace of yours always exercise us, Lord, we ask, [Col. 1180C] so that it may renew our hearts through the divine mysteries and gladden us through the commemoration of your holy martyr Cecilia. Through.

## LXV. On the feast of Saint Clement. 9th day before the Kalends of December

May your devoted Church receive, Lord, the venerable feast of the nativity of blessed Clement, your priest and martyr, and become more devoted through love of his great glorification. Through.

### Secret

We offer you a sacrifice of praise, Lord, for the feast of Saint Clement, so that we may attain through the intercession of this devout advocate your reconciliation, which we do not deserve through our own works. Through.

### Postcommunion  
[Col. 1180D]

May the feast of blessed Clement, Lord, aid your faithful through his gift; and may he who pleased you implore help for us. Through our Lord.

## LXVI. On the feast of Saint Felicity. Also 9th day before the Kalends of December

May the votive intercession of Saint Felicity, your martyr, sustain us, Lord, we ask, so that we may celebrate her consecrated feast in time and behold it eternally. Through.

### Secret  
[Col. 1181A]

We bring you gifts, Lord, for the glorious commemoration of Saint Felicity, a solemnity that dedicated us to her through its effect and through confession and blood.  
[Note: [Col. 1181D] Pamelius: “beseeching that what this solemnity has effected for us…”]  
[Note: [Col. 1181D] The same source adds: “and may she also implore the continual help of your mercy.”] Through.

### Postcommunion

Grant, Lord, we ask, that, strengthened by participation in your sacrament, we may also be helped by the prayers of Saint Felicity the martyr. Through.

## LXVII. On the feast of the holy martyrs Saturninus, Chrysanthus, Maurus, Daria, and others. 3rd day before the Kalends of December

May the prayer of the blessed martyrs Saturninus and Chrysanthus be present, Lord, so that those whom we venerate through our service we may [Col. 1181B] continually experience as a devout help. Through.

### Secret

May the sacrifice of your people, Lord, be pleasing to you, which is offered on the solemn feasts of your holy martyrs Saturninus and Chrysanthus. Through.

### Postcommunion

We have been filled with the mysteries, Lord; grant, we ask, that through the intercession of your holy martyrs Saturninus and Chrysanthus we may spiritually obtain what we carry out bodily, in vows and joys. Through the Lord.

## LXVIII. On the vigil of Saint Andrew. 3rd day before the Kalends of December

Protect us, merciful God, and always govern us by [Col. 1181C] the protections of your apostle blessed Andrew, whose feast we anticipate. Through.

### Secret

We offer the summit of apostolic reverence to be imbued with the sacred mysteries. Grant, Lord, we ask, that through the intercession of blessed Andrew, whose feast we anticipate, your people may always express their vows here and receive what they desire. Through the Lord.

Rejoicing in the fast dedicated to your reverence, by which we anticipate the apostolic merits of blessed Andrew with desired offices, may we prepare ourselves to celebrate the same solemnly. Through.

### Postcommunion

May your sacraments always purify and protect us, [Col. 1181D] Lord, and through the intercession of your apostle blessed Andrew lead us to the effect of perpetual salvation. Through.

## LXVIIII. Also, on the feast of the same. Day before the Kalends of December

We humbly beseech your Majesty, Lord, that just as your apostle Saint Andrew was a preacher and ruler of your Church, so he may be a perpetual intercessor for us. Through our Lord.

[Col. 1182A] May the apostle blessed Andrew implore you for us, Lord, we ask, so that, freed from our offenses, we may also be rescued from every danger. Through.

### Secret

May the holy prayer of blessed Andrew reconcile our sacrifice to you, Lord, we ask, and may it become acceptable through the merits of him whose honor we solemnly render.  
[Note: [Col. 1181D] Pamelius and Menard read: “so that through the merits of him in whose honor…”] Through.

You granted your Church to stand upon foundations in the apostles.  
[Note: [Col. 1182D] Menard, on the feast of Saint Thomas: “in the apostolic [foundations].”]  
As we celebrate the solemn rites of blessed Andrew from their fellowship, Lord, we do not keep silent about your praises. And therefore, with…

### Postcommunion

Help us, Lord, we ask, through the intercession of your apostle blessed Andrew, for whose solemnity we [Col. 1182B] joyfully receive your holy gifts. Through the Lord.

## LXX. On the octave of Saint Andrew the Apostle. 7th day before the Ides of December

May the frequently repeated solemnity of your apostle blessed Andrew protect us, Lord, so that we may experience perpetual defense from him whose patronage we recall without interruption. Through.

### Secret

May these gifts, which are offered through the intercession of venerable Andrew, provide us with more abundant pardon, Lord, we ask. Through the Lord.

### Postcommunion

May your venerable apostle Andrew help your household by supplication, Lord, and may he, who was [Col. 1182C] a preacher of your name, become a devout intercessor.  
[Note: [Col. 1182D] In the same source, in the vigil of Saint Andrew: “may he become.”] Through the Lord.

## LXXI. On the feast of Saint Thomas the Apostle. 12th day before the Kalends of January

Grant us, Lord, we ask, to glory in the solemn rites of blessed Thomas the apostle, so that we may always be raised up by his patronage and follow the faith with fitting devotion. Through.

### Secret

We render the debt of our service, Lord, humbly beseeching that through the intercessions of the blessed apostle Thomas you may guard your gifts within us; in honoring his confession, we offer sacrifices of your praise.  
[Note: [Col. 1182D] The source has “your” or “of yours,” as in the exemplar. Menard: “to you.”] Through.

### Postcommunion  
[Col. 1182D]

Preserve your people, Lord; and grant them to rejoice in perpetual remedies, whom you never cease to help through the protections of your saints. Through.

## LXXII. Prayer on the feast of many saints

Hear, Lord, the people who beseech you under the patronage of your saints, so that you may grant us to rejoice in the peace of temporal life and to find the helps of eternal life. Through.

### Secret  
[Col. 1183A]

Look upon the prayers and offerings of your faithful, Lord, so that they may be perpetually pleasing to you in the feast of the saints and bring us the help of your reconciliation. Through.

### Postcommunion

Propitiated through the intercession of your saints, grant, we ask, Lord, that what we celebrate in temporal observance we may receive in perpetual salvation. Through.

## LXXIII. Also, another Mass

Grant, Lord, we ask, that just as the feasts of your saints, which are to be celebrated, do not abandon us, so they may continually accompany us through their intercessions. Through.

Be present to your people who beseech you with the patronage of the [Col. 1183B] saints, so that what it does not dare to obtain through its own confidence it may obtain through the merits of its intercessors.  
[Note: [Col. 1183] We emended this from Pamelius, since the exemplar incorrectly reads “may we attain.”] Through the Lord.

### Secret

May your people always rejoice in the saving sacrifice, Lord, by which due honor is offered to the holy martyrs and the gift of your sanctification is acquired. Through.

### Postcommunion

Strengthened by the feasts of the saints and by the sacramental gift, we ask that we may enjoy eternally the good things with which we are now sustained through your grace. Through.

## LXXIV. Also, another Mass

[Col. 1183C] May your saints, Lord, continually ask pardon and advancement for us from you. Through.

God, who surround and protect us both with the solemnities of the holy martyrs and with the glory of confessors, grant us always to advance through their imitation and to shine through purification. Through.

### Secret

May this sacrifice, Lord, which is solemnly to be offered for the commemoration of your just ones, always cleanse and protect our consciences. Through.

### Postcommunion

We receive votive gifts, Lord, because, through the prayers of the saints, we ask that you grant us protection alike in the present life and in the eternal one. Through [Col. 1183D] our Lord.

## LXXV. Also, another Mass

Make us, Lord, we ask, always follow the feasts of your saints, whose intercessions enable us to experience the gifts of your protection. Through.

### Secret

May the sacrifice to be consecrated become pleasing, Lord, through the celebration of the precious martyrdom; may it purify our sins and reconcile to you the vows of your holy servants. Through.

### Postcommunion

We ask, almighty God, that the solemnity celebrated [Col. 1184A] through the heavenly mysteries of your saints may obtain for us the pardon of your reconciliation. Through the Lord.

## LXXVI. Also, another Mass

May the blessed supplication of the martyrs reconcile us to your Majesty, Lord, so that we who offend continually through our deeds may be expiated through the prayers of the just. Through.

May the feasts of your martyrs always gladden us, Lord, and may we, whose merit we celebrate, be expiated through their help. Through.

### Secret

May the prayer of your consecrated people be acceptable to you, Lord, for the honor of your saints, whose merits it recognizes as having always begun to provide help in tribulation. Through. [Col. 1184B] 

### Postcommunion

May the vows of your saints continually gladden us, Lord, and may the feasts themselves always offer us the patronage of the holy martyrs. Through.

## LXXVII. Also, another Mass

Magnifying your clemency, Lord, we humbly beseech you that you who make us participate in the frequent feasts of your saints may grant us to rejoice in their perpetual fellowship. Through the Lord.

Grant us, almighty God, always to praise you in the commemoration of your saints, because you will refresh those whom you grant to persevere in your honor. Through.

### Secret  
[Col. 1184C]

May the offering of our devotion be acceptable to you in your sight, Lord, and may it become salutary for us through the supplication of those for whose solemnity it is brought. Through.

### Postcommunion

Extend the right hand of your Majesty, Lord, for the defense of the faithful; and, so that they may be fortified by perpetual protection of your mercy, may the continual intercession of the holy martyrs not be lacking for them. Through.

## LXXVIII. Also, another Mass

May the fraternal crown of your martyrs gladden us, Lord; may it provide incentives of virtue to our faith and console us through manifold intercession. Through.

[Col. 1184D] Grant, we ask, Lord, that just as the undivided devotion of these blessed martyrs offers us an example of indivisible charity, so it may always implore the spirit of your grace, by which we are continually fortified. Through.

### Secret

With devout mind, Lord, we celebrate the repeated mysteries for the holy martyrs, through which both protection and joy increase for us. Through.

### Postcommunion

Having been nourished by the heavenly gift, we ask, Lord our God, that this blessed doubling of the gifts of your martyrs may sanctify us. Through.

## LXXVIIII. Also, another Mass

[Col. 1185A] Lord our God, multiply your grace upon us; and grant that we who celebrate their glorious struggles may follow their victory in holy confession. Through.

### Secret

Receive, Lord, we ask, the gifts of your people for the feast of the holy martyrs, and make us participate in their feasts with sincere hearts. Through.

### Postcommunion

May the blessing of your sacrament, Lord, which we have received, sanctify our bodies and minds and prepare us to be enrolled among those of perpetual mercy. Through the Lord.

## LXXX. Prayer for the Advent of the Lord

[Col. 1185B] Awaken your power, Lord, and come; and mercifully bring about what you promised to your Church until the end of the age. Through.

Awaken your power, Lord, and come to our aid with great strength, so that the help of your glory, which our sins impede, may be hastened by the indulgence of your propitiation. Through.

### Secret

Be reconciled, Lord, we ask, by the prayers and sacrifices of our humility; and where no support of merits is available, come to our aid through the protections of your indulgence. Through.

God, whose proper and singular attribute is [Col. 1185C] that you are good and who are never changed by any alteration, be favorable to our supplications and show your mercy to your Church, which confesses it; revealing to your people the wondrous sacrament of your only-begotten Son, so that among all nations what you promised through the Gospel of your Word may be brought to perfection, and the fullness of adoption may possess what the testimony of truth has borne. Through Christ the Lord.

### Postcommunion

Filled with spiritual nourishment, we humbly beseech you, almighty God, that through participation in this mystery you may teach us to despise earthly things and love heavenly ones, and, freed from every bond of deadly desire, make us participants in the kingdom of perpetual freedom.  
[Note: [Col. 1185D] Menard, in the third week before the Nativity of the Lord, reads *spiritalis*, “spiritual.”] Through the Lord.

## LXXXI. Also, another Mass

[Col. 1185D] Awaken our hearts, Lord, we ask, to prepare the ways of your only-begotten Son, so that through his coming we may deserve to serve you with purified minds. Through.

May your grace, almighty God, always precede and follow us, we ask, so that at the coming of your only-begotten Son, which we await with the deepest desire of our hearts, we may obtain both the supports of the present life and those of the future.  
[Note: [Col. 1185D] Pamelius has: “through the coming.”] Through.

Purify our consciences, almighty God, we ask, by visiting [Col. 1186A] them daily, so that, when the Lord your Son comes, he may find a dwelling prepared for himself in us. Through.

Make us, we ask, Lord our God, watchful and attentive in awaiting the coming of Christ your Son, our Lord, so that, when he comes knocking, he may find us not sleeping in sins but watchful and rejoicing in his praises. Through.

### Secret

Mercifully look upon the sacrifice to be celebrated for you, Lord, which may both cleanse us from the vices of our condition and render us acceptable to your name. Through.

### Postcommunion
Having received the gifts, O Lord, we ask that, as our participation in the mystery increases, so too may the effect of our salvation increase. Through him.

### LXXXII. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1186B]

Gird, we ask, O Lord our God, the loins of our minds with your divine power of the mighty [uncertain: potentium; Note: [Col. 1186D] In the same author: “powerfully”], so that, when our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, comes, we may be found worthy of the banquet of eternal life and may merit to receive from him the desires of heavenly dignities. Through him.

Help, O Lord, the frailty of your people, so that, guided bodily toward the fulfillment of the great festival we desire, they may complete the journey and, with devoted mind, attain perpetual grace. Through him.

**Secret.**

May the gifts by which the mysteries of our freedom and life are celebrated be pleasing to you, O Lord. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

May our souls, we ask, almighty God, attain this desire: that they may be inflamed by your Spirit, so that, having been nourished by divine bounty like [Note: [Col. 1186D] In Menardus, in the fifth week before the Nativity of the Lord: “lamps”] lamps, we may shine like bright lights before the presence of Christ your Son when he comes. Through him.

### LXXXIII. ANOTHER MASS

Hasten, we ask, and do not delay, O Lord, and extend to us the protection of your mercy, so that those who trust in your compassion may be raised up by timely consolations. Through him.

Grant, we ask, almighty God, this grace to your people: to await the coming of your Only-Begotten with the utmost vigilance, so that, as he himself, the author of our salvation, taught, we may prepare our souls like shining lamps for his coming. Through him.

Incline the ears of your mercy to our voice, O Lord, we ask, and illumine the darkness of our hearts with the light of your visitation. Through him.

**Secret.**

Look favorably, O Lord, upon the sacrifices now offered, we ask, so that they may advance both our devotion and our salvation. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

Grant, we ask, almighty God, to your entire household this will: to meet Christ your Son, our Lord, who is coming, prepared by righteous works, and, joined to his right hand, to merit possession of the heavenly kingdom. Through him.

### LXXXIIII. ANOTHER MASS

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the coming solemnity of our redemption may bring us the supports of this present life and bestow the rewards of the blessedness of eternal life. Through the Lord.

Stir up your power, O Lord, we ask, and come, so that those who trust in your goodness may swiftly be freed from every adversity. Through him.

Let us all rejoice, O Lord our God, gathered in unity of faith, upright in heart, so that, when our Savior, your Son, comes, we may meet him undefiled in the company of his saints. Through the same Lord.

Make us, O Lord, we ask, reject our evils with all our heart, so that, when your Son, our Lord, comes, we may be able to receive his good things. Through him.

**Secret.**

May the sacrifice of our devotion be continually offered to you, O Lord, we ask; may it both carry out the ordinances of the sacred mystery and wondrously work your salvation in us. Through the Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

Hear graciously, O Lord, we ask, the prayers of your people, so that those who rejoice in the coming of your Only-Begotten according to the flesh may, when he comes a second time in his majesty, receive the reward of eternal life. Through him.

Gladden us, O Lord, your unworthy servants, whom the guilt of our own deeds saddens, by the coming of your Only-Begotten. Through the Lord.

Look upon our prayers, we ask, almighty God, and extend over us the bowels of your mercy, so that we who are afflicted by our own guilt may revive when our Savior comes. Through him.

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we who are justly weighed down under the yoke of sin may be freed by the awaited new birth of your Only-Begotten. Through him.

Stir up your power, O Lord, and come, so that by your propitiation we may be saved. Through him.

Hasten, do not delay, O Lord our God, and powerfully free us from diabolical fury. Through him.

Extend to us, O Lord, the right hand of your veneration, and come; in your mercy absolve our sins. Through him.

O God, who see that we are afflicted by our own perversity, mercifully grant that we may be consoled by your visitation. Through the Lord.

As we hasten to meet your Son, our Lord, let no works or actions of earthly things impede us, almighty God; rather, let the instruction of heavenly wisdom make us sharers in him. Through the Lord.

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that the coming solemnity of your Son may bring us the remedies of this present life and grant eternal rewards. Through him.

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, since we deserve to be afflicted for our sins, we may be freed from every adversity through the coming of your Son. Through him.

O God, who gladden us by the annual expectation of our redemption, grant that we who joyfully receive your Only-Begotten Son as Redeemer may also behold him, when he comes as Judge, without fear. Through him.

### LXXXV. PRAYER AND PRAYERS FOR THE TENTH MONTH. FOURTH DAY

O God, who see that we trust in your goodness, mercifully grant that we may always rejoice in heavenly protection. Through him.

May your mercy come to our aid, O Lord, so that, when you come, we may merit to be saved from the dangers of our impending sins. Through him.

**Secret.**

Graciously receive, O Lord, the gifts of your Church, which in your mercy you have granted to be offered, and powerfully cause them to pass into the mystery of our salvation. Through him.

As we return devotion and thanks for what has passed, we more readily trust that what is to come will be provided; nor should we despair of the fruitfulness of seed, since, for our supplications, Christ our Lord also intervenes—the venerable and saving fruit of the Virgin Mother—through annual devotion. Whom may they dare [uncertain: Quem audant].

**Postcommunion.**

By the abundance of your gifts, O Lord, raise us up both with temporal supports and with a way of life pleasing to you, so that we may serve you securely. Through the Lord.

**For the people.**

Be, O Lord, the sanctifier and guardian of your people; fortified by the protections of blessed Mary, may they please you by their way of life and serve you securely. Through the Lord.

**On the sixth day**

Grant us, we ask, O Lord, a measure of this abstinence, so that what we remove from the license of the flesh may acquire for us a saving fruit. Through him.

O God, who always see our weakness abandoned, guard us by the visitation of your coming. Through him.

Be present, we ask, almighty God, and in all our actions both go before us by your inspiration and guard us by your help. Through him.

**Secret.**

Grant, O Lord, we ask, that we may offer an affection of devotion corresponding to the dedicated gift. Through him.

**Postcommunion**

Refreshed by life-giving food, we ask, O Lord, that what we carry out in the time of our mortality we may attain by the gift of your immortality. Through him.

**For the people.**

Look favorably, O Lord, we ask, upon your people, and absolve from all sins those whom you grant to advance through the divine sacraments. Through our Lord.

**Saturday with twelve readings**

Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, and grant that we may present the vows of this present fast with a devotion pleasing to you. Through him.

Convert us, O God our Savior, and instruct our minds in heavenly disciplines, so that bodily fasting may benefit us. Through him.

O God, who commanded the observances of sacred fasting for the expiation of our souls, grant assistance to our frailty and benignly inspire the fulfillment of heavenly commandments. Through the Lord.

May we be anticipated by the help of your mercies, O Lord, we ask, and may the devotion of all the faithful be pleasing to you in this solemnity of fasting. Through him.

Hear graciously, O God, we ask, the prayers of your people, so that we who are justly afflicted for our sins may be consoled by the visitation of your mercy. Through him.

**After the blessing**

O God, who tempered the flames of fire for the three boys, grant, we ask, that the flame of vices may not consume us, your servants. Through him.

**Secret.**

Sanctify the gifts of your Church, O Lord [Note: [Col. 1189D] Menardus: “sanctify, and grant”], and grant that through these venerable mysteries we may merit to be refreshed with heavenly bread. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

May the mysteries we have received benefit us, O Lord, and at once strip us of sins and raise us up by the protections of your propitiation. Through him.

**For the people.**

May the outpouring of your blessing come, O Lord, we ask, upon your supplicating people; may it repel from them diabolical snares, cleanse and protect their frailty, and sustain and cherish the needy. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**Α + Ω HERE BEGINS THE THIRD BOOK: PRAYERS AND PETITIONS WITH THE CANON FOR SUNDAYS**

[Col. 1189]

### I

[Col. 1189C]

O God, who have prepared invisible good things for those who love you, pour the affection of your love into our hearts, so that, loving you in all things and above all things, we may attain your promises, which surpass every desire. Through our Lord.

**Collection**

O God, who dwell in the saints and do not forsake devout hearts, free us from earthly desires and carnal craving, so that, with no sin reigning in us, we may serve you alone, the Lord, with free minds. Through him.

**Secret.**

Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and graciously receive these offerings of your male and female servants, so that what each has offered for the honor of your name may benefit all for salvation. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

Having satisfied those whom you have fed with heavenly gifts, O Lord [Note: [Col. 1189D] Read: “gifts.” — In Pamelius, on the Sixth Sunday after Pentecost: “by the gift”], grant, we ask, that we may be cleansed from our hidden faults and freed from the snares of our enemies. Through the Lord.

### II. ANOTHER MASS

O God of powers, to whom belongs everything that is excellent, implant in our breasts the love of your name, and grant [Note: [Col. 1189D] In the same author, in the same place: “grant in us”] that you may nourish in us the increase of religion [Col. 1190B] and the good things that exist [Note: [Col. 1190D] Pamelius: “that you may nourish the good things that exist”], and preserve with vigilant zeal what has been nourished [Note: [Col. 1190D] In the same author: “and preserve with vigilant zeal what exists”]. Through him.

Grant us, O Lord, we ask, that, truly trusting in your grace, we may both ask for what is worthy and continually receive what we ask. Through him.

**Secret.**

Be favorable, O Lord, to our supplications, and graciously receive these offerings of your people [Note: [Col. 1190D] Pamelius, on the Seventh Sunday after Pentecost, reads: “and grant that”], so that no one’s vow may be fruitless and no one’s petition empty; grant that what we faithfully ask we may effectively obtain. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

We have been filled, O Lord, with your gifts; grant, we ask, that by their effect we may both be cleansed [Note: [Col. 1190D] In the same author: “by their effect”] and protected by their help. Through him.

### III. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1190D]

O God, whose providence is not deceived in its ordering of things, we suppliantly implore you to remove everything harmful and grant us everything that will benefit us. Through him.

Guard us, O Lord, we ask, who have been established in your service, so that to those whom you wish to be sincerely your servants you may mercifully grant what you have commanded. Through him.

**Secret.**

O God, who established the distinctions among legal sacrifices by the perfection of one sacrifice, receive the sacrifice of servants devoted to you [Note: [Col. 1191D] Pamelius, on the Eighth Sunday after Pentecost, has: “the sacrifice offered by the devout”], and sanctify it with an equal blessing, as you sanctified the gifts of righteous Abel, so that what each has offered for the honor of your Majesty may benefit all for salvation. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

Grant us, O Lord, we ask, the perpetual increase of salvation through the daily gift of the sacrament [Note: [Col. 1191D] Read: “daily”]. Through the Lord [Note: [Col. 1191D] Read: “Through our Lord”].

### IIII. ANOTHER MASS

Grant us, O Lord, we ask, in your mercy always the spirit to think what is right and to do it, so that, since we cannot exist without you, we may be able to seek you according to your will [Note: [Col. 1191D] In Pamelius, on Sunday [lacuna] after Pentecost, it reads: “to live”]. Through him.

[Col. 1191B]

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, running along your way with devoted mind, we may escape the snares of stealthily approaching sins. Through him.

**Secret.**

Receive, O Lord, we ask, the gifts that we bring to you from your own generosity, so that these most holy mysteries, through the power of your grace at work, may sanctify us in the conduct of this present life and lead us to everlasting joys. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

May the heavenly mystery be for us the restoration of mind and body, so that we may feel the effect [Note: [Col. 1191D] The same: “the effect”] of that whose celebration we perform. Through him.

### V. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1191C]

Grant, we ask, almighty and merciful God, that amid the darknesses of this life we may not be overwhelmed by deceptive ignorance; nor may we deliberately strive to sin with rash will; rather, to those to whom you grant confidence in hoping for your mercy, mercifully grant the fulfillment of the mercy they desire. Through him.

May the ears of mercy, O Lord, be open to the prayers of those who entreat you [Note: [Col. 1191D] The same, on the Tenth Sunday after Pentecost: “and that you may grant to those who ask”], so that you may grant what they desire; make them, we ask, ask for what is pleasing to you. Through him.

**Secret.**

Grant us, we ask, O Lord, to celebrate these mysteries frequently, because whenever the memorial of this sacrifice is celebrated [Note: [Col. 1192D] Read: “celebrated”], the work of our redemption is carried out [Note: [Col. 1192D] Read: “performed”]. Through him.

[Col. 1191D]

**Postcommunion.**

We ask, O Lord our God, that you mercifully not deprive of your help those whom you never cease to restore through the divine sacraments. Through him.

### VI. ANOTHER MASS

O God, who manifest your omnipotence especially by sparing and showing mercy, multiply your grace over us [Col. 1192A], so that, running toward your promises, you may make us sharers in heavenly goods. Through him.

**Secret.**

May the sacrifices dedicated to you, O Lord, be returned to you; you granted them to be brought to the honor of your name in such a way that you would make them remedies for us. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

We ask, O Lord our God, that you mercifully not deprive of your help those whom you never cease to restore through the divine sacraments. Through him.

### VII. ANOTHER MASS

Almighty and eternal God, whose abundant goodness surpasses both the merits and the vows of those who entreat you, pour out your mercy upon us, so that you may forgive what conscience fears and add what prayer does not dare to hope. Through him.

Almighty and eternal God, from whom alone come holy desires, right counsels, and just works, grant your servants that peace which the world cannot give, so that our hearts may be devoted to your commandments and our times tranquil under your protection. Through him.

**Secret.**

Look favorably, O Lord, we ask, upon our service, so that what we offer may be an acceptable gift to you and a support for our frailty. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

May we experience, O Lord, we ask, through receiving your sacrament, support for mind and body, so that, saved in both, we may glory in the fullness of heavenly healing. Through him.

### VIII. ANOTHER MASS

Almighty and eternal God, through whom what was not began to exist and what was hidden became visible, cleanse the foolishness of our heart and purify the secrets of vice within us, so that we may serve you, O Lord, with a pure mind. Through him.

Almighty and merciful God, from whose gift it comes that your faithful serve you worthily and laudably, grant us, we ask [Note: [Col. 1192D] Pamelius, on the Thirteenth Sunday after Pentecost: “to your promises”], that we may run without offense toward your promises. Through him.

**Secret.**

[Uncertain: “inte”], O Lord, we ask, the offerings which we present at the sacred altars [Note: [Col. 1192D] Perhaps “behold” or “attend.” — “And attend” in Pamelius, in the same place], so that you may grant us forgiveness [Note: [Col. 1192D] The same, in the same place: “by granting”]; may they give honor to your name. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

May the holy participation in this mystery give us life, O Lord, we ask, and grant us alike expiation and protection. Through him.

### VIIII. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1193A]

Almighty and eternal God, grant us an increase of faith, hope, and charity; and, so that we may merit to attain what you promise, make us love what you command. Through him.

Almighty and eternal God, make us always bear a devoted will toward you and serve your Majesty with a sincere heart [Note: [Col. 1193D] We have corrected this from Pamelius, on the Sunday after the Ascension of the Lord; the copy incorrectly reads: “your Majesty”]. Through him.

**Secret.**

May the offering dedicated to your name, O Lord, purify us and transfer us day by day to the practice of heavenly life. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

Having received the heavenly sacraments, may we advance toward the increase of eternal redemption [Col. 1193B], we ask [Note: [Col. 1193D] In Pamelius, on the Fourteenth Sunday after Pentecost, it reads: “may we advance toward”]. Through him.

### X. ANOTHER MASS

Guard your Church, O Lord, by perpetual propitiation, and, since human mortality falls without you, let it always be both withdrawn from harmful things by your help and directed toward what brings salvation. Through him.

Grant us, merciful God, that we may implore your appeasement with ready minds and, obtaining forgiveness of sins, be freed from harmful attacks. Through him.

**Secret.**

Grant us, O Lord, we ask, that this saving sacrifice may become both the cleansing of our sins and the propitiation of your power. Through him.

**Secret.**

May the sacraments we have received purify us, O Lord, and make us absolved from every vice. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

May the holy things we have received give us life, O Lord, and prepare us, purified, for eternal mercy. Through him.

### XI. ANOTHER MASS

May continual mercy cleanse and fortify your Church, O Lord; and, since it cannot remain safe without you, may it always be governed by your gift. Through him.

[Col. 1193D]

Give, we ask, O Lord, this mind to your people: since they come to appease you out of necessity, may they also be devoted to your Majesty by their will. Through him.

**Secret.**

May your sacraments guard us, O Lord, and always protect us against diabolical attacks. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

May the operation of the heavenly gift possess our minds and bodies, O Lord, we ask, so that it may not be our own judgment in us [Col. 1194A] [Note: [Col. 1194D] We have corrected this from the same source, on the Tenth Sunday after Pentecost, since the copy mistakenly has: “are”], but that its effects may continually precede us [Note: [Col. 1194D] In Pamelius, in the same place: “may the effects of the age precede us”]. Through him.

### XII. ANOTHER MASS

Make us, O Lord, we ask, subject with ready will, and always stir up our wills to supplicate you. Through him.

Make us obey your commandments, O Lord, we ask, because then all good things will go before us, if we follow the author of the whole of life. Through him.

**Secret.**

Cleanse us, O Lord, by the effect of the present sacrifice, and mercifully perfect us, so that we may merit to share in it. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

[Col. 1194B]

Mercifully purify our minds, O Lord, we ask, and renew us through the heavenly sacraments, so that consequently we may receive alike the present and future help of our bodies. Through him.

### XIII. ANOTHER MASS

Grant, O Lord, we ask, that your people may avoid diabolical contagion and follow you alone, O Lord, with a pure heart. Through him.

Guard us, almighty God, so that, with your right hand guiding us, neither our own sins nor those of others may prevail against us. Through him.

**Secret.**

We suppliantly beseech your Majesty, O Lord, that these holy things we perform may strip us of past sins and future ones. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that, satisfied by divine bounty, we may be renewed both by the sacred mysteries and in our conduct. Through him.

### XIIII. ANOTHER MASS

May the working of your mercy direct our hearts, O Lord, we ask, because without you we cannot please you. Through him.

Be present, O Lord, we ask, to those who supplicate you, and amid the snares of worldly perversity pursue our frailty with everlasting goodness. Through him.

**Secret.**

O God, who through the venerable exchange of this sacrifice have made us sharers in the one supreme Divinity, grant, we ask, that just as we know your truth, so we may attain it through worthy conduct and minds. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

We give you thanks, O Lord, invigorated by the sacred gift, and implore your mercy to make us worthy of sharing in it. Through him.

### XV. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1195A]

Almighty and merciful God, having been propitiated, exclude from us everything opposed to us [Note: [Col. 1195D] Pamelius, on the Twentieth Sunday after Pentecost, reads: “having been propitiated”], so that, freed alike in mind and body, we may carry out what is yours with free minds. Through him.

Grant, we ask, almighty God, that we may merit your forgiveness in such a way that we correct our transgressions; and that you may forgive those who confess in such a way that we restrain those who persist in their perversities. Through him.

**Secret.**

Grant, we ask, O Lord, that these gifts which we offer before the eyes of your Majesty may be salvific for us. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

[Col. 1195B]

We ask, almighty God, that the divine gift we have received may benefit us with a saving effect. Through him.

### XVI. ANOTHER MASS

Mercifully grant your faithful pardon and peace, O Lord, so that they may be cleansed from all offenses alike and serve you with a secure mind [Note: [Col. 1195D] The same, on the Twenty-first Sunday after Pentecost: “and serve you with a secure mind”]. Through him.

Wipe away our sins, O Lord, by which adversities dominate us, and guard us everywhere by your mercy. Through him.

**Secret.**

May these mysteries, we ask, O Lord, provide us heavenly medicine and cleanse the vices of our heart. Through him.

**Postcommunion.**

May the mysteries we have received assist us, O Lord, and strengthen us with everlasting protection. Through him.

## HERE BEGINS THE CANON OF THE ACTION

**Lift up your hearts.**

**Response:** We have them with the Lord.

**Let us give thanks to the Lord our God.**

**Response:** It is worthy and just.

It is truly worthy and just, right and salutary, that we should always and everywhere give you thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, through Christ our Lord. Through whom angels praise your Majesty, dominions adore it, powers tremble, the virtues of the heavens and of the heavens above the heavens, and the blessed seraphim, celebrate it together in exultant joy. With them, we ask, command that our voices also be admitted, as we humbly confess and say:

Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of hosts. Heaven and earth are full of your glory. Hosanna in the highest. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Hosanna in the highest.

[Col. 1196A]

Therefore, most merciful Father, through Jesus Christ your Son, our Lord, we humbly ask and beseech you to accept them and + bless these + gifts, these + offerings, these + holy sacrifices + unblemished. First of all, those which we offer to you for your holy catholic Church: may you deign to grant her peace, guard her, unite her, and govern her throughout the whole world, together with your servant, our pope N., and our bishop N. Remember, O Lord, your male and female servants and all standing around. Their faith is known to you and their devotion is evident. They offer this sacrifice of praise to you for themselves and all their own, for the redemption of their souls, for the hope of their salvation and well-being; to you, the eternal, living, and true God, they return their vows [Note: [Col. 1195D] In Pamelius: “and to you they return”].

In communion with and venerating the memory, first, of the glorious ever-Virgin Mary, Mother of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and also of your blessed apostles and martyrs Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, [lacuna], James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon, and Thaddeus, Linus, Cletus, Clement, Sixtus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian [Note: [Col. 1195D] Dionysius, Rusticus], [lacuna], and Eleutherius [Note: [Col. 1196D] Hilary, Martin, Augustine, Gregory, Jerome, Benedict], [lacuna], and all your saints, grant that by their merits and prayers we may be protected in all things by the help of your protection. Through Christ our Lord.

We ask you, O Lord, to receive graciously this offering of our service and of your entire household; order our days in your peace, rescue us from eternal damnation, and command that we be numbered among your chosen flock. Through Christ our Lord.

Deign, O God, we ask, to make this offering in every respect blessed, enrolled, ratified, reasonable, and acceptable, so that it may become for us the body and blood of your most beloved Son, our Lord God Jesus Christ.

Who, on the day before he suffered, took bread into his holy and venerable hands, and, with eyes raised to heaven toward you, God his almighty Father [Note: [Col. 1196D] Pamelius: “and with his eyes raised”], giving you thanks, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples [Note: [Col. 1196D] Thus from the same source. The copy has: “gave”], saying:

Take and eat from this, all of you: for this is my body.

In like manner, after supper had been eaten, taking also this excellent chalice into his holy and venerable hands, again giving you thanks, he blessed it and gave it to his disciples, saying:

Take and drink from it, all of you: for this is the chalice of my blood, of the new and eternal covenant, the mystery of faith, which will be poured out for you and for many for the forgiveness of sins [Note: [Col. 1196D] We have corrected this from Pamelius; the copy reads: “in forgiveness”]. Whenever you do these things, you shall do them in remembrance of me.

Therefore, O Lord, mindful [Note: [Col. 1196D] In Pamelius: “being mindful”], we, your servants, and also your holy people, of the blessed passion of Christ your Son, our Lord and God, and likewise of his resurrection from the dead and his glorious ascension into heaven, offer to your excellent Majesty, from your gifts and grants, a pure sacrifice, a holy sacrifice, an unblemished sacrifice, holy bread of eternal life, and the chalice of perpetual salvation.

Upon these be pleased to look with a favorable and serene countenance and accept them, just as you deigned to accept the gifts of your righteous servant Abel, the sacrifice of our patriarch Abraham, and what your high priest Melchizedek offered to you: a holy sacrifice, an unblemished victim.

We humbly beseech you, almighty God: command that these offerings be carried by the hands of your angel to your sublime altar, before the presence of your divine Majesty [Col. 1197B], so that all of us who have received from this participation in the altar the most holy body and blood of your Son may be filled with every heavenly blessing and grace. Through Christ our Lord.

To us also, your sinful servants, who hope in the multitude of your mercies, deign to grant some share and fellowship with your holy apostles and martyrs: with John, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcellinus, Peter, Felicity, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucy, Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia, and with all your saints. Admit us into their company, we ask, not as one who estimates merit but as the giver of forgiveness [Note: [Col. 1197D] We have corrected this from Pamelius; the copy incorrectly has: “not an estimator of merit, but of forgiveness”]. Through Christ our Lord.

Through him, O Lord, you continually create all these good things, sanctify them, make them alive, bless them, and bestow them upon us. Through him, with him, and in him, to you, God the almighty Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, is all honor and glory throughout all ages of ages. Amen.

**Let us pray.**

Instructed by saving precepts and formed by divine teaching, we dare to say:

Our Father, who are in heaven. But deliver us from evil.

Deliver us, we ask, O Lord, from all evils, past, present, and future; and, through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, ever-Virgin, Mother of God, and of your holy apostles Peter and Paul, and Andrew, mercifully grant peace in our days, so that, aided by the help of your mercy, we may always be free from sins and secure from every disturbance. Through him.

May the peace of the Lord always be with you.

**Response:** And with your spirit.

After this, the people are to be reminded of the fasts of the fourth, seventh, and tenth months at their appointed times, or of the examinations, or of the opening of the ears [Note: [Col. 1198D] Read: “openings”], or of prayer for the sick, or of announcing the birthdays of the saints.

After this, the priest communicates with the sacred orders and with all the people.

**Postcommunion.**

[Col. 1198A]

Having satisfied those whom you have fed with heavenly nourishment, O Lord, guard us, we ask, through the intercessions of the apostles, from every adversity. Through the Lord.

We have joyfully received the heavenly sacraments, O Lord; through the intercession of blessed and glorious Mary, ever-Virgin, Mother of God, may they advance us toward eternal life. Through him.

May the working of your power increase in us, O Lord, we ask, so that, strengthened by the divine sacraments, we may by your gift be prepared to receive their promises. Through him.

Almighty God, make us always bear a devoted will toward you and serve your Majesty with a sincere heart [Note: [Col. 1198D] In the Roman Missal: “and serve your Majesty”]. Through him.

[Col. 1198B]

May the holy mysteries purify us, O Lord, and protect us by their gift. Through him.

Since you grant us to use such great mysteries, we ask that you deign to make us truly suited to their effects. Through him.

May your table, O God, free us from earthly pleasures and always equip us with heavenly nourishment. Through him.

May communion in your sacrament, O Lord, grant us both purification and unity. Through him.

May your holy things, almighty God, grant us forgiveness and provide the help of perpetual defense. Through him.

May your medicinal working, O Lord, mercifully free us from our perversities and always make us cling to your commandments. Through him.

May your sacraments always purify and fortify us, O God, and lead us to the fulfillment of eternal salvation. Through our Lord.

We ask, almighty God [Note: [Col. 1198D] We have corrected this, since the copy less suitably reads: “by the divine gift”], that the divine gift we have received may benefit us with a saving effect. Through him.

### XVII. BLESSINGS OVER THE PEOPLE AFTER COMMUNION

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, grant that your male and female servants may be enriched by the abundance of your mercies; grant them security, so that, strengthened by your blessings, they may abound in every act of thanksgiving and bless you with perpetual exultation. Through him.

Look graciously upon your flock, good Shepherd, and do not allow the sheep whom you have redeemed with your precious blood to be torn apart by diabolical attack. Through him.

Bless, O Lord, this family of yours in heavenly things, and fill it with your spiritual gifts; grant them love, joy, peace, patience, goodness, gentleness, hope, faith, and self-control. Filled with all your gifts and desiring chastity, may they merit to come to you. Through him.

[Col. 1199A]

May God bless you with every heavenly blessing and make you holy and pure in his sight; may the riches of his glory overflow upon you; may he instruct you with the word of truth and educate you through the Gospel of salvation, and enrich you with the love of all the saints. Through him.

Turn the hearts of your people always toward you, O Lord, we ask, and do not cease to govern those whom you cause to be aided by such great intercessions with perpetual protections. Through him.

Be favorable to your people, O God, so that, freed from their perversities, they may serve you with all their heart and always remain under your protection. Through him.

Guard your family, O Lord, we ask, and instruct it in spiritual disciplines. Through our Lord.

May your family, O God, eagerly come to celebrate the beginnings of its redemption [Col. 1199B] and steadfastly acquire its gifts. Through him.

Purify your faithful, O Lord, we ask, alike in body and mind, so that, pierced by your inspiration, they may prevail in avoiding harmful pleasures; and, so that they may not be captured by their allurements, may they always be nourished by your sweetness. Through him.

Be favorable, O Lord, to your people, and absolve them from all sins, so that what we deserve through our offenses may be driven away by your forgiveness. Through him.

Be present, O Lord, to your supplicants, who presume nothing from their own conscience, and aid them with ineffable mercy, so that what confidence in merits does not possess may be consecrated by the unconquerable abundance of your gifts. Through our Lord.

[Col. 1199C]

Grant, we ask, O Lord, to your people both a mind by which they may remain devoted to you and understanding by which they may ask for what is just; and your propitiation, so that it may avail for the things beneficial to those who devoutly desire them. Through him.

Look favorably, O Lord, upon the people subject to your name, and graciously work your consolations in them continually through heavenly grace. Through him.

Preserve your family, O Lord, with vigilant protection, and defend it with perpetual safeguards, so that, with every disorder always excluded, it may continually be directed by your providence. Through him.

Look favorably, O Lord, upon your people, and raise up those who are subject to you with all their heart by the protections of unconquerable goodness. Through him.

### XVIII. PRAYER FOR ORDINARY DAYS: FOR MASSES

[Col. 1199D]

Guard in perpetual peace, we ask, O Lord, those whom you have granted to hope in you. Through our Lord.

Be present to us, merciful God, and mercifully grant within us the gifts of your goodness. Through him.

**Secret.**

Sanctify, we ask, O Lord, the gifts dedicated to you, and through them, once appeased, look favorably upon us. Through him. [Note: [Col. 1199D] In the margin: “Postcommunion.”]

[lacuna]
.

Holy mysteries, O Lord, may both fill us with spiritual nourishment and protect us with bodily assistance. Through [Christ our Lord].

## XIX. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1200A]

Hear us, O God, compassionate and merciful, and graciously grant us the salutary gifts of self-restraint. Through [Christ our Lord].

Turn the hearts of your people toward you, O God, so that by your gift they may become such that you may continually bestow your benefits upon them. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.**

May the mystical offering we desire, O Lord, profit us: may it free us from our offenses and strengthen us with perpetual salvation. Through the Lord.

**Postcommunion.**

May your holy gifts, O Lord, we beseech you, both strip us of our sins and strengthen us with the power of heavenly life. Through [Christ our Lord].

## XX. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1200B]

We beseech you, almighty God, that your people, serving you with their whole heart, may continually deserve both your benefits and peace. Through [Christ our Lord].

Have mercy on us, O God, and graciously bestow upon us the effect of your compassion through your powerful goodness. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.**

Receive, O Lord, we beseech you, the sacrifice of human redemption, and in your favor work salvation for us in mind and body. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Postcommunion.**

May participation in your sacrament, O Lord, bring us purification and grant us unity. Through [Christ our Lord].

## XXI. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1200C]

Govern our wills graciously, O Lord, so that they may neither become entangled in our own iniquities nor be subjected to those of others. Through [Christ our Lord].

Grant your servants, O God, forgiveness of sins, consolation in life, and perpetual governance, so that, faithfully serving you, they may continually deserve to reach your mercy. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.**

May your sacraments, O God, surround and renew us, and at the same time grant us both a temporal remedy and an eternal one. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Postcommunion.**

May your holy gifts, almighty God, which we have received, both grant us forgiveness and provide the help of perpetual protection. Through the Lord.

## XXII. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1200D]

Restrain, O Lord, we beseech you, harmful attacks at all times, and graciously grant peaceful security in our days. Through [Christ our Lord].

You, O Lord, always remove every wickedness from us, and graciously turn us toward your justice. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.**

May our gifts, O Lord, we beseech you, become such in your sight that they may both be able to appease you and bring us to please you [Note: [Col. 1200D] In the margin: “Through.”].

[Col. 1201A] **Postcommunion.**

May your medicinal working, O Lord, graciously free us from our perverse ways and lead us to what is right. Through [Christ our Lord].

## XXIII. ANOTHER MASS

Defend us, we beseech you, O Lord, from all adversities, and protect us with continual safeguards. Through [Christ our Lord].

Preserve your people, O God, and make them devoted to your name, so that, subject to divine duties, they may courageously fulfill both temporal and eternal gifts. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.**

May this offering, O God, cleanse and renew us, govern and protect us. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Postcommunion.**

[Col. 1201B] Having been nourished by heavenly delights, O Lord, we beseech you, may we always seek those same things [Note: [Col. 1201D] In the Roman Missal: “through which”], by which we truly live. Through [Christ our Lord].

May the effect of sacred blessing be present with your faithful, O Lord, and by spiritual nourishment dispose the minds of all, so that they may be filled with the gifts of your work of mercy. Through [Christ our Lord].

## XXIIII. PRAYERS: For departing on a journey

Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, and arrange the journey of your servant N. in the prosperity of your salvation, so that amid all the changes of this life he may always be protected by your help. Through [Christ our Lord].

O God, who always bestow your mercy upon those who love you [Col. 1201C], and are in no region far from those who serve you, direct the journey of your servant N. according to your will, so that with you as protector and guide he may walk without offense along the paths of justice. Through [Christ our Lord].

Hear our prayers, O Lord, and extend your mercy to the departure of your servant N., you who are always everywhere, so that, defended from all adversities by your assistance, he may obtain the fulfillment of righteous desires. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Secret.**

Be gracious to our supplications, O Lord, and kindly receive these offerings that we present to you for your servant N., so that you may direct his journey with your grace going before him and graciously accompany him with your grace following after, [Col. 1201D] so that we may rejoice in his conduct and safety according to the protections of your mercy. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Within the Canon.**

We beseech you, O Lord, graciously to receive this offering of your servant N., which he offers to you out of the desire of his soul, commending his journey to you, O God; and may you deign to send him your holy angel, the angel of peace, just as you sent Raphael the angel to your servant Tobias, so that he may bring him safely and unharmed to the appointed places, and, when the proper time has come and all things have been duly completed, cause him to return [Col. 1202A] to your holy Church, where he may joyfully give thanks to you and your name. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Another within the Canon.**

We beseech you, O Lord, graciously to receive this offering of your servant N., which he offers to you for the safety of your servant N. For him we pour forth supplications before your Majesty: once the bonds of peace have been confirmed, may you cause him to return to us as quickly as possible with every joy. Through. [Note: “Which offering.”]

**Postcommunion.**

O God of infinite mercy and immeasurable majesty, whom neither distances of place nor intervals of time separate from those whom you protect, be present with your servants who trust in you everywhere, and deign to be their guide and companion throughout every journey they are to undertake. May no adversity harm them, may no difficulty impede them; may all things be healthy and all things prosperous for them, so that under the aid of your right hand they may swiftly obtain whatever they have rightly desired. Through [Christ our Lord].

**Another.**

O God, who lead people to life and preserve those who confess you by paternal protection, we beseech you to grant an angelic escort to this servant of yours who is departing from us, so that, protected by his aid, he may be shaken by no fear of evil, oppressed by no anguish of adversity [Note: [Col. 1201D] Read: “of no one”], and troubled by no ambushes of an attacking enemy; but, having completed the necessary stages of his journey with prosperous progress and having been happily restored to his own places, may he find everyone safe and pay the thanks due to your name. Through [Christ our Lord].

## XXV. ANOTHER: Prayers for travelers

[Col. 1202C]

O God, author and giver of true blessedness, direct us along the way in which the blameless walk, so that, seeking the testimonies of your law with devout hearts, we may persevere both in loving what they command and in desiring where they lead. Through [Christ our Lord].

O God, who direct the steps of your saints, remove from us the way of iniquity and have mercy on us according to your law, so that, not forgetting your judgments, we may run along the way of your commandments with an enlarged heart. Through [Christ our Lord].

## XXVI. PRAYER FOR CHARITY

O God, who make all things work for the good of those who love you, [Col. 1202D] grant our hearts an inviolable effect of charity, so that desires conceived through your inspiration may not be changed by any temptation. Through.

O God, who choose your justice [Note: [Col. 1201D] Pamelius has: “the justice of your law”] and write it with your finger in the hearts of believers, grant us an increase of faith and [Note: [Col. 1202D] Pamelius has: “of hope and charity”] hope and charity; and, so that we may deserve to attain what you promise, make us love what you have commanded. Through.

**Secret.**

O God, who renew us through sacraments and commandments according to your image [Note: [Col. 1202D] Read: “your image in your own”], perfect our steps in your paths, so that through these sacrifices you may cause us to attain the gift of charity which you have made us hope for. [Col. 1203A] Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Deliver us, O Lord, from every evil, and graciously grant that what we ask to be forgiven us, we too may forgive our neighbors. Through.

## XXVII. ANOTHER MASS

O God, giver of peace and lover of charity, grant your servants true harmony with your will, so that we may be freed from all the temptations that assail us. Through our Lord.

O God, who, although you made all creatures loving, fashioned humanity in such indulgence that you might redeem it even from ungodliness [Note: [Col. 1203D] We have emended this, since the exemplar reads: “that you redeemed”], grant your servants this disposition of charity, so that they may be moved by your example to repay good for evil. Through.

**Secret.**

Graciously grant, O Lord, through these sacrifices, we beseech you, that we who pray to be absolved from our own offenses may not be burdened by those of others. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Pour into us, O Lord, the Spirit of your charity, so that those whom you have satisfied with one heavenly bread you may make harmonious through one compassion. Through.

**For the people.**

Grant to your Church, O Lord, that it may not think proudly [Note: [Col. 1204D] In the Roman Missal: “but to you.”], but may advance in the humility pleasing to you, so that, despising arrogance and desiring all that is mature, it may practice free charity. Through.

[Col. 1203C] Strengthen, O Lord, we beseech you, the hearts of your faithful, and fortify them by the power of your grace, so that they may be devoted in supplication to you and sincere in mutual love. Through.

## XXVIII. PRAYER IN TRIBULATION

Mercifully show us your ineffable mercy, O Lord, so that you may at once strip us of our sins and rescue us from the punishments that we deserve for them. Through.

Spare, O Lord, spare those who sin; and, so that we may be able to approach your propitiation, grant us the spirit of amendment. Through.

**Secret.**

We beseech you, O Lord, to be appeased by our gifts, by which you yourself grant that you may be pleased. Through.

[Col. 1203D] **Postcommunion.**

May the perpetual protection of the sacrifice we have received, O Lord, never abandon us, and may it always drive every harmful thing away from us. Through.

## XXVIIII. ANOTHER MASS

Be present with your faithful, O Lord, and, in your mercy, grant the help of consolation most graciously to those to whom you grant the devoted inclination to pray. Through.

Grant us joy from tribulation, O Lord, we beseech you, so that we who have long been afflicted for our sins may, through the intercession of your saints, breathe again more quickly in your mercy. Through.

[Col. 1204A] **Secret.**

Receive, we beseech you, O Lord, the prayers of your people together with the offerings of sacrifices, and defend from every danger those who celebrate your mysteries. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

May the infusion of sacred participation give us life, O Lord, and defend us with perpetual protection. Through our Lord.

## XXX. ANOTHER MASS

Spare, O Lord, spare our sins; and although continual punishment is owed to us who offend without ceasing, grant, we beseech you, that what we deserve as perpetual destruction may be turned into a means of correction. Through.

[Col. 1204B] Remember, O Lord, human frailty; and you who justly scourge sinners, graciously spare those who are afflicted. Through.

**Secret.**

Be appeased, O Lord, by the gifts of your people, so that, pleased by this offering, you may grant us forgiveness and concede what we ask. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

May this medicine, O Lord, we beseech you, restrain the vices of the human heart, since it has come to cure the illnesses of our mortality. Through our Lord.

## XXXI. ANOTHER MASS

Lord God, who become angry for the purpose of coming to our aid and threaten for the purpose of sparing, stretch out your hand to those who have fallen, [Col. 1204C] and bring help with manifold compassion to those who labor; and may those who have been redeemed through you be preserved by your moderation for the hope of eternal life. Through.

Be present, O Lord, to our invocations, and do not let the mercy of your clemency be far from us: heal our wounds, forgive our sins, so that, separated from you by no iniquities, we may always be able to cling to you. Through.

**Secret.**

May the sacrifices to be offered to you, O Lord, together with the prayers of the Church, purify our hearts, obtain for us the gifts of your forgiveness, and bring it about that we experience prosperity amid adversity. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Having received the blessing of the heavenly gift, we humbly beseech you, almighty God, that this same gift may be for us both the cause of the sacrament and of salvation. [Col. 1204D] Through.

## XXXII. ANOTHER MASS

Almighty and merciful God, who do not wish the souls of sinners to perish, but rather their sins, restrain the anger we deserve and pour out the clemency we ask, so that through your mercy we may be transferred from sorrow into joy. Through.

O God, refuge of the poor, hope of the humble, and salvation of the wretched, mercifully hear the supplications of your people, so that those whom the justice of punishment has made afflicted may be consoled by an abundance of remedies. Through.

[Col. 1205A] **Secret.**

Receive, O Lord, being appeased, the sacrifices by which you have willed both to be appeased [Note: [Col. 1205D] Menard has: “to be pleased”] and to restore salvation to us through powerful compassion. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Guard by divine protection those whom you renew with a heavenly gift, O Lord, so that, rejoicing in your mysteries, we may be subjected to no adversities. Through.

## XXXIII. ANOTHER MASS

O God, who are justly angry at the offenses of your servants and mercifully forgive them, grant petitioners forgiveness of sins, so that, the condition of the freedom subjected to you having been restored, there may be both correction from iniquity and cessation from the scourge. Through.

[Col. 1205B] Spare, O Lord, spare those who plead; grant the help of reconciliation, you who provide a remedy even through the scourges themselves. May this correction of yours, O Lord, not become a greater cause of punishment for the negligent, but may it become paternal instruction for those who are corrected. Through.

**Secret.**

Be appeased, O Lord, by the offerings you have received, and graciously compel our wills, even when they rebel, toward you. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

May what we receive from the blessing of your holy altar, O Lord, we beseech you, be medicine for our minds and bodies, so that we who are fortified by participation in so great a remedy may suffer no adversities. Through.

## XXXIIII. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1205C]

O God of infinite mercy and immeasurable goodness, be gracious toward our iniquities and heal all the illnesses of our souls, so that, having received the forgiveness of your mercies, we may always rejoice in your blessing. Through.

**Secret.**

Graciously protect us, O Lord, by the divine sacraments, and powerfully grant their effect, so that we may serve them suitably. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

May the life-giving sacrament we have received fortify your faithful, O Lord, we beseech you, and, having freed them from every vice, make them proceed in holy devotion. Through.

## XXXV. ANOTHER MASS

[Col. 1205D]

O God, before whose eyes everything trembles [Note: [Col. 1205D] It seems that “the heart trembles” should be written. Menard has the same], and before whom all consciences are afraid, be gracious toward the groans of all [Note: [Col. 1205D] Menard likewise has: “the pains of all who groan”], and heal the wounds of everyone, so that, just as none of us is free from guilt, so no one may be excluded from forgiveness. Through.

Almighty and eternal God, who are perceived in fear, honored in love, and appeased by confession, pour out your mercy upon those who plead, so that we who distrust the quality of our merits [Col. 1206A] may experience not your judgment but your forgiveness. Through.

**Secret.**

May the sacrifices we are to celebrate purify us and imbue us with heavenly ordinances. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Grant, O Lord, we beseech you, that, having been cleansed from earthly affections [Note: [Col. 1206D] Read: “having been cleansed”], we may strive toward the fullness of the heavenly sacrament whose holy gifts we have tasted. Through.

## XXXVI. ANOTHER MASS

O God, consoler of the humble and strength of the faithful, be gracious to those who plead, so that human frailty, which of itself is inclined to fall, may always be fortified by you to stand; and what of itself is prone to offense may always be restored by you to forgiveness. Through.

Receive, merciful Lord, the prayers of those who plead, and according to the multitude of your pardons absolve us from all sins, so that, with you sparing us, we may be restored to every work of mercy, and those whom you make innocent through forgiveness you may make effective through your help. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**Secret.**

May this sacrifice, O Lord, we beseech you, always free your Church from hidden offenses and suitably cleanse it from manifest ones. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

**Postcommunion.**

May the sacraments we have received purify us, O Lord, and make us absolved from every vice. Through our Lord [Col. 1206C] Jesus Christ.

## XXXVII. ANOTHER MASS

If you were to observe our iniquities, O Lord, who could endure it? We therefore beseech your clemency: where no confidence in our actions is available, may your abundant grace shine forth, both when you forgive offenses in the unworthy and when you bestow benefits upon the undeserving. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

Merciful and compassionate Lord, you sustain us in equity by sparing us and sanctify us by forgiving us [Note: [Col. 1206D] Menard has: “who sustain us”]; grant forgiveness for our sins, and grant that, serving the heavenly sacraments, we may be free from every fault. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

[Col. 1206D] **Secret.**

We offer you sacrifices of appeasement, O Lord, so that in your mercy you may absolve our offenses and direct our wavering hearts. Through our Lord Jesus.

**Postcommunion.**

We humbly ask you, O God, that those whom you renew with your sacraments you may graciously form in conduct pleasing to you [Note: [Col. 1206D] Menard has: “to you, without …”]. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## PRAYER ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF A PRIEST, concerning how he ought to celebrate Mass for himself

O God, by whose decision the course of all ages runs [Col. 1207A] on, look graciously upon me, your servant, whom you have deigned to promote to the order of the priesthood; and, so that my service may please you, mercifully preserve your gifts in me. Through.

Lord our God, truthful promiser, be gracious toward your work, and grant me, your servant who serves you, perseverance in service according to your will, so that in our days the people serving you may increase both in merit and in number. Through.

**Over the offerings.**

Perfect in us, O Lord, we beseech you, graciously, so that what we profess in the sacred mysteries we may carry out in devout actions. Through.

We beseech you, O Lord, graciously to receive this offering of my service, which I, your servant and priest, offer to you because you have deigned to choose me for the order of the priesthood, so that I might serve your sacrifices and divine altars. For this I render my vows to you, the true and living God, humbly beseeching your Majesty that you yourself may guard in me the works of your hands and make me a suitable minister of your will in all things [Note: [Col. 1207D] Read: “through all things.” Pamelius likewise]. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

As we receive the abundance of your gifts, O Lord [Note: [Col. 1208D] Likewise: “generosity”], we humbly beseech you to grant those to whom you have given the service of this ministry the ability to carry out your grace. Through the Lord.

## XXXVIII. PRAYERS IN A TIME OF MORTALITY

[Col. 1207C] O God, who desire not the death but the repentance of sinners, mercifully turn your people toward you, we beseech you, so that, while they remain devoted to you, you may remove the scourges of your anger. Through.

Receive, we beseech you, almighty God, with paternal compassion, your people fleeing from your anger to you, so that those who fear the scourges of your Majesty may deserve to rejoice in your forgiveness. Through.

**Secret.**

May the working of this present sacrifice come to our aid, O Lord, we beseech you; may it powerfully absolve us from every error and rescue us from the assault of total destruction. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

[Col. 1207D] As we receive your holy gifts, O Lord, we beseech you, graciously defend us from every iniquity. Through.

## XXXIIII. ANOTHER MASS

Graciously regard the assembly of your Church, almighty God, we beseech you; and may your mercy come before us rather than your anger, because if you should wish to observe our iniquities, no creature could remain standing. But in the marvelous compassion with which you made us, forgive those who sin, so that you may not allow the works of your hands to perish. Through.

Hear our prayers, O Lord, and do not wish to enter into judgment with your servants, because just as no justice is found in us [Col. 1208A] in which we can place confidence, so we acknowledge you as the fountain of compassion, from whom we trust that we are both washed from our sins and freed from our necessities. Through.

**Secret.**

Through these sacraments, we beseech you, O Lord, may the effect of our redemption come, which may always draw us back from human excesses and lead us to every salutary thing. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

May the working of this sacrament, O Lord, we beseech you, always purify and fortify us. Through.

## XL. ANOTHER MASS

O God, whose mercy is needed even by the powers of the heavenly virtues [Col. 1208B], and in whose sight no human being is without the stain and punishment of sin, graciously turn away the offenses of your people, we beseech you, so that those whom the guilt of their own conscience accuses may, through the patience of your goodness, advance toward forgiveness. Through our Lord.
