O God, whose excellence of compassion is so great that, when one sinner is converted, you cause the greatest joy to be in heaven, look upon the small portion of your people, so that, when every affliction has been driven away, your inheritance may increase in number and be perfected in devotion. Through.

**Secret.**

May the saving sacrifice protect us, O Lord, we beseech you; and may what is offered to the honor of your name benefit us for forgiveness. Through.

[Col. 1208C] **Postcommunion.**

May your holy gifts, O Lord, which we have received, give us life and prepare us, cleansed, for eternal mercy. Through our Lord.

## XLI. ANOTHER MASS

Hear, O Lord, we beseech you, your people supplicating your mercy for forgiveness of their evils; and because you are powerful to forgive sins, turn away by the power of your compassion the punishments that we deserve for our deeds. Through.

Turn away your anger from your people, O Lord, we beseech you in your mercy. We indeed deserve it through our deeds, but in our human frailty we cannot endure it; therefore restrain it from us by that compassion which you are accustomed to show to the undeserving. Through.

**Secret.**

Grant us, O Lord, we beseech you, that this saving sacrifice may become both the cleansing of our offenses and the appeasement of your power. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Look graciously upon the people subjected to your name, O Lord, and graciously work your consolations in them continually through heavenly grace. Through.

## XLII. PRAYER FOR THE MORTALITY OF ANIMALS

O God, who have supplied human labors with assistance even from mute animals [Col. 1209A], we humbly ask you to ensure that those without which human society is not sustained may not perish from our uses. Through the Lord.

O God, who in your mercy have provided what human frailty needs, we beseech you not to withdraw, in your compassion for the wretched, the support of beasts of burden; and may you, sparing us, command the devastation to cease, although their destruction rages because of our merits. Through.

**Secret.**

Appeased by the sacrifices offered, O Lord, mercifully extend your help in our times. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

May the faithful people receive your blessing, O Lord, by which, saved in body and mind, they may always offer you suitable service and always find the benefits of your appeasement. Through.

Mercifully turn away, O Lord, we beseech you, all errors from your faithful, and drive away the destruction of raging diseases, so that those whom you justly scourge when they stray, you may cherish once corrected through your mercy. Through.

## XLIII. PRAYER IN A TIME OF BARRENNESS

We humbly implore the abundance of your eternal compassion, O Lord, so that, anticipating us with benefits that we do not deserve, you may be known to do good to the undeserving. Through.

Grant us, we beseech you, O Lord, the effect of devout supplication, and, being appeased, turn away pestilence and famine, so that mortal hearts may recognize that such scourges arise when you are angry and cease when you show mercy. Through.

**Secret.**

O God, who nourish both substances of the human being with the food of these present gifts and renew them through the sacrament, grant, we beseech you, that their support may not be lacking either to our bodies or to our minds. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Govern with temporal assistance, we beseech you, those whom you deign to instruct with eternal mysteries. Through our Lord.

## XLIIII. PRAYER TO ASK FOR RAIN

O God, in whom we live, move, and exist, grant us suitable rain [Col. 1209D], so that, sufficiently aided by present supports, we may seek eternal things with greater confidence. Through.

Pour heavenly waters upon your land, O Lord, which we see wasting away because of our iniquities, and irrigate it with the benefits of eternal grace. Through.

Mercifully absolve our offenses, O Lord, we beseech you, and provide the support of heavenly waters, by which our earthly condition may subsist after being nourished. Through our Lord.

**Secret.**

Be appeased, O Lord, by the gifts offered, and grant us the timely help of sufficient rain. Through.

[Col. 1210A] **Postcommunion.**

Protect us, O Lord, we beseech you, as we receive your holy gifts, and graciously absolve us from every sin. Through.

## XLV. ANOTHER MASS

Almighty and eternal God, by whose gift all the elements are renewed, remember your mercies and graciously grant life-giving rains to the human race, so that the whole earth may rejoice in the nourishment of your fruitfulness. Through.

Almighty and eternal God, we ask your divine clemency: deign to water the face of the whole earth with more abundant rains, grant healthy breezes, restore their former health to the sick, and may the souls that thirst for your promises always be filled with an abundance of your charity. Through.

O God, who, for changing the quality of the air, prepare the heavens with clouds and rain for the earth through your work, open the fountain of your goodness and make the barren earth and dusty dryness fruitful with joyful rain, so that, correction having now ceased, we may rejoice that we have received forgiveness of sins. Through.

**Secret.**

Be appeased, O Lord, by gifts that are always accepted, and, through clouds spread out over a long period [Note: [Col. 1209D] Menard has: “temper”], end the drought. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Graciously breathe upon the prayers of your people, O Lord, we beseech you, so that you may grant forgiveness for human excesses and kindly bestow help upon the wretched [Note: [Col. 1209D] Menard has: “may you bestow”]. Through our Lord.

Grant us, O Lord, we beseech you, saving rain, and graciously pour heavenly streams over the dry face of the earth. Through.

## XLVI. PRAYERS TO ASK FOR CLEAR WEATHER

Hear us, O Lord, as we cry to you, and grant clear weather to us who plead, so that we who are justly afflicted for our sins may, with your mercy going before us, experience clemency. Through.

O God, who are moved by the prayers of the faithful and appeased by the confession of the humble, be gracious to those who plead and have turned toward you; and those whom you have made to understand anger by chastisement, make them experience the mercy of one who spares. Through.

O God, who establish the nature of all things serving you through the very movements of the air for the worship of your Majesty [Note: [Col. 1210D] Likewise: “the nature of things through their very movements”], grant us tranquility in your mercy, once terrors have been removed, so that we may experience the clemency of the one whose anger we have feared. Through.

**Secret.**

May your grace, we beseech you, O Lord, always go before us and follow after us, and graciously receive these offerings that we bring to be consecrated to your name for our sins [Note: [Col. 1210D] Likewise: “we have failed”], so that through the intercession of your saints they may avail all of us [Col. 1211A] for salvation [Note: [Col. 1211D] Read: “they profit”]. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

May your people, O Lord, receive an increase of sacred blessing and be lifted up by abundant aids of your benefits, since it is helped by such great supplications of intercession. Through.

## XLVII. PRAYER [Note: [Col. 1211D] Menard has: “TO DRIVE AWAY A STORM”] AFTER A STORM AND LIGHTNING

We humbly implore your magnificence, O Lord, so that, since you have rescued us from eminent dangers, you may also graciously absolve us from sins, so that you may grant us greater benefits and make us obey your commandments. Through.

May spiritual wickedness be driven from your house, we beseech you, O Lord, [Col. 1211B] and may the malignity of the aerial powers depart [Note: [Col. 1211D] Read: “of the air”]. Through.

[Note: [Col. 1211D] In the margin: “Secret.”] [lacuna]

We offer praises and gifts, O Lord, giving thanks for the benefits granted and humbly praying continually for those yet to be granted. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Almighty and eternal God, who both heal us by chastening and preserve us by forgiving, grant your suppliants that we may rejoice in the consolation of this desired tranquility [Note: [Col. 1212D] Pamelius has: “tranquilities”] and always make use of the gifts of your compassion [Note: [Col. 1212D] In the same author: “by the gift”]. Through.

## XLVIII. PRAYERS FOR THOSE WHO MAKE AN AGAPE

[Col. 1211C] Let us pray, most beloved, to almighty God for our son N., who, mindful of the divine commandments, supplies food from his righteous labors to those in need, so that this devotion of his, just as it is necessary for us, may likewise always be acceptable to God. Through.

**Let us pray.**

We beseech the holy and venerable Lord, the rewarder of good works, for our son N., who provides food for those in need from his righteous labors, that the Lord, by his heavenly mercy, may recompense his earthly almsgiving and bestow spiritual riches upon him: may he give him great things for small, heavenly things for earthly, everlasting things for temporal. Through.

## XLVIIII. ANOTHER PRAYER AT MASSES

[Col. 1211D]

O God, who after the sacrament of baptism established almsgiving as a second washing away of sins, look graciously upon your servant N., on account of whose works thanks are rendered to you; make him blessed in reward, whom you have made devoted in piety. Through.

O God, who also prepared spiritual nourishment for the human being made in your image, grant to our son, your servant N., who sows your gifts among your poor, that he may more truly reap the fruits of his works, and that the recompense of his present generosity may be granted him for ever; and may he receive [Col. 1212A] great things for small, heavenly things for earthly, everlasting things for temporal [Note: [Col. 1212D] In the margin: “Through.”]

**Secret.**

O God, who said that the hearts of your faithful can be cleansed through almsgiving, grant, we beseech you, that as sharers in this sacrament they may strive, for the fruit of their conscience, not to burden the wretched but to help them. Through.

**Within the Canon.**

We beseech you, O Lord, graciously to receive this offering of your servant N., which he offers to you because of his righteous alms, which he bestows upon your poor. For him we humbly pour forth prayers before your Majesty, that you may add years of life to him, so that through many courses of years he may joyfully do these things for you among your poor [Col. 1212B] and pay his annual vows to you. Through Christ. [Note: “Which offering.”]

**Postcommunion.**

Almighty and eternal God, look graciously upon this servant of yours, N., who works among your poor; preserve him by your strength and protect him by your power, so that through many courses of years he may joyfully do these things for you among your poor. Through our Lord.

## L. MASS IN A MONASTERY

Almighty and eternal God, who alone work great wonders, pour out upon your servants the spirit of saving grace, and, that they may please you in truth, infuse into them the perpetual dew of your blessing. Through.

[Col. 1212C] Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that your servants may always hasten to you with their whole heart, serve you with a mind subject to you, humbly implore your mercy, and continually rejoice in your benefits. Through.

Look graciously, we beseech you, O Lord, upon your servants, and both mercifully absolve them from sins and kindly rescue them from all adversities. Through our Lord.

**Secret.**

Look graciously, O Lord, upon the offerings of your servants; and may they find that the offerings which they celebrate with devout mind in honor of your name advance their healing. Through.

Through Christ our Lord. Since, while you glorify your confessors with such great mercy that you teach no holy purpose to be without reward before you, how much more do you invite to the gift of your recompense those who endure harsher contests? And therefore.

**Within the Canon.**

We beseech you, O Lord, graciously and mercifully to receive with a clement countenance this offering of your servants, which they offer to you because of the devotion of their minds; willingly protect them as they supplicate you, graciously hear them, and preserve them with eternal protection, so that, always rejoicing in your religion, they may persevere steadfastly in the catholic faith of the Holy Trinity; and you yourself, almighty God, will grant this also to us, who unanimously [Col. 1213A] and frequently ask it [Note: [Col. 1212D] Read: “unanimously.”] [Note: [Col. 1213D] Read: “Through Christ.”]. Through.

**Postcommunion.**

Accompany with perpetual protection, O Lord, those whom you refresh with a heavenly gift; and grant those whom you never cease to foster to become worthy of everlasting redemption. Through.

## LI. ANOTHER PRAYER FOR MONKS

Graciously establish good morals in your servants, we beseech you, O Lord; graciously infuse into them what is pleasing to you, so that they may be worthy and able to merit your benefits. Through.

Look, we beseech you, O Lord, upon your servants, and kindly protect with heavenly help those who trust in your mercy. [Col. 1213B] Through.

Grant your servants, we beseech you, O Lord, constancy in your faith and sincerity, so that, strengthened in divine charity, they may be torn away by no temptations from its integrity. Through.

May your grace always bless your servants, we beseech you, O Lord, and bring them blameless to eternal life. Through.

Look kindly, we beseech you, O Lord, upon your servants, and graciously bestow upon them the protection of your mercy. Through.

Grant your servants, we beseech you, O Lord, the things they hope for, and excuse them from all faults. Through.

Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, and preserve your servants with unceasing protection, so that those who [Col. 1213C] continually serve you may be enriched with continual reward. Through.

## LII. THE NUPTIAL ACTION BEGINS

Be present, O Lord, to our supplications, and kindly assist your institutions, by which you ordained the propagation of the human race, so that what is joined by you as author may be preserved by you as helper. [Note: [Col. 1213D] In the margin: “Through.”]

We beseech you, almighty God, accompany the ordinances of your providence with gracious favor; and preserve in long-lasting peace those whom you join in lawful union. Through.

**Secret.**
Be present, O Lord, at our supplications, and graciously and kindly receive this offering of those female servants of yours, which they offer to you for that female servant of yours, whom you have deigned to bring to the age of maturity [Col. 1213D] and to the day of her wedding, so that what is brought to completion by your ordering may be fulfilled by your grace. Through Christ.

You who have bound the covenants of marriage with the gentle yoke of harmony and the unbreakable bond of peace, so that the chaste fruitfulness of holy unions might serve the multiplication of adopted children: for by ineffable means your providence and your grace, O Lord, administer both, so that what generation produced for the adornment of the world [Col. 1214A], regeneration may bring to the increase of the Church.

Within the Canon.

Therefore, O Lord, we ask that you graciously receive this offering of those female servants of yours, that man and that woman, which they offer to you for that female servant of yours. On her behalf we humbly implore your majesty: just as you have granted her to reach an age suitable for marriage, so may you cause her, joined by your gift to a marital partner, to rejoice in the desired offspring, and, in your kindness, bring her and her husband to the desired succession of years and to our days.

Within the Canon. For the thirtieth day, or the annual celebration, of the wedding.

We beseech you, O Lord, graciously to receive this offering of your male and female servants [Col. 1214B], that man and that woman, which they offer to you on the thirtieth day of their union, or on its anniversary—the day on which you deigned to join them by the marital bond. Therefore they return their vows to you, the true and living God; for them we pour out humble prayers before your awesome mercy, asking that they may grow old together in goodness and peace, see their children’s children to the third and fourth generation, and bless you throughout all the days of their life. Through Christ our Lord. This offering, O God.

[Note: [Col. 1213D] Menardus: “Complete the full Canon.”]

When you have completely finished the full Canon, say the Lord’s Prayer, and then bless her with these words:

### The prayer begins.

O God, who at the beginning of the growing world blesses it with multiplied offspring, be favorable to our supplications [Col. 1214C], and pour out upon this female servant of yours the help of your blessing, so that in the marital partnership they may be joined by corresponding affection, like-mindedness, and mutual holiness. Through Christ.

[Note: [Col. 1213D] In the same author: “beginning.”]

### The blessing begins.

Father, creator of the world, begetter of those who are born, founder of the multiplication of our race, you who added a companion to Adam with your hands, so that bones growing from his bones might mark an equal form with wondrous diversity: from this the ordained unions of the marriage-bed, for the increase of the whole multitude, bound the covenants of the human race by which they might join the entire world together among themselves. For this was pleasing and necessary to you, O Lord: [Note: [Col. 1213D] Menardus judged that this blessing should be corrected as follows: “Since what was made like a human being is far weaker than what you had made for yourself, O God, the stronger sex is added to the weaker, so that you might make one from two.”]

since—because what is like a human being is far weaker than what you had made for yourself, O God—the weaker sex, added to the stronger, [is joined] so that you may make one from two [Col. 1214D]; and so that by an equal pledge the mingled offspring might remain; then posterity, described in the corrupt text as *dejesta*, might flow in due order [Note: [Col. 1214D] In Menard: *egesta*; see there the emendations to this most corrupt prayer.], and those to come might follow those before them, nor might they set for themselves any end within so brief a span, although they were perishable. Therefore let laws and institutions for the future be given. For this reason sanctify the [text uncertain: “pat.”] beginnings of this female servant of yours, so that, joined in a good and prosperous union, she may keep the commands of the eternal law. Let her remember, O Lord, that she has been joined not only for marital license [Col. 1215A], but for the observance of faith and the careful nurture of holy children; let her marry faithfully and chastely in Christ, and remain an imitator of holy women. Let her be lovable to her husband like Rachel, wise like Rebecca, long-lived and faithful like Sarah. Let that [text uncertain: “substitute”] author of transgression usurp nothing from her. Let her remain bound to the commands of faith and of women, devotedly serving the true God; let her fortify her weakness with the strength of discipline. Joined to one marriage-bed, let her avoid unlawful contacts in life. Let her be modest, dignified, venerable in chastity, instructed in heavenly teachings; let her be fruitful in offspring, approved and innocent, and reach the rest of the blessed, even the heavenly kingdoms. Through Christ.

After this say: “Peace be with you.” Then give them Communion. After they have received Communion, say the following blessing over them [Col. 1215B]:

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, with repeated prayers we humbly implore you. For them Christ is an intercessor with you; deign to foster the unions of your servants. May they deserve to receive your blessings [Note: [Col. 1215D] Read: “so that they may be fruitful with sons.”], and may they be made fruitful by the succession of children. Deign to confirm their marriage [Note: [Col. 1215D] Read: “as you confirmed that of the first human being.”]. Let all the snares of the enemies be turned away from them, so that even in marriage they may imitate the holiness of the Fathers, who by your providence, O Lord, were found worthy of marriage. Through Christ.

[Note: [Col. 1215D] Read: “as.”]

### Likewise, after Communion.

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, so that what is administered through our ministry may rather be fulfilled by your blessing. Through Christ.

## LIII. PRAYER FOR A NATURAL BIRTHDAY

[Col. 1215C]

Almighty, everlasting God, creator of the whole creation, mercifully hear our prayers, and grant your servant, that man, whom you commanded to emerge from his mother’s womb into this life, many prosperous years, so that he may pass through every age pleasing to you. Through our Lord.

O God, who rule the course of all the ages and the moments of time, graciously hear us, and grant that your servant, that man, whose birthday we celebrate through the consecration of the divine mystery, may be granted a long life, so that by the increase of his faith and through many courses of years this solemn devotion may endure. Through Christ.

[Col. 1215D] Secret prayer.

Be present, O Lord, at our supplications, and graciously and kindly receive this offering of your servant, that man, which he offers to you on the day of his natural birth, the day on which you commanded him to be born from his mother’s womb into this world. Through Christ.

Within the Canon.

Therefore, O Lord, we beseech you graciously to receive this offering of your servant, that man, which he offers to you while celebrating the day of his natural birth, the day on which you commanded him to be born from his mother’s womb into this world in order to know you, the true and living God. Therefore he returns his vows to you, the living and true God. On his behalf we pour out humble prayers before your majesty, asking that you add years and seasons to his life, so that through many courses of years he may joyfully pay these vows of his to you, reach the desired old age, and bless you throughout all the days of his life. Through Christ.

[Col. 1216A]

### After Communion.

God, life of the faithful, savior and guardian of those who fear you, you who have deigned to bring your servant, that man, to this day of his natural birth, with the year completed: increase in him the grace of life and the protections of the guardian; multiply his days by a multitude of years, so that, with your assent, having advanced through a happy age, he may deserve to reach the beginning of heavenly joys. Through Christ.

## LIV. PRAYERS AT MASS FOR THE BARRENNESS OF WOMEN

[Col. 1216B]

O God, who deigned to make Sarah’s dead womb fruitful through the seed of Abraham, so that offspring might be born to her even against hope, mercifully regard the prayers of your female servant, that woman, who supplicates you for her barrenness; grant her, according to the precedent of the Fathers, fruitfulness, and bless the son whom you give her. Through Christ.

O God, who deigned to hear your servant Isaac when he prayed to you concerning the barrenness of his marriage and to grant conception to Rebecca, kindly hear the prayers of your female servant, that woman, for the reception of offspring, so that the foundation of hope which she has placed in your mercy may be confirmed for her by the gift she seeks and receives. Through Christ.

[Col. 1216C] O God, who removed the reproach of barrenness from Rachel, who, while anxiously seeking a child, deserved to become fruitful, mercifully grant that your female servant, that woman, may receive a share in the fruitfulness of those women who pleased you, and obtain what she faithfully asks from your mercy. Through Christ.

Almighty, everlasting God, who turned Hannah’s continual groaning after her prayer to you into joy when you made her fruitful, mercifully fulfill the desire of your female servant, that woman, to become fruitful, and kindly remove from her the reproach of barrenness, for the praise of your glory [Note: [Col. 1216D] Add: “of yours.”]. Through Christ.

O God, by whose hidden counsel Elizabeth’s womb was barren so that one day it might be made fruitful by an angelic voice, mercifully grant that, just as she bore the Lord’s forerunner among the Jewish people, so your female servant, that woman, may become fruitful in a son who may purely serve you in the faith of this people. Through Christ.

O God, who in your mercy look upon the anxiety of barren women and wondrously work fruitfulness in them even in their despair, mercifully grant that your female servant, that woman, may obtain through the prayers of your servant Gregory what she cannot obtain by herself, namely, the reception of offspring. Through Christ.

Almighty, everlasting God, who did not deny maternal affection even to the ever-virgin Mary, who bore our Redeemer, mercifully grant that your female servant, that woman, may deserve to become a mother through the prayers of that same Mother of God. Through Christ.

[Col. 1217A] Secret prayer.

Receive, O Lord, our prayers together with the offerings of sacrifices, which we bring with humble heart to your mercy on behalf of your female servant, that woman. Since you have especially implanted affection for children in the wombs of mothers, remove from her the sorrow of infertility, and mercifully bless her for conceiving offspring. Through [Note: [Col. 1217D] Delete: “the Lord.”] the Lord.

Within the Canon.

We beseech you, O Lord, graciously to receive this offering of our service and of your entire household, which we offer to you for your female servant, that woman. On her behalf we pour out humble prayers before your majesty: hear her prayer, release her womb from the bond of barrenness, and grant her offspring in whom your name may be blessed [Col. 1217B]. And our days.

### After Communion.

Having received the gift of heavenly life, we beseech you, almighty God, that what we have asked for your female servant, that woman, may deservedly be heard by your mercy. Through Christ.

## LV. BLESSING OF A WIDOW WHO HAS PROFESSED CHASTITY

Comfort, O Lord, this female servant of yours, bound by the afflictions of widowhood, just as you deigned to comfort the widow of Zarephath through the prophet Elijah. Grant her the fruit of modesty, so that she may not remember former pleasures and may not know the incitements of desire; let her submit her own neck to you alone, so that for such great labors she may receive the sixtieth degree [Col. 1217C], the delightful gift of holiness. Through Christ.

## LVI. PRAYER FOR PEACE

O God, from whom come holy desires, right counsels, and just works, give your servants that peace which the world cannot give, so that hearts devoted to your commandments may be tranquil under your protection, with fear of enemies removed. Through Christ.

O God, creator of the world, under whose judgment the order of all the ages proceeds, graciously attend to our invocations, and grant peace and tranquility in the present times, so that we may rejoice with unceasing exultation in praise of your mercy. Through Christ.

O God, strength of those who hope in you, preserve among your peoples what you have deigned to accomplish. Show the power of your mighty mercy [Col. 1217D], so that we who are attacked by the proud savagery of enemies may deserve to rejoice in your peace. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

O God, who allow no terrors to harm the peoples believing in you [Note: [Col. 1217D] Menardus: “peoples.”; in Pamelius and Menardus: “to be shaken.”], deign to receive the prayers and offerings [Note: [Col. 1217D] In both: “the prayers and offerings.”] of the people dedicated to you, so that the peace granted by your mercy may make the Roman borders secure from every enemy. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

O God, author and lover of peace, to know whom is to live, and to serve whom is to reign, protect your suppliants from every attack [Col. 1218A], so that we who trust in your defense [Note: [Col. 1217D] Menardus: “so that we who trust in your protection.”] may fear the weapons of no hostility. Through Christ.

O God, who by the help [Note: [Col. 1217D] In the same author: “assistance.”] of your mighty mercy grant prosperity and drive away adversity, overcome every obstacle that opposes your servants, so that, when the terror of wars has been removed, secure freedom and tranquil religion [Note: [Col. 1218D] The same: “and religion.”] may prevail. Through Christ.

## LVII. PRAYER IN TIME OF WAR

O God, who crushes wars [Note: [Col. 1218D] In the same author: “you crush.”], and defeats those who attack those hoping in you by the defense of your power [Note: [Col. 1218D] In Menardus: “by your power”], aid those who implore your mercy, so that, when the savagery of all nations has been restrained, we may praise you with tireless thanksgiving. Through Christ.

[Col. 1218B] O God of all kingdoms and ruler of kings, you who heal us by striking and preserve us by forgiving, extend your mercy to us, so that, strengthened by your power through the tranquility of peace [Note: [Col. 1218D] The same: “made firm”], we may use the remedies of correction. Through our Lord.

O God, whose kingdom is of all ages, mercifully hear our supplications, and protect the principate of the Roman kings [Note: [Col. 1218D] Read: “the kingdom of the Romans”], subject to you, so that, trusting in your strength, they may please you and excel above all kingdoms. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

Attend to the sacrifice that we offer, O Lord, so that it may strip us of every evil of war and establish us in the security of your protection. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

Strengthened by the nourishment of the most holy body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, we humbly ask you, almighty God, that through this singular remedy you purify us from the contagion of all sins and guard us from the assault of every danger. Through Christ.

## LVIII. ANOTHER MASS

Crush, we beseech you, O Lord, the enemies of your people and cleanse our sins, by whose merit they dominate us, so that, when you are pleased to pour purity into our minds, you may also grant us peace. Through Christ.

We beseech you, O Lord, end the pride of our enemies and overthrow it by the power of your right hand. Through our Lord.

Almighty God, restrain the enemies of the Roman name by the power of your majesty [Col. 1218D], we beseech you, so that your people may rejoice in the integrity of faith and always exult in the tranquility of the times. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

By the power of this mystery, O Lord, we beseech you, may we be cleansed from our hidden faults and delivered from the snares of our enemies. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

May participation in your holy mysteries [Col. 1219A] give us life, O Lord, we beseech you [Note: [Col. 1219D] Menardus: “of the mystery”], and likewise grant us purification and protection. Through Christ.

## LIX. ANOTHER MASS

O God, who rule all kingdoms with eternal authority, incline the ears of your mercy to the prayers of our humility, and be present to the rulers of the Roman kingdom, so that by your mercy they may always be victorious in your tranquillity and by your power [Col. 1219A]. Through Christ.

Be merciful, O Lord, to the peoples who hope in you, and show the right hand of your protection over the guardianship of the Roman name, so that the kingdom devoted to your majesty may always be defended by your power. Through Christ.

O God, who under the judgment of your majesty hold the power of all kingdoms, be merciful to the rulers of the Roman empire [Col. 1219B], so that those who await defense by your protection may be stronger than all enemies. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

Graciously receive, O Lord, the offerings by which you have willed both to be appeased [Note: [Col. 1219D] In the same author: “to be appeased”] and, by powerful mercy [Note: [Col. 1219D] Read: “of power”], to restore salvation to us. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

Be present, O Lord, to the peoples who have received the sacred mysteries, so that those who trust in you as protector may be afflicted by no dangers. Through Christ.

## LX. ANOTHER MASS

O God, who by your providence govern heavenly and earthly things alike, be merciful to the Roman state and its rulers, so that, while you fight for us, every strength of the enemies may be broken [Col. 1219C]. Through Christ.

O God, strength of kingdoms that serve you, be mercifully present to the rulers [Note: [Col. 1219D] “Be present to the rulers of the Roman name.” Menardus: “of Christians.”] of the Roman name, so that the power of those whose humility is subject to you [Note: [Col. 1219D] In the same author: “subjected to you”] may everywhere be more excellent. Through Christ.

O God, whose kingdom no ages preceded and none enclose, mercifully hear our supplications, and protect the principate of the Roman kings [Note: [Col. 1220D] Read: “the kingdom of the Romans”], subject to you, so that, trusting in your power, they may be stronger than all enemies. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

Be merciful, O Lord, to the prayers and offerings [Note: [Col. 1220D] Menardus: “to the prayers and offerings”] of your servants, and for your name’s sake defend the rulers of the Roman empire, so that the safety of those serving you in positions of authority [Note: [Col. 1220D] The same: “of the rulers”] may be the peace of your peoples. [Col. 1219D] Through Christ.

### After Communion.

Protect your servants, O Lord, with the supports of peace, and, nourishing them with bodily and spiritual food, make them secure from all enemies. Through Christ.

## LXI. ANOTHER MASS

O God, salvation of those who hope in you and strength of those who serve you, graciously receive our prayers, and be present to the rulers of the Roman empire [Col. 1220A], so that, inspired by your counsels and fortified by your aid, they may prevail against every weapon raised against them. Through Christ.

O God, author of temporal and eternal life, have mercy on those who, trusting in your protection, supplicate you, so that, by the strength of your arm, all who oppose us having been defeated, we may be excluded neither from earthly things nor from heavenly ones. [Note: [Col. 1220D] In the margin: “Through Christ.”]

Almighty, everlasting God, have mercy on those who trust in your protection, and for the glory of your name restrain the savagery of barbarian nations, so that, defended by the strength of your right hand, we may serve you with free minds. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

O God, who glorify the powers subjected to you, graciously receive our offerings [Col. 1220B], and add men to the Roman rulers, so that those whom your right hand protects when they entrust themselves to it may not be overcome by any adversity. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

May the invincible defense of your power fortify your faithful people, O Lord, so that, always devoted to you in pious affection, they may be freed from hostile enemies and continually persevere in your grace. Through Christ.

### Likewise, another.

Mercifully pardon the sins of your people, almighty God, we beseech you, and turn away from us the errors of every hostility, so that the secure freedom of the Roman name may always exult in devotion to you. Through Christ.

Look upon us, O God, our protector, and defend us from the dangers of enemies, so that, when every disturbance has been removed [Col. 1220C], we may serve you with free minds. Through the Lord.

## LXII. MASS FOR KINGS

O God of all kingdoms, and especially protector of the Roman empire, grant your servants, our kings, that they may wisely cultivate the triumph of virtue, so that they who are rulers by his appointment may always be powerful by his gift. Through Christ.

O God, in whose hand are the hearts of kings, incline the ears of your mercy to the prayers of our humility, and establish for our rulers, your servants, that man, the governance of your wisdom, so that, having drawn counsel from your fountain, they may please you and excel above all kingdoms. Through Christ.

[Col. 1220D] Secret prayer.

Receive, O Lord, the prayers and offerings of your Church, which supplicate you for the salvation of your servant, that man, and work, through the protection of faithful peoples, the ancient miracles of your arm [Note: [Col. 1220D] The Roman edition of the Sacramentary of Saint Gregory: “so that”]; when the enemies of peace have been overcome, may Roman freedom serve you in security. Through Christ.

Within the Canon.

Therefore, O Lord, graciously and kindly receive this offering of your servant, that man, which we offer to you through the ministry of priestly office, for him upon whom you have deigned to confer the power of empire [Col. 1221A]. Hear our entreaty, and grant that, trusting in the protection of your majesty, he may increase in age and in kingdom. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

O God, who prepared the Roman empire by the preaching of the Gospel of the eternal kingdom, extend heavenly weapons to your servants, those men, our rulers, and let no storm of wars disturb the peace of the Churches. Through our Lord.

## LXIII. MASS AGAINST WICKEDLY ACTING JUDGES

Graciously admit the prayers of your Church, O Lord [Note: [Col. 1221D] In Pamelius: “so that, freed from…”], and, with every adversity removed, let her serve you in secure freedom. Through Christ.

[Col. 1221B] Secret prayer.

Protect us, O Lord, we beseech you, as we serve your mysteries, so that we may serve divine things with both body and mind. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

We beseech you, O Lord our God, that those whom you grant to rejoice in participation in divine things you may not allow to be subjected to human dangers. Through our Lord.

## LXIV. ANOTHER MASS

Grant, O Lord, we beseech you, that, wholly subject to you, we may reject the desires of those who fear [text uncertain: “of fearful wills”]. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

Graciously receive, O Lord, the offerings that we sacrifice, both for the expiation of our sin and for the hastening of heavenly aid. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

Give your people, O Lord, an affection of ever-pious devotion, so that, rejecting what is wrong, they may be strengthened in holy conduct and, freed from sins, not be worn down by any adversity. Through Christ.

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that your Church may serve you with ready will, because she can be heard and defended more readily when you have made her serve you worthily. Through Christ.

## LXV. PRAYER AT MASS IN A DISPUTE

[Col. 1221D]

Almighty, everlasting God, who resist the proud and give grace to the humble, grant, we beseech you, that we may not provoke your indignation by being lifted up, but, made subject, may receive the gifts of your favor. Through Christ.

Grant us, merciful God, both to lay aside perverse pursuits and always to love holy justice. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

May the holy things that we handle absolve us, O Lord, from every guilt [Col. 1222A] [Note: [Col. 1221D] The same: “and protect us from the same.”], and protect us from the assault of every wickedness. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

Those whom you have refreshed with the heavenly mystery, graciously absolve, we beseech you, from their own and others’ offenses [Note: [Col. 1221D] In the same author: “from their own and others’ offenses”], and let us enjoy the divine gift with purified minds [Note: [Col. 1221D] Pamelius reads: “so that…”]. Through Christ.

## LXVI. ANOTHER MASS

Grant, we beseech you, almighty God, that, always meditating on what is reasonable, we may carry out what pleases you both in word and in deed. Through Christ.

O God, who command us to dwell as one in your house, graciously drive away the causes of dissension among us, so that, aided by suitable supports, we may, by your bounty, be able to live in harmony. Through Christ.

Grant us, almighty God, that, having rejected the falsehoods of the wicked, we may carry out what is reasonable and fitting for our souls. Through our Lord.

### Secret prayer.

We humbly ask you, O Lord our God, that through the working of this mystery our vices may be cleansed and our righteous desires fulfilled. Through our Lord.

### After Communion.

Graciously work your sanctification in us, O Lord, through these mysteries, so that they may cleanse us from earthly vices and lead us to heavenly gifts. Through our Lord.

## LXVII. PRAYER AT MASS AGAINST SLANDERERS

[Col. 1222C]

Grant, we beseech you, O Lord, that we may not care about the slander of corrupt minds, but, having trampled down that same perversity, we ask that you neither permit us to be terrified [Note: [Col. 1221D] Pamelius: “to be frightened”] by unjust attacks [Note: [Col. 1222D] In the same author: “permit”], nor allow us to become entangled in deceitful flatteries, but rather to love what you command. Through Christ.

Overthrow by the power of your right hand those who conspire against the foundation of your fullness, O Lord, so that wickedness may not rule over justice, but falsehood may always be subject to truth. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

We beseech you, O Lord, that the offering to be sacrificed before your sight may powerfully absolve us from every vice and defend us from all enemies. Through Christ.

[Col. 1222D] After Communion.

Grant, O Lord, we beseech you, that through these holy things which we have received, while the attacks of the wicked are disregarded [Note: [Col. 1222D] Corrected from Pamelius; in the exemplar it is erroneously written: “concealed”], with these same holy things guiding us [Note: [Col. 1222D] Pamelius: “with you guiding [us]”], we may more cautiously carry out what is right. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## LXVIII. PRAYER AT MASSES FOR THE IRRELIGIOUS

O God, who rejoice in the devotion of the faithful, make your people devoted to your saints, we beseech you, so that those who depart from their service through impious perversity of mind may, converted by your grace, recover their senses from the snares of the devil by which they are held captive. Through Christ.

O God, who abandon the faithless and are justly angry with the irreligious, mercifully convert your people, we beseech you, so that those who continually offend you through the hardness of an irreligious mind may, inspired by the grace of your mercy, be converted to earning the benefits of the saints. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

Mercifully convert the heart of your people, O Lord, we beseech you, so that they may not turn away from these offerings by which we ask to magnify your majesty. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

Grant us, we beseech you, O Lord, to seek what is right and avoid what is harmful, so that the holy things we receive may benefit us not for judgment but rather for healing. Through Christ.

### For the people.

Be present, O Lord, at our supplications, and, in your ineffable mercy, help those who presume on nothing in their conscience, so that what confidence in merits does not possess your unconquerable abundance of gifts may bestow. Through Christ.

## LXIX. PRAYER OVER A SICK PERSON AT HOME

O God, who always show compassion to your creation with loving affection, incline your ear to our supplications, and graciously regard your servant [Col. 1223C] who suffers from adverse bodily health; visit him with your salvation and with the medicine of heavenly grace. Through Christ.

O God, who have bestowed upon the human race both the remedy of salvation and the gifts of eternal life [Note: [Col. 1223D] In Pamelius: “the remedy of salvation and of eternal life for the human race”], preserve in your servant the gifts of your virtues, and grant that he may feel your healing not only in body but also in soul. Through Christ.

God of the heavenly powers, who by the authority of your command drive every sickness and every infirmity from human bodies, graciously be present to this servant of yours, so that, when infirmities have been driven away and strength restored, he may bless your holy name at once in renewed health. Through Christ.

[Col. 1223D] Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, you who strengthen the frailty of our condition by the gracious infusion of your power, so that our bodies and limbs may be invigorated by the saving remedies of your mercy, graciously look upon this servant of yours, so that, when every bodily necessity of infirmity has been excluded, the grace of his former health may be perfectly restored in him. Through Christ.

## LXX. ANOTHER PRAYER AT MASS FOR THE SICK

Almighty, everlasting God, eternal salvation of believers [Col. 1224A], hear us on behalf of your servants, those men, for whom we implore the help of your mercy [Note: [Col. 1223D] Pamelius: “aid”], so that, health being restored to them, they may offer thanksgiving to you in your Church. Through Christ.

Almighty, everlasting God, who drive away the illnesses both of souls and of bodies, show the power of your aid over our sick, so that by the help of your mercy they may be restored to every service of your goodness. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

O God, under whose nod the moments of our lives pass, receive the prayers and offerings of your male and female servants [Note: [Col. 1223D] In the same author, “and” is lacking], for whom we implore your mercy while they are sick, so that we may rejoice in the health of those whose danger we fear. Through Christ.

[Col. 1224B] After Communion.

O God, singular protection in human infirmity, show the power of your aid over our sick, so that, helped by your merciful assistance, they may deserve to be restored to your holy Church. Through our Lord.

## LXXI. PRAYER FOR RESTORED HEALTH

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, you who, by pouring the grace of your blessing into sick bodies, preserve your creation through manifold mercy [Note: [Col. 1224D] The same: “through manifold mercy”], kindly attend to the invocation of your name. Raise this servant of yours, freed from illness and granted health [Note: [Col. 1224D] More correctly in Pamelius: “freed from illness and granted health”], by your right hand; strengthen him by your power; guard him by your authority; and restore him to your Church and your holy altars with every desired prosperity. Through our Lord.

## LXXII. PRAYER FOR THOSE ENTERING A HOUSE, OR A BLESSING

Be present, O Lord, at our supplications, and enrich with the abundance of your grace your servants whom we visit in the duties of charity, so that we may continually rejoice in their prosperity. Through our Lord.

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and join the duties of our humility with the visitation of your grace, so that in the hearts of those whose dwelling we approach you may make your dwelling. Through our Lord.

Be present, O Lord, at our supplications, and illuminate this house with the serene eyes of your mercy. May the rich blessing of your grace descend upon those who dwell in it, so that, while these handmade structures remain in good health, the inhabitants themselves may always be your dwelling. Through our Lord.

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, so that if there are any adversities or hostile things in this house of your servant, that man, they may be driven away by the authority of your majesty. Through our Lord.

## LXXIII. ANOTHER PRAYER AT MASSES

God, protector of those who hope in you and guardian of minds subject to you [Col. 1225A], deign to be graciously present to your servants who dwell in this house. May an abundance of blessing breathed forth by you come upon them, and, filled with the gifts of your mercy, may they always rejoice gladly in your grace and in your name. Through Christ.

God, protector of the faithful and frequent visitor of minds subject to you, deign to be graciously present to your servants who dwell in this house, so that those whom we visit with human concern you may fortify with divine power. Through Christ.

### Secret prayer.

Receive, O Lord, we beseech you, the prayers and offerings of your servants, and surround this house with the wall of your protection, so that, every adversity having been driven away, this dwelling may always be a place of safety and peace. Through Christ.

[Col. 1225B] Within the Canon.

We beseech you, O Lord, graciously to receive this offering of your servant, that man [Note: [Col. 1225D] Add: “O Lord”], which he offers to you for his vows and desires and for the safety of his house. For him, in this dwelling, I ask the help of your majesty: deign to send him your holy angel to guard everyone in this dwelling. Through Christ.

### After Communion.

Almighty, everlasting God, who alone work great wonders, extend over these servants who dwell in this house the spirit of saving grace, and, so that they may please you, O God, pour out upon them forever the dew of your blessing in your truth. Through Christ.

[Col. 1225C] Almighty, everlasting God, join yourself to our duties, and grant your presence as a protection to those dwelling in this house, so that you may appear as the defender of your household and the inhabitant of this entire dwelling. Through Christ.

## LXXIV. PRAYER OVER THOSE WHO COME INTO A HOUSE

God, visitor of the humble, who console us with fraternal condescension, extend your grace over our fellowship, so that through those in whom you dwell [Note: [Col. 1225D] In Pamelius: “and through them may we feel your presence”], we may also feel your coming to us. Through Christ.

O God, who reveal to us signs of your presence in your servants, send the spirit of charity upon us, so that at the coming of our brothers and fellow servants the grace of your bounty may increase for us. Through the Lord.

## LXXV. BLESSING OF WATER TO BE SPRINKLED IN A HOUSE

[Col. 1225D]

O God, who established the greatest mysteries for the salvation of the human race in the substance of water, attend to our invocations, and pour the power of your blessing into this element prepared by manifold purifications, so that this creature, serving your mysteries, may receive from divine grace effects for casting out demons and driving away diseases.

So that whatever this water sprinkles in the places and houses of the faithful [Note: [Col. 1225D] Pamelius: “in houses or in places”] may be free from impurity and delivered from harm [Note: [Col. 1225D] The same: “from injury”]; let no pestilential spirit remain there, no corrupting breeze; let all the hidden snares of the enemy depart. And if there is anything that envies the safety or quiet of the inhabitants, let it flee from the sprinkling of this water, so that health, made effective through the invocation of your name [Note: [Col. 1226D] In the same author: “health sought”], may be defended from every attack. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who is to come to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire.

## LXXVI. ANOTHER

I exorcise you, creature of water, in the name of God the almighty Father, and in the name of Jesus Christ, his Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Uproot and drive away from this creature of water every power of the adversary, every attack of the devil, every phantom, and all the power of the enemy [Col. 1226B]. Therefore I exorcise you, creature of water, by the true God, and by the living God, by the holy God, and by our Lord Jesus Christ, so that you may become holy water, blessed water; so that wherever you are poured or sprinkled, whether in a house or in a field, you may drive away every phantom and all the power of the enemy, and so that the Holy Spirit may dwell in this house. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the living and the dead and the world by fire.

Likewise, for sprinkling.

Hear us, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, and deign to send your holy angel [Col. 1226C] from heaven, who may guard, cherish, protect, visit, and defend all who dwell [Note: [Col. 1226D] Pamelius: “in the dwelling.”] in this dwelling of your servant N.; and grant, we ask, that sanctification may be the entrance of this our house. May he grant to all established within it the abundance of divine blessedness, governance to masters and household, to preserve obedience and irreproachable discipline, the grace of good character to children, unstained youth to adults, a holy period of serious conduct to the elderly, and to all a long old age pleasing to him; and, with the saints acting as patrons, may he grant this house enduring blessedness, so that the continual protection of angelic guardianship may remain over it. Through the Lord.

After this he blesses the salt and says:

[Col. 1226D] I exorcise you, creature of salt, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, who commanded you to be cast by Elisha into [Note: [Col. 1226D] Pamelius: “water.”] the water, so that sterility might be healed; who by the voice of his divine mouth said to his disciples: “You are the salt of the earth”; and through the Apostle he says: “Let your heart be seasoned with salt.” Therefore make this salt exorcised, so that all who take you may find you a protection for their souls, and so that you may be for this house, for the remission of sins, for health of mind, for the protection of the soul, and for the strengthening of salvation, to drive away and exclude all temptations of demons. In the name of God the almighty Father and of Jesus [Col. 1227A] Christ, his Son, who is to come to judge the world by fire. Through him.

Then you put the salt itself into [Note: [Col. 1227D] In Menardus: “water.”] the water and blow over it, [Note: [Col. 1227D] Add: “and.”] saying:

God, who established the greatest sacraments for the salvation of the human race in the substance of water. And the rest as written above.

Here you put wine into the same water and bless it, saying:

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, hear my prayer, just as you deigned to hear your servant Moses at the Red Sea, when Pharaoh was oppressing your people, so that the army of the sea itself might be destroyed. Thus also, when your priest Elisha saw that your people could not drink the water because it was bitter, he took salt, threw it into the outlets of the waters, [Col. 1227B] and blessed it, and said: “The Lord has healed these waters; there shall be from them neither death nor sickness.” And those waters were healed. Thus, Lord, deign to heal these waters, so that wherever they are sprinkled around the corners of the house, wherever the enemy may be concealed, he may immediately be seized and flee; and, Lord, may this water of sprinkling be for him like a burning furnace of unquenchable fire. May this water of sprinkling be for us, Lord, water of power, water cooling according to the manner of the devil, so that, having been freed, we may offer praises and thanks to you, Lord almighty Father, as guests. Through our Lord.

After this you put consecrated oil into the water, and thus sprinkle the houses with it using hyssop.

## PRAYER FOR THE SPRINKLING OF WATER

[Col. 1227C] Dearest brothers, let us humbly beseech almighty God, in whose house there are many dwellings, that he may deign to bless and guard this dwelling together with its inhabitants; that he may drive darkness away from it, pour in light, and grant no power to the raging adversary. Rather, may it be a house dedicated to God himself, so that the enemy may have no license to harm anyone in it, through the power and name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is to come to judge the world by fire. Through the Lord.

Bless this house, Lord; bless the masters of this house. Look down from heaven and see with the eyes of your mercy. Open the ears of your compassion, and incline yourself over this dwelling and its inhabitants. Send a guardian angel around those who beseech you, [Col. 1227D] who may continually keep watch at the sides of this house and remain forever for its protection; may his shadow be the salvation of all and his patronage the blessedness of everyone. Through our Lord.

Bless, Lord, this house and all who dwell in it, just as you deigned to bless the house of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, so that an angel of light may dwell within these walls. May those who live together here experience the abundance of heaven’s dew, and through your forgiveness rejoice in peace and security. Send them an angel of peace who may guard our coming in and our going out. Through him.

## LXXVII. ANOTHER PRAYER FOR LIGHTNING

[Col. 1228A]

Almighty eternal God, spare those who fear, and show favor to those who beseech you, so that after the harmful fires of the clouds and the force of storms, the threat [Note: [Col. 1227D] In Pamelius: “the warning.”] of your power may pass into material for praise. Through the Lord.

God, under whose command everything is governed by a word and everything is changed by prayer, spare those who fear and show favor to those who beseech you, so that after the harmless fires of the clouds [Note: [Col. 1228D] Menardus: “harmful.”] and the whirlwinds of storms, the threat of your power may pass into material for praise. Through him.

## LXXVIII. BLESSING OF EXORCISED WATER FOR LIGHTNING

I exorcise you, creature of salt and water, in the name [Col. 1228B] of our Lord Jesus Christ the Nazarene, Son of the living God, so that you may be purification and cleansing in those places where you are sprinkled, for driving away wandering spirits, expelling every unholy power of the devil, exterminating every apparition and threat of Satan’s phantasm, and so that the lightning and stars which appear to have been sent against this tree may harm neither human beings nor cattle nor crops, but may withdraw and flee through the invocation of the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and of the Holy Spirit, who is to come to judge the living and the dead and the whole world by fire. Through him.

## LXXIIII. PRAYER FOR A NEW THRESHING FLOOR

Almighty eternal God, multiply your mercy over us, and graciously [Col. 1228C] hear our prayers, so that in this threshing floor of your servant N. you may deign to send your Holy Spirit, the Paraclete; and may an abundance of the hoped-for blessing come, so that, filled [Note: [Col. 1228D] Pamelius: “with your crops,” omitting “from.”] with your crops, they may always rejoice and exult in your name and in your grace. Through the Lord.

Multiply, Lord, your mercy over us, and graciously deign to hear our prayers, just as you heard your servant King David, who, by offering victims to you on the threshing floor, [Note: [Col. 1228D] Thus we have emended it from the same source, since the exemplar incorrectly reads “pleased.”] appeased you, turned away your anger, and obtained forgiveness. Thus, we ask, may an abundance of the hoped-for blessing come, so that, filled with your crops, we may always glory in your mercy. Through the Lord.

## LXXX. ANOTHER PRAYER IN A MONASTERY

[Col. 1228D] God, who prepare a dwelling in heaven for those who renounce the world, enlarge the temporal dwelling of this holy congregation with heavenly blessings, so that they may hold brotherhood together in the bond of charity with one mind; may they soberly, simply, and quietly keep the precepts of your continence, and recognize that grace was freely given to them; may their life agree with their name, and may their profession be perceived in their conduct. Through him.

Receive our prayers, Lord, and surround this holy fold with the wall of your protection, so that, every adversity having been driven away, this may always be a dwelling of security [Col. 1229A] and peace. Through our Lord Jesus Christ.

## LXXXI. PRAYER IN THE HOUSE OF THE HANDMAIDS OF GOD

As they enter, Lord, this tabernacle of your handmaids who serve you, may you guard them through the visitation of your angel and defend them from the adversities of this age. Grant them steadfastness of mind, so that they may offer you the chastity of purity. Help them as they struggle against vices, and let them receive the crown of victory as they come to you. Through him.

## LXXXII. PRAYER FOR THOSE WHO RENOUNCE THE WORLD

Grant, we ask, Lord, that your servants who renounce worldly pomp may have the doors of your grace opened to them; for, having despised the devil, they flee beneath the title of Christ. Command that those who come to you be received with a serene countenance, lest the enemy be able to triumph over them. Grant them the tireless arm of your help; surround their minds with the breastplate of faith, so that, enclosed within a fortunate wall, they may rejoice that they have escaped the world. Through him.

## LXXXIII. PRAYER FOR ONE WHO HAS HIS BEARD CUT FOR THE FIRST TIME

[Note: [Col. 1229D] In Menardus it is more correctly read: “God, whose Spirit causes every mature creature to rejoice,” etc.; “rejoicing in the beauty of youthful age,” etc.; “so that he may be fortified in all things by the help of your protection,” etc.] God, whose providence every growing creature, when mature, rejoices in, be favorably present over this servant of yours, N., rejoicing in the beauty of youthful age and cutting the flower of his first beginnings. May he be fortified in all things by the help of your protection; advanced through a longer life, may he rejoice in the supports both of the present life [Col. 1229C] and of the eternal one. Through our Lord.

## LXXXIV. PRAYER AT MATINS

We give thanks, holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, who have deigned, after the passage of time allotted to us, to bring us to the hours of morning. We ask that you grant us to pass this day without sin, so that at evening we may return thanks. Through him.

Rising from our beds, Lord, we implore the help of your grace in our morning prayers, so that, when the darkness of vices has been dispersed, we may deserve to walk in the light of virtues. Through the Lord.

Look favorably, Lord, upon the morning vows of those who beseech you, [Col. 1229D] and illumine the hidden things of our hearts with the remedy of your mercy. [Note: [Col. 1229D] In the same source: “secret things.”] Let dark desires not hold those whom the light of heavenly grace has restored. Through our Lord.

We beseech you, Lord, who are the true light and the Author of light, that you may deign to drive the darkness of vices away from us and illumine us with the light of virtues. Through him.

Increase your faith in us, Lord, we ask, [Col. 1230A] and always kindle in us the light of the Holy Spirit. Through him.

God, who distinguish day from night, distinguish our deeds from the darkness of shadows, so that, always meditating on holy things, we may continually live in your praise. Through [Note: [Col. 1229D] Add: “the Lord.”]

Send your light, Lord, we ask, into our hearts, [Note: [Col. 1230D] In Menardus: “so that.”] and, with the perpetual light of your commandments [Note: [Col. 1230D] In the same source: “having received on the way.”] guiding us, as we walk in your way, may we suffer no error. [Note: [Col. 1230D] Menardus: “of error.”] Through the Lord.

May your truth shine, Lord, we ask, in our hearts, and may every falsehood of the enemy be destroyed. Through him.

We offer ineffable thanks to your mercy, almighty God, who, having dispelled the darkness of night, have brought us to the beginning of this day and, having cast away the blindness of ignorance, have recalled us to the worship of your name and to knowledge. [Note: [Col. 1230D] Pamelius: “enter our senses.”] Almighty Father, enter into our senses, so that, walking in the light of your commandments, we may follow you as guide and leader. Through him.

God, who drive away the darkness of ignorance by the light of your word, increase in our hearts the power of the faith you have given, so that the fire which your grace has caused to be kindled may not be extinguished by any temptations. Through him.

Graciously pour your holy light into our senses, Lord, we ask, so that we may always be devoted to you, by whose wisdom we were created and by whose providence we are governed. Through him.

## LXXXV. PRAYER AT VESPERS

Almighty eternal God, at evening, morning, and midday we humbly beseech your Majesty to drive the darkness of sins from our hearts and bring us to the true light, which is Christ. Through our Lord.

God, who illumine the night and bring forth light after darkness, grant us to pass through this night without Satan’s hindrance, and, returning to your altar in the morning hours, to give thanks to you, God. Through the Lord.

Illumine our darkness, Lord, we ask, and graciously repel the snares of the whole night. Through him.

The day is yours, Lord, and the night is yours. Grant that the Sun of righteousness may remain in our hearts, to drive away the darkness of wicked thoughts. Through the Lord.

As we complete the offices of evening praise, we humbly ask for your clemency, Lord, so that, with you protecting us, we may overcome [Note: [Col. 1230D] More correctly in Pamelius: “the deceits of the nocturnal ambusher.”] the deceit of the nocturnal ambusher. Through him.

Show favor, Lord, to our evening supplications, and make us present praises to you in the morning without any guilt. [Note: [Col. 1230D] Pamelius: “to be presented in praises.”] Through our Lord.

As darkness begins, Lord, may the dawn [Col. 1231A] of righteousness arise, so that, when the day has ended, [Note: [Col. 1231D] In the same source: “when the day has passed.”] we may humbly give thanks to you and may you also graciously regard us in the morning as we fulfill our vows. Through him.

We shall give you thanks, Lord, having been guarded through the day; we give you thanks for being guarded through the night. Present us unharmed in the morning hours, we ask, Lord, so that you may have us as your praisers at all times. [Note: [Col. 1231D] In Pamelius: “We give thanks.”]

## LXXXVI. PRAYER BEFORE FOOD

Refresh us, Lord, with your gifts, and sustain us with the abundance of your wealth. Through him.

Let us be refreshed, Lord, by your gifts and things given, and let us be satisfied by your blessing. Through him.

Protect us, Lord our God, and provide the sustenance necessary for our frailty. Through our Lord [Col. 1231B].

Bless, Lord, your gifts, which by your generosity we are about to consume. Through him.

God, who always invite us to spiritual delights, give a blessing over your gifts, so that we may deserve to receive, sanctified, those things which are to be eaten in your name. Through the Lord.

May your gifts refresh us, Lord, and may your grace comfort us. Through our Lord.

## LXXXVII. PRAYER AFTER FOOD

Having been satisfied, Lord, with the gifts of your abundance, we give you thanks for these things which, through your generosity, [Note: [Col. 1231D] In the same source: “we have received.”] we receive, beseeching your mercy, so that what was necessary for our bodies may not be burdensome to our minds. [Note: [Col. 1232D] In the same source: “so that.”] Through him.

We have been satisfied, Lord, with your gifts and things given. Fill us with your mercy, [Note: [Col. 1232D] Pamelius: “because you are.”] for you are blessed. You live and reign as God with the Father and the Holy Spirit forever and ever.

## LXXXVIII. PRAYER FOR BLESSING NEW FRUITS

Bless, Lord, these new fruits of the grape or of the bean, which you, Lord, have deigned to bring to maturity through the dew of heaven, the abundance of rains, and calm and tranquil seasons, so that we may receive them with thanksgiving, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom, Lord, all these things are always good.

Another.

[Col. 1231D] Let us beseech your mercy, almighty God, that you may drench with the rain of your blessing these first fruits of your creation, which you have deigned to nourish through the tempering of air and rain; bring the fruits of your earth to maturity, and grant your people always to give you thanks for your gifts, so that, from the fertility of the earth, you may fill the souls of the hungry with abundant good things, and let the needy and poor praise the name of your glory. Through him.

## LXXXIX. BLESSING OF FRUIT

We beseech you, almighty God, to bless [Col. 1232A] this new fruit of apples, so that we, who through the eating of the deadly fruit of the forbidden tree in our first parent were condemned to a just sentence of death, may, through the illumination of your only Son, God and Redeemer, our Lord Jesus Christ, and through the blessing of the Holy Spirit, receive all things sanctified and blessed, after the snares of the ancient enemy and instigator of the first crime have been driven away and cast down, for our health, from the annual solemnity of this day, as we eat the various shoots of the earth. You live and reign in unity.

## XC. BLESSING OF A TREE

God, who brought forth this tree’s fruit by your command and providence, we pray that you may now also deign to bless and sanctify it, so that whoever [Col. 1232B] takes from it may be able to remain unharmed. Through him.

## XCI. PRAYER AFTER A PERSON’S DEATH

With pious affection and remembrance, dearest brothers, let us make commemoration of our dear N., whom the Lord has taken from the temptations of this age, beseeching the mercy of our God, that he himself may deign to grant him a pleasing and peaceful dwelling; may he forgive all offenses of slippery rashness, so that, forgiveness and full pardon having been granted, whatever his own error brought about in this age may be completely compensated by his ineffable mercy and goodness. Through him.

Struck by the novelty of a dreadful wound and, as it were, wounded in our hearts, we implore your mercy, Redeemer of the world, with tearful voices, so that you may gently and tenderly receive the soul of our dear N., returning to you, its proper giver; and if it contracted any stains from this bodily dwelling, may you, God, mercifully erase them in your innate goodness, piously forgive them, and consign them forever to oblivion; and may you receive it, destined to render praises to you with the others and one day to return to the body, into the company of your saints. Through the Lord.

May you deign to grant us help, Lord; may you grant assistance and mercy. Receive also the spirit of your servant N. and our dear one, freed from bodily bonds, into the peace of your saints, so that he may escape the place of punishment, the fire of Gehenna, and the flame of Tartarus into the land of the living. Through him who lives and reigns with you as God in the unity of the Holy Spirit. Through him.

Receive, Lord, the soul of your servant N., returning to you and departing from the regions of Egypt toward you. Send your holy angels to meet him, and show him the way of righteousness. Open to him the gates of righteousness and drive away from him the rulers of darkness. Recognize the faithful deposit that is yours. Receive, Lord, your creature, created not from foreign gods but by you alone, the one true and living God, because there is no God besides you alone, and none according to your works. Gladden, Lord, the soul of your servant N.; glorify, Lord, your servant. Do not remember his former iniquities [Col. 1233A] and drunkenness, which the fury of evil desire aroused. For although he sinned, he nevertheless did not deny the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, but believed, possessed zeal for God, and worshiped God as the maker of all things.

Receive, Lord, the soul of your servant N. returning to you. Clothe it with a heavenly garment, and wash it in the holy fountain of eternal life, so that it may rejoice among those who rejoice, be wise among the wise, sit among crowned martyrs, advance among patriarchs and prophets, strive to follow Christ among the apostles, behold the glory of God among angels and archangels, possess joy among the shining stones of paradise, and recognize the knowledge of the mysteries; may it find the glory of God among cherubim and seraphim, [Col. 1233B] hear the Song of Songs among the twenty-four elders, wash its garment among those washing robes in the fountain of light, and, knocking among those who knock, find the gates of the heavenly Jerusalem open; may it see God face to face among those who see him, and hear the heavenly sound with heavenly hearing among those who hear. Receive, Lord, that servant of yours into an eternal dwelling, and give him rest and a kingdom, that is, the heavenly Jerusalem, so that you may deign to place him in the bosoms of our patriarchs, that is, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. May he have a portion in the first resurrection, rise among those who rise, receive a body among those receiving bodies on the day of resurrection, come with the blessed who come to the right hand of God the Father, and possess eternal life among those who possess it. [Col. 1233C] Through the Lord.

Mindful of the ancient legal document, dearest brothers—that the human condition has been subjected to the sin and corruption of the first man, under whose law each person fears for himself what he sees happen to others—let us beseech the mercy of almighty God for the spirit of our dear N., whose day of burial is celebrated today, so that he may receive him into eternal rest and present him in a blessed resurrection. Through the Lord.

God, who are present to righteous supplications and deign to regard pious vows, grant your servant N., whose day of burial we piously commemorate today, a share in blessed reward with your saints and elect. Through the Lord.

Say: “In everlasting remembrance.”

[Col. 1233D] Another prayer before he is carried to the grave.

Let us beseech the God who judges all things, the God of the heavenly, earthly, and infernal realms, the Lord, for the spirit of our dear N., so that the Lord may deign to place him in rest and raise him in the portion of the first resurrection. Through our Lord.

Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God, we humbly beseech you for the spirit of your servant N., whom you commanded to be summoned to you from the beginnings of this age, that you may deign, Lord, to give him a place of light, a place of refreshment and rest. May he be permitted to pass through the gates of hell and the ways of darkness; may he remain in the dwellings of the saints and in the holy light which you once promised to Abraham and his seed. May his soul suffer no injury, but, when that great day of resurrection and recompense has come, may you deign, Lord, to raise him together with your saints and elect; forgive him offenses and sins down to the last farthing, and may he attain with you the life of immortality and the eternal kingdom. Through our Lord.

Let us beseech the mercy of almighty God, dearest brothers, by whose judgment we are either born or brought to an end, so that eternal rest may receive the soul of our brother N., whom the Lord’s mercy has commanded to pass from the dwelling of this world; may it present him in a blessed resurrection and deign to place him in the bosoms of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Through him.

God, who are the creator and founder of all things, who, although you are the blessedness of your saints, grant us who ask that you may cause the soul of our brother N., released from the bonds of the body, to be presented in the first resurrection of your saints. Through him.

Another prayer at the grave, before he is buried.

Let us pray, dearest brothers, for the soul of our dear N., whom the Lord has deigned to free from the snare of this age, whose little body is today handed over to burial, so that the Lord’s mercy may deign to place him among his saints and elect—that is, in the bosom of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and that he may have a share in the first resurrection which he will bring about at the prayers of the saints. Through our Lord.

It is the work of your mercy, almighty Father, [Col. 1234C] eternal God, to pray for others, since we are not sufficient for ourselves. Receive, Lord, the soul of your servant N. returning to you. May Michael, the angel of your covenant, stand beside him. Free him, Lord, from the rulers of darkness and from places of punishment, so that he may no longer be confounded by any errors of first birth or ignorance. May he be recognized by your own, and through the mercy of your goodness may he be transferred to the place of refreshment and rest, into the bosom of Abraham. Through our Lord.

God, Redeemer of souls, grant eternity to the dead, and do not allow the triumph of the Passion to be emptied through the death of the world. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit forever and ever.

Another prayer after burial.

Having duly completed, according to the custom of the faithful, the duty of burying the human body, let us faithfully beseech God, to whom all things live, that he may raise this body, buried by us in weakness, in the power and order of the saints, and command that its soul be joined to the saints and faithful; may he grant each person mercy at the judgment; and may he grant each one, redeemed by death, released from debts, reconciled to the Father, and carried back on the shoulders of the good Shepherd, to enjoy everlasting joy and the company of the saints in the retinue of the eternal King. Through our Lord.

Almighty eternal God, who deigned to breathe a soul into the human body from yourself, while, at your command, dust is returned again to dust, command that your image be joined with your saints and elect in eternal dwellings. Through our Lord.

[Col. 1235A] Now that the rites have been duly celebrated, the members have been removed from the bier, and the tomb arranged according to custom, after the departure of Israel from Egypt, let us beseech the clemency of God the Father for the soul of our dear N., whom the Lord has freed from the snare of this world. [A corrupt phrase, apparently referring to the Lord’s ubiquitous and immeasurable power and spiritual riches, precedes:] may the exalted Lord assist this soul, so that it may be free from the heat of eternal fire and obtain the refuge of the everlasting kingdom before its king; may it rejoice in generative joy on the exalted throne of the chosen Fathers, amid the splendors of the saints, in the seat of majesty, in great light, in the land and kingdom of the living. Through him.

### Commendation of the Soul

We commend to you, Lord, the soul of our brother N. [Col. 1235B] We beseech you: for whose sake you descended to the earth through your mercy, do not refuse to admit it into the bosoms of your patriarchs, but have mercy on one who departs in your name from this unstable and most uncertain life to that eternal life and joy in the heavens. Grant this, Savior of the world. You live with the Father as Ruler and reign as God in the unity of the Holy Spirit forever.

Another.

God, with whom all things that die live, to whom our bodies do not perish by dying but are changed for the better, we humbly beseech you to command that the soul of your servant N. be received and led by the hands of the holy angels into the bosom of your friend, the patriarch Abraham, to be raised on the last day of the great judgment; and whatever it contracted from the mortal realm contrary to you through the devil’s deception, wash away through your mercy by forgiving it. Through him.

## XCII. ANOTHER MASS FOR A DECEASED PRIEST
